speaker: pūrvapakṣin (Vijñānavādin)
question: What in things themselves distinguishes real from unreal, conscious from unconscious?
premises: Real and unreal show no difference in their own self (nijātmani).
Inert and non-inert likewise show none.
Hence the certainty: no distinguishing mark sits in the thing itself.
inference: The opponent's opening certainty: distinctions have no seat in things themselves.
uncertainties: Scope of the collapse (all things, or only cognized ones) stays open; vv2-8 grant it arguendo.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: Do appearing, describing, or being touch a thing's essence?
premises: Showing (prakhyā), telling (upākhyā), being, and non-being its reverse contact nothing of own-form.
Own-form faces the knower alone (jñātṛgāmin); Vṛ: showing and kin are the knower's property (jñātur dharmas).
inference: Essence is knower-facing, never predicate-fixed.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: Can a thing's own self consist in being-an-object-of-appearing?
premises: Object-of-appearing status leans on another (parāpekṣitayā).
What leans so keeps no single form (naikarūpatva).
It oversteps being itself (sattvalaṅghanāt).
inference: Appearing-objecthood cannot be a thing's self: dependence, formlessness, and excess rule it out.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: Granted no difference — does the dispute collapse?
premises: Let distinction be denied outright (mā bhūd).
Still, from appearing's presence and absence a working difference succeeds (siddhyaty eva).
That much serves the end (prayojanam); Vṛ: function (arthakriyā) succeeds on that basis.
inference: Concession costs nothing: a purpose-serving difference survives the grant.
uncertainties: Whose purpose — the disputant's or the world's? Read as the opponent's own pragmatic end, per Vṛ's arthakriyā gloss.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: What is being, cut loose from appearing?
premises: Being fits (ucitā) only as bound to appearing (avabhāsānuṣaktā).
Without that tie, existent and nonexistent stay undistinguished.
inference: Being is not free-standing; it is appearing-tied or nothing determinate.

speaker: objector (pāda ab), answered by Utpaladeva (pāda cd)
question: Does function (arthakriyā) distinguish existent from nonexistent?
premises: The existent alone works its function (arthakriyāṃ kuryāt); the other does not — so how undistinguished?
And yet the thing, in its own self (nijātmani), stays without mark.
Vṛ names the move: the objection (ākṣepa), then the reply — function runs on knowers (tattatpramātradhīnatayā), never self-seated.
inference: Function marks the scene, not the self: the objection states itself and is contained within the reply.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: Does function-conditioned being escape the collapse?
premises: The existent arrives dyed with the qualifier 'appearing-as-functional' (arthakriyābhāsopādisaṃbhedam āgataḥ).
By own form it would subsist — yet nowise apart from the non-existent (nāsatas tu viśiṣyate).
Vṛ: grounded nowhere in awareness, the tint stays borrowed (upādhi).
inference: Borrowed dye is no distinction: conditioned being differs from non-being nowhere.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: Is function at least what we declare of already-proven things?
premises: Of the thing with established being, no function is declared (na varṇitā).
Proven and unproven run exactly level (samam eva).
Hence (tena) all standing rests on awareness (pratiṣṭhā saṃvidāśrayā).
inference: First positive thesis: standing (pratiṣṭhā) is awareness-grounded, since function presupposes what it should prove.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: Does bare, ungrasping awareness escape?
premises: Suppose awareness itself ungrasping-formed (aparāmarśarūpā).
Then it too, in itself, equals non-being and the inert (abhāvena jaḍena tulyā) — as before (prāgvat).
Vṛ: grasp-less shining, however world-illumining, is as dependent as crystal; the quietist Brahman-reading (śāntabrahmavāda) is glanced in refutation.
inference: The turn: grasp-less light is inert; only self-reflective awareness can ground.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: Can the ungrounded ground another?
premises: She — grasp-less awareness, the subject carried over from v9 — stands unwon in finality (alabdhapariniṣṭhitiḥ) even by her become self (bhūtātmanā, svena).
How then would she go to standing-placehood (pratiṣṭhāspadatām iyāt) for another's being?
Vṛ: ungrounded awareness cannot settle another, as sky-flower yields no scent.
inference: The unself-grounded grounds nothing: v9's inert light cannot found another being.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: How does consciousness take on grounding?
premises: Consciousness, apt (ucita) to ground another thing's showing by saying 'this' (idam iti).
And again, by itself (ātmanā), by saying 'I' (aham iti).
Vṛ: the split thing merits showing through this-grasp, then settlement through I-grasp; without rest in I, nothing becomes usable (vyavahārya).
inference: Consciousness fits itself to both poles: 'this' for the other's showing, 'I' for itself.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: What orders the inert selves?
premises: By exclusion and inclusion (vyatireketarābhyām — Vṛ: anvayavyatirekābhyām, double concomitance) certainty (niścayaḥ) is called fixed-order, foundation, attainment, completion.
Of the other inert selves (anyajaḍātmanoḥ).
Vṛ: knower settled, the inert stands otherwise; self-and-other certainty runs on presence-and-absence.
inference: Certainty's four offices — order, ground, winning, winding-up — govern inert selves through double concomitance.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: What being have inert things?
premises: In self near-unreal (asatkalpāḥ), these inert ones belong to shining alone (prakāśasyaiva).
Shining alone is — of own self, through selves own and other (svaparātmabhiḥ).
Vṛ: without rest in awareness they are near-unreal; shining alone swells, non-separate from its form, in both knower-known heaps — the autonomy-teaching (svātantryavāda) dawns here.
inference: Inert things have only borrowed being: shining alone is, owning both heaps — autonomy's first dawn.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: Is there experience without grasp?
premises: No experience (anubhavaḥ) stands apart from distinct-and-indistinct certainty (bhinnābhinnaviniścayam).
None apart from connected shining, grasp-less in its self (vimarśarahitātmanaḥ).

Vṛ: cut from joining-severing autonomy, dull shining yields no relish-experience (saṃrambhātmānubhava); grasp's greatness is housing the world inside as self-one, then outshining it as this, then resting it in full I.
inference: Experience just is grasping certainty; grasp-less shining experiences nothing.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: Where does cut-off 'this'-grasping complete?
premises: For this 'this'-grasping cut off (vicchinnavimarśasya), fulfillment (kṛtārthatā) is rest in own form (svasvarūpe viśrāntiḥ).
And that grasping — 'I am this' (so 'ham ity ayam) — is this itself.
Vṛ: the life-principle (jīvitasthānīya) — through it even inert stuff, one with the grasper-self, comes to rest as I; the non-inert are in truth one with the higher knower.
inference: Severed grasping completes in self-rest — 'I am this,' the done-ness that quickens even the inert.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: How is the self both bound and free?
premises: The same self (sa eṣa evātmā) twofold: measured (mitaḥ) and unmeasured (aparimitaḥ).
Breath-bound (prāṇādinā niruddhaḥ): atom (aṇuḥ); as supreme self: unbroken (akhaṇḍitaḥ).
Vṛ: the Lord Himself, longing to sport the world-play, shows as breath-selves and contracts into living; uncontracted, He stays full, free awareness-self.
inference: One self, two measures — contracted atom, unbroken whole: play (krīḍā), not split.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: What holds both measures?
premises: For both, this (eṣaḥ) is the end-ground (paryantabhūmiḥ) of all object-awarenesses (sarvārthasaṃvidām).
One alone (eka eva) through continuity (anusaṃdhānāt) — before-after joining makes flashing one.
So no other is possible (ato 'nyo nopapadyate).
Vṛ: resting-seat of all being-and-non-being awarenesses; difference cannot hold.
inference: Continuity alone gathers both measures into one end-ground; no second stands.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: What shows at the limit?
premises: In I-knowing (ahaṃvidi) whose self is non-separation grasp (avyatirekātma-vimarśātman), limit-dwelling (paryantavartinyām).
Nothing inert beyond shining (bhāsanād adhikaṃ jaḍam) appears (bhāti).

Vṛ: in I-light non-separate from the world — seat of all knowing — the inert has no being past shining's measure; the lone non-inert knower flashes, never fallen from self-seat, outshining and reabsorbing the world-heap.
inference: Seal of the passage: at the limit, shining exhausts the inert; one knower flashes, world outshone and reabsorbed.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: Can breath and kin be the knower?
premises: Though joined (samavāyin) with knowing and the rest, breath-and-kin are never proved (na siddhaḥ) by non-spreading (aprathana).
They would be knowables (prameyam), never knower (pramātā) — otherwise, delusion (anyato bhramāt).
Vṛ: the measured knower, joined with knowing-qualities, still fails by grasp-lack; grasp-lessness means inertia-compatriot; the breath-cage's knowability is borrowed error.
inference: Breath is demoted to knowable: the knower cannot be what never spreads.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: Does the confined order escape the self?
premises: Though thing-abiding stands locked in the living (jīve niruddhā), curbed by breath and the eightfold city (prāṇapuryaṣṭakaniyantrite).
Even there, it abides (sthitā) in the supreme self (paramātmani).

Vṛ: in transactional living, all outer-inner order is curbed in contracted living — yet by contraction-lifting, as one with the higher knower, it stands in Śiva-self alone, since breath is non-separate from awareness-shine.
inference: Confinement is rehoused: even locked order abides in the supreme self.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: Can breath restrain that self-nature?
premises: How (katham) could restraint (yantraṇā) by breath of him, of that self (tadātmana), ever be proved (sādhitā) — in recognition (pratyabhijñāyām)?
By living-ness (jīvatā), beyond non-showing (akhyāteḥ param).

Vṛ: how could breath-knowers veil unbroken full-I-flashing Śiva? Bondage is just unspreading of boundless power — called living-ness — settled at length in the Īśvarapratyabhijñā; discriminate thence.
inference: Breath-restraint is unprovable; living-ness outlies non-showing — recognition, not breath, settles it.
uncertainties: sādhitā's scope parsed with the Vṛ: restraint unprovable (kathaṃ), living-ness beyond non-showing — the nominal close read as verdict, not afterthought.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: Where lies the ordering of things?
premises: No thing-ordering (nārthavyavasthā) lies in breath-and-kin through I-blocking (ahaṃbhāvanirodhataḥ).
Shining's self-rest (prakāśasyātmaviśrāntiḥ) is sung (kīrtitaḥ) as I-ness (ahaṃbhāvaḥ) — indeed (hi).
Vṛ: blocking the grasp (parāmarśa) that is mere self-shining, no thing-order holds, since order rests in awareness; self-rest of awareness is full-I-grasp by nature — the thing-orderer is sung.
inference: Order is not in breath but in I-ness: shining's self-rest, sung as the orderer.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: What unfolds from rest?
premises: Told already (uktā): that rest (sā eva viśrāntiḥ — feminine, resumed) by blocking of all dependence (sarvāpekṣānirodhataḥ).
Freedom (svātantryam), then doership (kartṛtvaṃ) foremost (mukhyam), and lordship (īśvaratā) with it.
Vṛ: that same rest — end-ground of world-things' final standing — is freedom (needing no kit beyond itself), foremost doership, and the lordship the āgamas trumpet.
inference: Rest unfolds: freedom, then doership, then lordship — the absolute's offices from dependence-blocked rest.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: Whence Māyā and world-making?
premises: Called Māyā (māyābhidāḥ), of his power alone (tacchakter eva — tat+śakteḥ, Vṛ: Śiva's power).
With no other proven (cānyāprasiddhitaḥ — ca+anyā+prasiddhitaḥ, Vṛ: no separate cause established, difference-identity vikalpa-felled).
This world-maker lordship (jagannirmātṛteśitā) is made of non-showing (tadakhyātimayam).
Vṛ: Māyā is Śiva's non-separate power, concealment-play; from that cause alone this non-showing-made world shines; world-shines' makerhood is lordship.
inference: Māyā from power alone, lordship from non-showing: no second cause survives.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: What is proclaimed through linking?
premises: One alone (ekaiva) through linking (anusaṃdhānāt), she (sā) is proclaimed (proktā).
Of all awarenesses (sarvasaṃvidām): the mother-principle (mātṛtattvam), self-feeling's synonym (svasaṃvedanaparyāya), beginningless (anādi).
Vṛ: the sovereign higher power — linking severed blue-etc. awarenesses across before-after ends — one alone, grounding them, bounding them: the mother's beginningless principle.
inference: Proclamation: one linking mother-principle of all awarenesses, self-feeling itself, beginningless.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: What fits the inert?
premises: Whatever grounding (niṣṭhā) of thing-ordering (bhāvavyavasthā) — pervasion (vyāpitvam) and linking (anusaṃdhānam) of the I-sharing him (tasyāhaṃbhāvabhāginaḥ).
That (taj) fits (yujyate) nothing inert (jaḍasya na).
Vṛ: where all things stand settled — awareness-self of full-I-grasp pith, freedom-never-parted — pervasion-as-linking holds everywhere; the unfree inert, grasp-pith-less, cannot host it.
inference: Pervasion and linking belong to I-sharers only: the inert cannot host them.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: What is the verdict?
premises: So (tatas) within difference (bhede), shining's shining (bhāsasya bhāsamānatā) holds good (ghaṭate).
Hence (tena) said (uktam) in recognition (pratyabhijñāyām): this world (jagat) is that-nondual-made (tadadvayamayaṃ).

Vṛ: holding to non-inertness — in this difference-flashing world, blue-pleasure-etc. shining keeps unspent inward seat while outshining through knowing-power (hence shining-shining holds); holding to non-difference, the inert re-shines — else unshining. So in the glorious Īśvarapratyabhijñā the world is said awareness-nondual-natured. Peace (iti śivam).
inference: Verdict: difference keeps shining-shining; recognition says the world that-nondual-made.

speaker: author (devotional voice)
question: Mind-wind dissolved in the inward aim; seeing yet not seeing with steady gaze — this is śāmbhavī mudrā by the guru's grace alone: reality free of void and non-void.
premises: Mind-wind dissolved in the inward aim; seeing yet not seeing.
This becomes śāmbhavī mudrā by the guru's grace alone.
Reality free of void and non-void: the śāmbhava state.
inference: Dissolution, not effort, becomes the mudrā; grace alone, reality beyond extremes.
uncertainties: Whether śāmbhavī mudrā is performed or occurring is unresolved.

speaker: author (devotional voice)
question: Four outer strokes — half-open eyes, steady mind, nose-tip gaze, moon-sun dissolved — then the vision: light-form without exterior, one supreme person attained; after which speech ends.
premises: Four outer strokes: half-open eyes, steady mind, nose-tip gaze, moon-sun dissolved.
Then the vision: light-form without exterior, one supreme person.
After which speech ends: what more is to be said?
inference: Portrait, then vision, then silence: recognition completes itself.
uncertainties: Whether the triple-throb state (trispandabhāva) is breath or consciousness is unresolved.

speaker: author (devotional voice)
question: No technique enjoined: whatever sounds is already transcendent mantra, whatever the body postures is already mudrā, whatever the breath's flow is already wonderful yoga — so, in the experienced śākta abode, what would not shine?
premises: Whatever sounds is already transcendent mantra.
Whatever postures is already mudrā; whatever breath flows is already wonderful yoga.
In the experienced śākta abode, what would not shine?
inference: No technique enjoined; recognition, not practice.
uncertainties: Whether 'śākta dhāma' means the abode of Śakti or the abode of the śākta is unresolved.

speaker: author (devotional voice)
question: Each sacred form defined by a vanishing: mantra where letters unnoticed, mudrā where all bodily action dissolved, yoga where breath-flow exhausted — then the festival: for the wise attaining Your abode, everything wonderful.
premises: Mantra: where letters are not distinguished.
Mudrā: where bodily action is dissolved; yoga: where breath-flow is exhausted.
In the festivals of attaining Your abode, everything is wonderful.
inference: Each sacred form defined by what drops out; festival of the abode.
uncertainties: Whether 'sudhī' means 'the wise' or 'the good-minded' is unresolved.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (devotee's voice, first-person)
question: What is the method, if no method is enjoined?
premises: Six techniques denied: contemplation, speech-connection, discussion, visualization, steadying, japa-practice-effort.
The question replaces the hunt: what stands well-decided? Speak it, hear it.
The answer is two refusals and one command: not renouncer, not possessor — enjoy happiness, wholly, as staying.
Staying (yathāvasthita) is the method that is no method — anupāya named by performance, not by label.
inference: No method is enjoined; staying is the method that is no method. Anupāya named by performance.
uncertainties: Whether 'suniścita' (well-decided) is an adjective of truth or a separate noun is unresolved.
Whether 'japābhyāsaprayāso na ca' is one token or several is unresolved (kept as printed).

speaker: Abhinavagupta (devotee's voice, first-person)
question: Is saṃsāra real, and what follows?
premises: Saṃsāra is not, in truth (tattvatas), for body-holders (tanubhṛtām).
Of bondage, what news (vārtā)? If bondage never truly is anyone's (bandho yasya na jātu), the liberation-rite (muktikriyā) is false (vitathā) for the free.
Diagnosis: an error-maker (mithyāmohakṛt), a heap of four delusions — rope, snake, shadow, ghost.
Rule: abandon nothing (mā kiṃcit tyaja), grasp nothing (mā gṛhāṇa); live (vihara) healthy (svasthaḥ), staying (yathāvasthitaḥ).
inference: Saṃsāra is delusion; bondage is unreal; the liberation-rite is false; abandon nothing, grasp nothing, stay.
uncertainties: Whether 'muktasya muktikriyā' means 'liberation-rite for the free' or 'rite of the liberated' is unresolved.
Whether 'vihara' is imperative or indicative is unresolved.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (devotee's voice, first-person)
question: What difference in the unsurpassed?
premises: Worship, worshipper, worshipped — what difference-course in the unsurpassed?
Transition: of whom, by whom effected, who enters? In the oneness of anuttara, what talk, what differentiated path?
Māyā, not different from consciousness-nonduality, in otherness, though different — alas, stands.
All is pure own-experience-nature; vain thought, do not.
inference: Worship-difference is Māyā: it stands as other without being different from consciousness-nonduality. All is pure own-experience-nature.
uncertainties: Whether 'māyeyam' is 'this Māyā' or 'Māyā, this [illusion]' is unresolved.
Whether 'bhinnā api' (though different) modifies Māyā or the illusion is unresolved.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (devotee's voice, first-person)
question: What is bliss, and how is it found?
premises: Bliss (ānandaḥ) here (atra) is not (na) wealth-middle-intoxication (vittamadhyamadavana).
Nor (naiva) like enjoying women (aṅganāsaṅgavat); nor lamp-sun-moon-made (dīpārkendukṛta) splendour-multitude (prabhāprakaravat); nor (naiva) even the light-rise (prakāśodayaḥ) as commonly pictured.

Joy (harṣaḥ) with gathered-difference-liberation-bliss-ground (saṃbhṛtabhedamuktisukhabhūr), like burden-lowering (bhārāvatāropamaḥ), is the attainment (prāptiḥ) of the forgotten treasure (vismṛtanidheḥ) of the all-nonduality state (sarvādvaitapadasya): the light-rise (prakāśodayaḥ).
Bliss = prakāśodaya: difference gathered, burden set down, treasure remembered.
inference: Bliss is neither pleasure nor splendour but joy like burden-lowering — the attainment of the forgotten treasure.
uncertainties: Whether 'saṃbhṛtabhedamuktisukhabhūr' is one compound or several is unresolved.
Whether 'prakāśodaya' in the first half and second half refers to the same or different light-rise is unresolved.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (devotee's voice, first-person address)
question: Why not delight in variety?
premises: Passion, aversion, pleasure, displeasure, rise, dissolution, I-ness, misery and the rest — things shining-forth, universe-bodied — are not different-natured.
Whosever manifestation you suddenly see — having regarded (avekṣya) that-that (tattattad) one-self-natured (ekātmatā) consciousness-form (saṃvidrūpam) —
Why (kiṃ na) do you delight (ramase), full (nirbharaḥ) of that contemplation (tadbhāvanā)?
Regard is the whole practice: see variety as one-self-natured consciousness-form — delight is the only consistent response.
inference: Variety is one nature; regard it as consciousness-form, and delight is the only consistent response.
uncertainties: Whether 'ekātmatāsaṃvidrūpa' is one compound or several is unresolved.
Whether 'ramase' is indicative or imperative is unresolved.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (devotee's voice, first-person)
question: Whence the truth of things?
premises: Former non-being (pūrvābhāva), being (bhava), action (kriyā) — indeed (hi) suddenly (sahasā) things (bhāvāḥ) always (sadā) in this existence (asmin bhave) — of middle-formed (madhyākāra) transformation (vikāra), confusion (saṃkaravatāṃ) of them (teṣām): whence (kutaḥ) truth (satyatā)?
In non-truth (niḥsatye), unsteady (capale), manifold (prapañcanicaye), dream-delusion (svapnabhrame), clever (peśale) —
From doubt-fear-stain-reasoning-contriving transcended (śaṅkātaṅkakalaṅkayuktikalanātītaḥ): awakened (prabuddhaḥ), become (bhava).
Four obstacles — doubt, fear, stain, reasoning — with reasoning listed last among the fetters.
inference: Things lack truth; the only response is awakening: transcend doubt, fear, stain, reasoning; awaken.
uncertainties: Whether 'madhyākāra' means middle-formed or of middle-form is unresolved.
Whether 'peśala' means clever or cunning is unresolved.
Whether 'bhava' (become) is imperative or indicative is unresolved.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (devotee's voice, first-person)
question: Do things arise, and whence the universe-glory?
premises: Of things (bhāvānām) no arising (na samudbhavaḥ) is — natural (sahajaḥ), by your contemplation (tvadbhāvitā) they shine (bhānti).
Non-true (niḥsatyāḥ) too (api), truth (satyatām) they partake (bhajanti) by experience-delusion (anubhavabhrāntyā) for a moment (kṣaṇam).
This universe-glory (eṣa viśvamahimā) will-born from you (tvatsaṅkalpajaḥ); its birth (janma) from elsewhere (anyataḥ) is not (nāsti).
Hence (tasmāt) you shine (bhāsi) by splendor (vibhavena) in worlds (bhuvaneṣu) — one (ekaḥ), though (api), many-selfed (anekātmakaḥ).
inference: No arising; things shine by contemplation; non-true borrows momentary truth; universe-glory is will-born; you shine one-yet-many.
uncertainties: Whether 'sahaja' means 'natural' or 'innate' is unresolved.
Whether 'anubhavabhrānti' means experience's delusion or delusion of experience is unresolved.
Whether 'ekopy anekātmakaḥ' means 'one, though many-selfed' or 'one, yet (becoming) many-selfed' is unresolved.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (devotee's voice, first-person)
question: What shines in the mirror, and what follows from knowing it?
premises: What true, what untrue, little-much, eternal, not eternal, what Māyā-stained, what self-pure — shines (rājate) in the consciousness-mirror (ciddarpaṇe).
All opposites, one mirror; the mirror doesn't sort them.
That all (tat sarvaṃ), from own-grasping-consciousness-rise (svavimarśasaṃvidudayāt), form-light-natured (rūpaprakāśātmakam), having known (jñātvā) —
— own-experience-risen (svānubhavādhirūḍha) glory (mahimā): Lordhood (viśveśvaratvam) — worship (bhaja).
inference: All opposites shine in the consciousness-mirror; knowing that all is own-grasping-consciousness-rise = glory = Lordhood; worship.
uncertainties: Whether 'svavimarśasaṃvidudaya' is one compound or several is unresolved.
Whether 'rūpaprakāśātmaka' modifies 'tat sarvam' or 'mahimā' is unresolved.
Whether 'bhaja' is imperative or indicative is unresolved.

speaker: Kṣemarāja (invoking voice)
question: Who is saluted, and who should shelter?
premises: Oṃ. Obeisance to Consciousness-Bhairava.
Ground-shelter-takers of consciousness-ground: take consciousness-state, wander not in vain.
Proclaiming thus, Śiva grace-bent conquers — of devotees.
inference: Salute Bhairava; shelter in ground; wander not; Śiva conquers.

World-grace-cause-nature Yours by palm.
inference: Fearlessness uproots; grace-nature palmed.

Borne by me, skull — thus You show.

By skull-staff-bone-bearing pretext, You give command.

Triple-split function sound hearing, standing am I — thus.

premises: Moreover — Parā-etc.-power-triple-spoke-lovely great power — gods You imitate outside, by trident-holding pretext, always — You.

premises: Will-etc.-own-power-shown-lower-abode-threefold — own indeed supreme power, thunderbolt-made — borne, six-spoked — You.
inference: Lower-threefold shown, thunderbolt borne six-spoked.

Shown by skull-cup-blood-pretext — this as-it-were my within.

Showing, held by You, Mahākāla.

By palm-pomegranate-show-play, O god.

speaker: Kṣemarāja (devotee voice)

Thus the Lord teaches.

speaker: Kṣemarāja (devotee voice)

inference: Bound-aimed expanding shows all-states unstained self.

speaker: Kṣemarāja (devotee voice)

By supreme-subtle-splits, Bhairava, world-lord-led.

inference: In-me flashing always; rite accomplished effortlessly.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (devotee's voice, first-person vandana)
question: What is the object of veneration, and how does veneration relate to it?
premises: The object is fixed in full: all-pervading (vyāpta) particular of moving-and-unmoving states (carācarabhāvaviśeṣa), consisting of consciousness (cinmaya), one (eka), endless (ananta), beginningless (anādi).
The act follows: Bhairava-Lord (bhairavanātham), refuge of the helpless (anāthaśaraṇyaṃ), venerated by mind-become-Yours (tvanmayacittatayā), in heart (hṛdi) — vande (I venerate).
Veneration is not ritual offering but mental absorption: the devotee's mind becoming His (tvanmaya).

The name Bhairava performs its own nirukta here: bearing/supporting the universe, the Roar (rava) of AHAM, benefactor of the terrified — all three senses lived in the single act of absorption (Tantrāloka 1.95-100).
Total surrender is sized to its object: the all-pervading consciousness is venerated by absorption into it, not by offering to it.
inference: The Absolute is named in full, then venerated by absorption into it; the name is lived, not glossed. Veneration is not offering but becoming.
uncertainties: Whether 'carācarabhāvaviśeṣa' means particular states or the particularity of states is unresolved.
Whether 'anādi' negates temporal beginning only or all limitation is unresolved.
The nirukta is performed, not stated; the verse does not gloss its own name.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (devotee's voice, first-person recognition)
question: How does the world appear as His, and how is identity declared?
premises: Disclosure first: all this (etad), become of You (tvanmayam), without remainder (aśeṣam), now (idānīm) appears (bhāti) to me (mama) — by the power of Your grace (tvadanugrahaśaktyā).
Then declaration: You (tvaṃ), Maheśa, always (sadaiva) my self (mamātmā); made of my own self (svātmamayaṃ), all (samastam) is mine (mama) through Him (tena).
Grace is the cause of both disclosure and declaration; merit is not.
Appearance, then ownership — the two-step is the pratyabhijñā structure.
inference: Recognition is two-step, not one.
uncertainties: Whether 'svātmamaya' means 'made of my self' or 'self-identical' is unresolved.
Whether 'tena' refers to grace or to Maheśa is unresolved.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (devotee's voice, first-person recognition)
question: How can fear be denied while suffering is conceded?
premises: Fear-talk denied: with You as Lord (nāthe) pervading (viśvagaye) own self (svātmani), therefore (tena) no talk of transmigration-fear exists (na saṃsṛtibhītikathā asti).
Affliction conceded in the same breath: even though (satsvapi) hard-to-bear suffering, delusion, terror-causing karma-hosts.
No-fear and full-suffering together — the concession framed by the denial, resolved within the verse, not deferred.
The non-dual recognition does not deny affliction; it denies fear of it: suffering is real, fear of it is not, because there is no 'other' to fear.
inference: Fear-talk denied while suffering conceded: denial and concession in one breath, resolved within the verse.
uncertainties: Whether 'prāyeṇa' (mostly) softens the claim or qualifies it is unresolved.
Whether 'karmagaṇa' means masses of karma or hosts of karmic beings is unresolved.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (devotee's voice, first-person prayer and declaration)
question: How does the devotee turn aside death's gaze?
premises: Prayer first: O Ender (antaka), do not (mā) direct (vinidhehi) toward me (māṃ prati) this (enām) most wrathful-terrible (krodhakarālatamām) gaze (dṛśam).
Then the ground: firm (dhīra) in Śaṅkara-service (sevana) and contemplation (cintana), filled (maya) with terrifying, awe-full Bhairava-power (bhīṣaṇabhairavaśakti) — asmi (I am).
Power first invoked against death's gaze, then declared as state.
Śaṅkara here = Śiva, not Śaṅkarācārya — the context of Bhairava-service requires it.
inference: Prayer first, then the ground: power declared as state, not begged. The devotee testifies to possessing power, grounded in service and contemplation.
uncertainties: Whether 'asmi' is a declaration of achieved state or a performative utterance is unresolved.
Whether 'śaṅkara' could refer to Śaṅkarācārya is resolved as Śiva by context.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (devotee's voice, first-person fearlessness)
question: How does fearlessness follow from awareness?
premises: Great darkness already dispelled (dārita bhūri tamisra) by rays (dīdhiti) of awareness (saṃvid) consisting of world-becoming (bhavanmaya).
Then the catalogue — death, Yama, ender, karma-ghosts — met with salutation (namo 'stu) alone.
Never (na jātu) fear (bibhemi): awareness burned the dark before the terrors were named.
Salutation finishes what light began: the terrors are met with salutation, not weapons.
inference: Awareness first, salutation finishes: absolute fearlessness. The dark that made terrors terrifying is already gone.
uncertainties: Whether 'bhavanmaya' (world-becoming) modifies awareness or rays is unresolved.
Whether the four terrors are a complete list or exemplary is unresolved.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (devotee's voice, first-person entry)
question: What does true awakening disclose, and what is bliss?
premises: Arisen (prodita) true (satya) awakening (vibodha): its rays (marīci) reveal (prekṣita) the true essence (satattva) of world-objects (viśvapadārtha).
On that ground — in You (tvayi), being-full (bhāvaparāmṛtanirbharapūrṇa), I the self (aham ātmani) enter (emi) bliss (nirvṛtim).
Awakening discloses; entry is bliss; pūrṇa (full/complete) is the Lord's nature.
Bliss is ingress into fullness, not a feeling produced.
inference: Awakening discloses things as they are; bliss is entry into the Lord's fullness — ingress, not feeling.
uncertainties: Whether 'prodita' (arisen) modifies awakening or rays is unresolved.
Whether 'bhāvaparāmṛtanirbharapūrṇa' is one compound or several is unresolved.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (devotee's voice, first-person recognition)
question: What is the relation between affliction and nondifference?
premises: When indeed (yadaiva) the affliction-state (kleśadaśā), producing slight anguish (tanutāpavidhātrī), comes (eti) into the mind's range (mānasagocaram) —
— then alone (tadaiva) my nondifference with You (mama tvadabhedaḥ), and the rain of supreme nectar arises (stotraparāmṛtavṛṣṭir udeti).
Affliction's arrival dated as nondifference's occasion: with it, not after it, the nectar rains.
The verse inverts the expected: suffering is not the enemy of recognition but its trigger.
inference: Affliction is the occasion, not the obstacle: nondifference + nectar arise with it, not after it.
uncertainties: Whether 'tanutāpa' (slight anguish) is physical or mental is unresolved.
Whether 'yadaiva' is temporal or conditional is unresolved.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (devotee's voice, first-person address)
question: What do rites and scripture each accomplish?
premises: Truly (satyam), O Śaṅkara: vow (vrata), giving (dāna), bathing (snāna), austerity (tapas) — dispels (vidāri) becoming's heat (bhavatāpa).
Rites relativized, not despised: heat dispelled by rites.
Contemplation (cintā) of Your (tāvaka) scripture (śāstra) as supreme nectar (parāmṛta), in mind (cetasi), streams (syandati) a bliss-stream (nirvṛtidhārā).
Heat dispelled by rites; bliss streamed by contemplation.
inference: Two means, two results: rites dispel heat, contemplation streams bliss.
uncertainties: Whether 'vadeśakālam' is obscure or means 'place-and-time under control' is unresolved.
Whether the rites are listed exhaustively or exemplarily is unresolved.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (devotee's voice, first-person rejoicing)
question: What is obtaining, and who obtains?
premises: This consciousness of mine (saṃvid iyaṃ mama) dances (nṛtyati), sings (gāyati), deeply (gāḍham) rejoices (hṛṣyati) — O Bhairava-Lord.
Having obtained (āpya) You, the dear (priyam): the beautiful vision alone (sudarśanam ekam), hard to get by others (durlabham anyajanaiḥ).
Addressed to, and fenced to, the knower of the samaya (samayajña).
Joy first, then its cause named: obtaining = vision, rare by structure.
inference: Joy, then its cause: obtaining is vision, rare by structure and fenced to the initiated.
uncertainties: Whether 'samayajña' is vocative or qualifier converging on the same fence is unresolved.
Whether 'sudarśanam ekam' means 'the one beautiful vision' or 'beautiful vision alone' is unresolved.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (devotee's voice, first-person colophon)

premises: In the month of Pauṣa, on the dark tenth, Abhinavagupta made this hymn: dated, signed.

By whom (yena) — devotee or hymn, undivided in effect — the pervasive (vibhuḥ), compassionate (dayāluḥ) Lord becomes (bhavati), pacifies (śamayati) the world's desert-heat of becoming — instantly (jhaṭiti).
The dated hymn turns outward: private recognition cools the world.
The verse moves from colophon to pacification to speed: inward dissolution (v.1) to world-pacification.
inference: Dated and signed: the hymn turns outward, private recognition cools the world.
uncertainties: Whether 'yena' refers to devotee or hymn is unresolved.
Whether 'bhavamarusantāpa' is physical or existential heat is unresolved.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)

premises: Never-setting light-form of bright powers and darknesses — darkness included, not opposed (api).
One within, in whom powers and darknesses end (yadantaḥ: limit and abode both).
inference: The all-containing One: light that never sets, holding bright and dark.
uncertainties: yadantaḥ read as limit and abode both — verse lets both stand.

inference: Identity, not process: He alone beings' nature; all things His Lordship-shaped power.
uncertainties: īśvaratāmayī read as power's form, not a second entity.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)

premises: Power wants no apartness from the power-bearer (na vāñchati: will, not mechanism).
Eternal identity of the two — sealed by fire-and-burning only ground offered.
inference: No-desire-for-difference, then eternal identity; fire-burning seals it.
uncertainties: na vāñchati personifies non-separation as will — kept as stated.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)

premises: He alone Bhairava, world-bearing-marked; reflection by power His manner (no emanation language).
Vision itself the mirror (svātmādṛś); no reflecting agent besides power named.
inference: Character then mechanism: world-bearing mark, power-mirroring manner.
uncertainties: Mirror-not-place reading; power sole agent.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: Whose is the goddess, and what does she want?
premises: His alone the supreme goddess, eager only for own-nature-grasping (desire bounded as granted).
Exact fullness in all beings: neither little nor excess (definition of pūrṇatva).
inference: Belonging, bounded eagerness, exact fullness.
uncertainties: utsukā appetite bounded to grasping; exactness not approximation.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: What do god and goddess do together?
premises: Always play-joy-eager (mood); varied creation-dissolution at once (act).
Simultaneity needs ubiquity: yugapad load-bearing, vibhuḥ closing.

premises: He who, made of the widely flashing wheel of diverse states, comes to be the objects of experience.
Whose one is given to contemplation, thus the bond of nondifference: Śaṃbhura, woe-averting, triumphs — treasury of the lights of knowing.
inference: The mangala invokes the knowing-treasury: the bhāva-cakra's nondifference-bond names what the work stores — bodha-bhāsās.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (mangala colophon)
question: Why is the Gītā held supreme among expositions?
premises: By the sage Dvaipāyana this scripture was expounded, measured by hundreds of thousands; here liberation is established as the fruit.
Other dharma-and-rest of it is recited to nourish that fruit [mādhānyataḥ: LIVE fork, grounds in L0].
inference: The Gītārthasaṃgraha claims prāmāṇya through Vyāsa-lineage, sahasraśata-measure, and mokṣa-as-phala; the forked ablative's sense-slot stays open (honest gap).
uncertainties: 5 LIVE L0 forks in this unit-set (see L0 grounds): yadekamayabhāvanāvaśata, etyabhedānvayaṃ, śaṃbhuraśivāpaho, mādhānyataḥ (prime), iyānprathiḥ — print corrupt per Ingalls; Gita Supersite + Sharma 1983 pending

speaker: Abhinavagupta (mangala colophon)
question: What is liberation named as?
premises: Liberation by name is complete-differentiation in form, all-knowing, auspicious-natured, free from need, in Bhagavān the Lord, ever-risen.
Dissolution — this much [prathiḥ: LIVE fork] — in summary.
inference: Mokṣa is defined by compound-nature (saṃskāra-svabhāva, sarvajña, nityodita) and reduced to laya in samāsa — the forked 'this-much-toward-it' held open.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (mangala colophon)
question: How does the Gītā compare to other mokṣa-celebrations?
premises: Although liberation by name is celebrated in other connections, yet the Bhagavadgītā is the giver of true attainment.
inference: Other texts sing mokṣa incidentally; the Gītā gives samyak-prāpti — the supremacy claim is exclusive (samyak retained).

speaker: Abhinavagupta (mangala colophon)
question: Why write another exposition?
premises: Earlier ones made many expositions among them, yet this attempt is reasonable — revealing its hidden meaning.
inference: The udyama is justified by gūḍhārtha-prakāśana: prior vyākhyās are many, this one discloses the hidden sense (bhāṣya not prakaraṇa).

speaker: Abhinavagupta (mangala colophon)
question: What is this work's colophon?
premises: From Bhaṭṭa Indurāja's oral tradition, examined long with thought, made by Abhinavagupta — this here is the Gītārthasaṃgraha.
inference: The verse seals authorship: āmnāya from Bhaṭṭa Indurāja (his Pratyabhijñā teacher), long vivicana, kṛta by Abhinavagupta — the name declared.

speaker: Utpaladeva's pūrvapakṣin (Buddhist objector voice), reported by Abhinavagupta
question: Given that action, object and determination all fail, and the relation itself is refuted, what becomes of the agent?
premises: A fourfold absence is consolidated as the reason: absence of action, of the other, of the relation, and of the determination of their being (abhāvacatuṣṭaya, hetutā via tena).
The relation cannot stand: what rests on two cannot be one (dviṣṭhasyānekatvāt); the established expects nothing further (siddhasyānyānapekṣaṇāt); dependence is unfitting (pāratantryādyayogāt).
Refutation works by determined non-being with place-time restriction (here, now, no jar) — not by bare non-perception; universal absence needs a prameya-grounded contradiction (tadrūpadvayavirodha).
The general-characteristic refuter: two simultaneous own-form completions cannot be one (two jars in two houses); ekatva is non-distinct form.

Expectation (apekṣā) cannot save the relation: in the inert it is unfit; the rājñaḥ puruṣa example shows the genitive marks dependence, not a real relation; mutual expectation collapses into word-only unity.
Therefore the agent too is constructed (tena kartāpi kalpitaḥ): the pūrvapakṣa closes, to be reversed by the siddhānta (the agent as the real, free self).
inference: Since relation is impossible in every proposed form (dependence, expectation, adhesion, word), and refutation is secured by determined non-being, the agent — like action and object before it — is only imagined.
uncertainties: dviṣṭhasyānekarūpatvāt: the two-resting many-form crux kept as Abhinavagupta states it.
sārvātrikī asattā via tadrūpadvayavirodha: Abhinavagupta’s own move, kept close.

saṃśca opening quotation (L0 AMBIGUOUS): unresolvable from T1/pilot; left open.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (commentator voice)
question:
The ṣaṣṭho vimarśa (the apohanaśakti) closes. Its final concern: the inner appearance
(antarābhāsa) stands firm in memory, construction, and cognition alike (kārikā 8); it is innate in the
cognition whose form is the external manifestation, while it stands in memory etc. (kārikā 9); it is
innate in the freely-wandering construction (kārikā 10); and hence, from the manifestation of the
uplifting as wished, knowledge and action are clear for every living one (kārikā 11). Along the way,
the freed souls (muktāṇava) and the mantreśvaras are discussed.
premises:
Even in the mokṣa-state, the freed atoms (muktāṇava) — from the parama-śiva, from the
ādi-śiva-ness, from the stain-removal-manifested-śiva-ness — have a distinction. By this part, in the
duality-side, the freed atoms are indeed distinct, and their manifestation, by the śiva-ness, is the
un-broken all-knowing; but the three-time-manifestation, being established in the māyīya-knower's
manifestation, does not fail to flash for them either (from their all-knowing). The 'ca' says: the
mantreśvaras, by the authority's exhaustion, even in the mokṣa, in that place, of the other — the atom's
word-obtaining-cause, the dīkṣā, the vow, the japa, the tapas, the samādhāna, the caryā — by the
transmigration, being all-knowing, in the traiyambaka, the knower-ness is not de-valued — so with
respect to the mantreśvara too, the eternal is fit. The "paśvaṇūn" (the animal-atoms) — the
animal-ness only, generally. The "tattvabhuvanādayaḥ" (the categories, the worlds) — the ādi includes
the bhāvabhūta, the kalā, the mantra, the word, the phoneme. Even the jars and the rest, with respect
to their own class, are not utterly unprecedented. The 'iti' shows the reason in the future meaning
("not then-created and then-withdrawn"). The prior-created-ness. The objection "how, in the dealing-
time, is the creation?" — the prior-view's reasonableness is shown. The "kintu" (but) removes the
"then how is the creation" — at that time, by the unity-going; "tathā sati" (thus being): per-knower,
the jar-appearance and the body-appearance are distinct; but (the vāsanāprabodha-sūtra 1.5.5, and the
1.5.7 sūtra) — the consciousness-self alone. The objection "then the knower-distinction is destroyed" —
answered: no (natu); by the prāṇa-puryaṣṭaka, in the triśākhā-and-the-rest-distinction-standing, the
sameness. And "the appearance is called the cognition" — the objection "the jar-form appearance is the
known, how is it the cognition?" — answered: "of the knower-operation-form, and"; "of the knower-
standing-ness." The objection "then by the knower's will, the knower-other-joining, per-moment the
creation and withdrawal of the objects and the knowers — how does the maheśvara shine?" — answered
("sā ca," "evamartham api"): not only the vṛtti's order-word's pure-form-sequence, but...
inference:
Decision for L2
Proceed. The argument is understood: the freed atoms and the mantreśvaras are distinct yet
all-knowing (their manifestation un-broken); the creation is by the unity, per-knower; the appearance is
the cognition; and kārikās 8–11 establish that the inner appearance stands firm in memory/construction/
cognition alike, innate in the cognition and the free construction, and that knowledge and action are
clear for every living one. The ||6|| colophon closes the apohanaśaktividadhi.
EOF

speaker: Abhinavagupta (commentator voice)
question:
The saptamo vimarśa closes with the question of the *omniscient* (sarvajña) — the
supreme knower who is the support of all the powers. The Buddhist objector presses: if the piśāca (the
goblin) is not perceived even by the omniscient, how can he deny it? The analysis turns on whether the
omniscient's non-perception of the piśāca establishes its non-being, and how the ordinary knower
(arvāgdarśana) differs. This grounds the omniscient as the one who knows all — the support of the
powers.
premises:
Even if the piśāca is not seen by us, the form-and-the-rest atoms are there — not seen by us, but seen
by the omniscient. The atoms have no un-precedented variety. The "na tathā" — the obstructing ones
also, not utterly. The "dūrataram" — the shadow, made by the darkness, with the interval, the
distinguished, the same-class-devoid interval; the middle-darkness or the middle-void. In their own
place, they withdraw; by the unable-moment-production-order, they are withdrawn. Hence the
piśāca-atoms are, for the omniscient, equal to the darkness-and-the-rest-other-being-atoms. But if the
piśāca is absent, then where the piśāca had occupied the interval, the āloka-atoms alone, being seen,
are the object of the piśāca's-absence-dealing for the omniscient. The objection: "seeing the other
objects, how does the omniscient deny the distinct piśāca?" — in the piśāca's being-or-not-being, the
own-form-standing of these is not lost; the distinct-piśāca's-absence is, by this way, hard to
establish even by the omniscient. The "athavā" (or): whatever is, is to be seen by him; then, there, if
he does not see the piśāca, it is not — and there, everything is the piśāca-included thing, known by
another cognition distinct from its being; or that very cognition is the object of the
piśāca's-absence-dealing — so the interval-atom-tracing does nothing. The objection "why is it not so
for us too?" — answered (arvāk): "he who sees the limited, for him there is no known" — this
cognition arises, by which the cognition is the cause of the being-included-cognition-marker
non-being-dealing. But where the certainty arises (like the smelling, the tasting, the attending, the
touching — the necessary-conceiving of the smell-cognition), there the smell-cognition's removal is
the cause of the non-being-dealing (the breath-entering-cognition-marker, the un-divided-from-the-
smell-taste-sound-touch-absence). Hence, though the piśāca's-absence is grasped by him who grasps the
āloka or the place (by the piśāca's otherness), still it is the limited, grasped as if un-grasped (no
cause of the removal of the conceiving of the distinct in the place or the āloka). The objection "if
the piśāca's non-negatability's cause is the invisibility, then the jar's negatability's cause would
be the visibility (1.7.10, the 'svajñāna-maghaṭātmatā')" — answered (siddham): "every negation
culminates in the identity-negation; and there the visibility is un-deviating (the hetubindu: the
distinction is to be said)."
inference:
Decision for L2
Proceed. The argument is understood: the omniscient, seeing all the atoms, knows the piśāca's absence
in its place (the āloka-atoms alone); the limited seer (arvāk) cannot — his non-perception is only the
limited, not the established non-being; and every negation culminates in the identity-negation, where
the visibility is un-deviating. The omniscient is the support of all the powers — the one who knows all,
whose non-perception establishes, whose perception is whole. The ||7|| colophon closes the saptamo
vimarśa.

speaker: Abhinavagupta expounding Utpaladeva (siddhānta voice, with pūrvapakṣa objections recorded as nanu)
question: How is the unity of the knowers established, and what does it establish — the great-Lordship that closes the jñānādhikāra?
premises: Kārikā 10: without that unity the world-path of consciousnesses would not be; from manifestation-unity, that one-ness; that one alone is the knower.
The dealing test: all shared practice (teaching, buying-selling, doubt, reasoning) presupposes one light; even Sāṃkhya, Jaiminīya and Vaiśeṣika witnesses confirm a self-luminous one.
Objections met: self-experience rest, blue-tint, mutual expectation, shell-silver error — each resolved by locating difference inside the one manifestation (māyā-śakti) without breaking it.
Kārikā 11: he alone, by fixed reflexive-awareness, is the great Lord; reflexive awareness is the God’s pure knowledge-action — Lordship is self-awareness, not an added power.
The vṛtti’s anuvāda/bhitti logic and the smoke-fire rule secure the exposition; the ahaṃ-vimarśa pervades pure, mixed and impure states, gathered not abandoned.
Colophons close both the aṣṭama vimarśa (śaktivargaikāśraya) and the whole first adhikāra (samāpta).
inference: The knowers are one because the manifestation is one and the manifestation is the knower; and the one knower, fixed in self-awareness, is the great Lord — which completes the jñānādhikāra.
uncertainties: Ajaḍapramātṛsiddhi 20 and 1.2.7 citations — cited, applications preserved.
Bhitti (wall-like) vs smoke-rule anuvāda distinction — kept as stated.

speaker: Abhinavagupta closing the IPVV (siddhānta voice, with pūrvapakṣa objections and the vivṛtikāra's lineage-praise)
question: How does the whole teaching close — what is the single recognition-path, and by what transmission does it stand?
premises: The maṅgala opens the close: the unsurpassed form spreading as bliss-sequence, the world held, all nectar borne within and without — the work bows before summing itself.

The triple source is fixed: part from the self, part from the śāstra, part must come from the guru — book-learning without the guru-order is mocked (the śāstra-sight needs the lineage to reach its proper power).

Kārikā 1 announces the path: well-fitted, new, shown for effortless attainment; kārikā 2 gives the lover-analogy (the unrecognized beloved near at hand); kārikā 3 names the author and the purpose (Utpala establishes it for the effortless attainment of people).
Objections are met on the way: the Sāṃkhya/Buddhist/Vaiśeṣika positions, the smoke-fire rule and the wall-like restatement, the threefold ahaṃ-vimarśa gathering pure, mixed and impure states.

The vivṛtikāra praises the lineage in seventeen verses — Varāhagupta, Cukhulaka, Bhūtirāja, Lakṣmaṇagupta, Tryambaka — and hands the work to the Lord with the two colophons (samastanigamana, samāptā).
inference: The closing sum gathers the whole teaching into one transmission — guru, śāstra, self — and one path: recognition itself, effortless, complete, handed on.
uncertainties: Lineage hagiographic details (Śrīkaṇṭhanātha → Durvāsa → Tryambakāditya) — preserved as given, not re-derived.
Print lacunae and wrap-splits (10 AMBIGUOUS L0 rows) — extent unknown, never smoothed.

speaker: Utpaladeva (maṅgala, praise voice)
question: Under what auspice does the Lord's proof open?
premises: He who makes (karoti) — him (tam), I (aham) praise (naumi): the one (ekam) God (devam), Maheśvara the Lord.
The auspice names the conclusion in advance: maker, one, Lord.
inference: Auspice: praise of the one maker-Lord whose proof follows.
uncertainties: Opening pādas lost to print lacuna; the surviving half-verse is complete as praise.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: What is the inference to be proved?
premises: Bodies and the rest (tanvādi) have conscious cause (buddhimaddhetu), having distinct arrangement (saṃniveśaviśeṣavat).
Like pots (ghaṭa ... like atoms, paramāṇuvat — mid-verse lacuna).
The Nyāya shape is unmistakable: pakṣa (bodies), hetu (arrangement), dṛṣṭānta (pot).
inference: Thesis stated in Nyāya dress: arranged bodies bespeak a conscious maker, like pots.
uncertainties: Mid-verse gap (dots) eats the example's middle; atoms-vs-pot pairing partly lost — read with prose.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: What survives of the example's turn?
premises: Urged by the conscious (buddhimat-prorito) — or (vā) ... [lacuna].
Remnant ṭato ([ta]ṭo? — thence?) — pot (ghaṭaḥ), as (yathā).
The yathā-form survives: 'as pot from [tha]t' — example-phrase intact.
inference: Fragment: the example-form (as pot...) survives its verse.
uncertainties: Major lacuna; prorito unattested (pra+√īr?); ṭato unresolved. No doctrine built on remnants.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: What survives of the fixed-meaning turn?
premises: ... without arrangement ([saṃ]skāra-saṃsthāna-varjitaḥ?).
Fixed (niścitaḥ) is its meaning (arthaḥ) in locus (saṃsthāne) — in that (tasmin), action-heaped (arthakriyā) ... (cite remnant).
inference: Fragment: fixed meaning in its locus, amid action-heaping.
uncertainties: Leading lacuna; cite isolated (vocative of cita? severed compound?). Held open.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: How is the maker marked?
premises: In the varied (vicitre), the conscious alone (buddhimān eva) is marked (lakṣyate) — as among pots (ghaṭādiṣv iva).
The maker (kartā), wise (vijñaḥ), having resolve for varied-this-use (vicitraitadupayogābhisaṃdhimān).
Prose: variety (vaicitrya) is the mark editors of Nyāya-examples read for intelligence.
inference: Variety marks the wise maker: resolved on varied use, visible among pots.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: Can matter arrange?
premises: There is (asti), in function-yoking (arthakriyāyoge), among bodies and worlds (śarīrabhuvanādiṣu).
This distinct arrangement (ayam saṃniveśaviśeṣaḥ) — not possibly from material (anupādānasaṃbhavī).
inference: Arrangement in function-fit things cannot come from matter alone.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: What follows from proved makers?
premises: Then here (tat atra), by proving conscious makers (buddhimatkartṛsiddhyā), Lord-action is proved (siddheśvarakriyā).
For knowers of such variety (tādṛśavaicitryaviduṣaḥ), non-lordliness (anīśitā) is impossible (syāt = would be — denied).
inference: Makers proved prove the Lord's act: variety-knowers cannot be lordless.

speaker: Objector (Nyāya-Buddhist voice; cf. anvaya debates)
question: Does concomitance hold for potter or Lord?
premises: Neither by potter (kulālena) nor by Lord (īśena) is agreement (anvayaḥ) shown here (atra).
Since (yatas) for him there would be either opposition (viruddhatā) or unproved agreement (asiddhānvayatā).
Prose: the stock Nyāya worry — anvaya with an unseen maker is unproved; with a seen one, off-point.
inference: Objection stated: the concomitance fails on both horns — opposition or unprovedness.
uncertainties: Voice attribution (objection vs concession) from prose context; the reply (v09) confirms objector.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: What answers the anvaya dilemma?
premises: Merely (kevalam) even from showing (saṃdarśanāt) pervasion (vyāpti) with the conscious alone (buddhimanmātra).
By thesis-property force (pakṣadharmabalāt), somewhere (kvacit), someone (kaścit) wise (dhīmān) is understood (pratīyate).
inference: Reply: bare showing of conscious-only pervasion suffices — by pakṣadharma-force alone, some wise one is grasped. Minimalism against the dilemma.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: How is the higher self shown in eye etc.?
premises: As (yathā) combination-ness (saṃghātatva) is seen (anvitekṣite) merely for another's sake (pārārthyamātreṇa).
In eye etc. (cakṣurādau), by that fitness (tadaucityāt): the self-dear (ātmeṣṭaḥ), uncompounded (asaṃhataḥ), higher (paraḥ).
Prose: Sāṅkhya's own eye-example turned — fitness, not assemblage, shows the self-cherished uncompounded.
inference: The higher self shows in eye etc. by fitness, as combination seen for another's sake.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: How is fire proved as khadira-wood?
premises: As (yathā) from afar (dūrataḥ), from smoke (dhūmāt), proving (siddhiḥ) in a khadira-grove (khadirakānane).
Fire (vahniḥ) is proved (siddhyati) just by knowing it (tatpratipattyā), as khadira-wood (khādiratvena).
Stock smoke-fire example redeployed: mere knowing-it suffices for wood-kind — no need to see the logs.
inference: Fire is proved as khadira-wood by mere knowing: the stock example turned for fitness.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: What is the hetu, and what is excluded?
premises: Thus (evam) the cause (hetuḥ): locus-form alone (saṃsthānamātram), here (atra) distinguished (viśeṣitam).
Not (na) by variety merely (vaicitryamātreṇa) as svalakṣaṇa-mark (svalakṣaṇalakṣmaṇā).
Prose: against the Buddhist svalakṣaṇa-only mark — bare variety doesn't mark; the hetu is fenced.
inference: The hetu stated (locus-form alone) and fenced: not bare variety as particular-mark.
uncertainties: svalakṣaṇalakṣmaṇā scope (whose mark?) from prose — read as the Buddhist's mark, refused.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: What do others sift?
premises: By others too (paraiḥ taiḥ api), of reasons (hetūnāṃ), in pot-self-sifting (ghaṭātmapravivecane).
Locus-form alone (saṃsthānamātram) ... even (eva) ... [gap] ... causehood (hetutvam) of the conscious-possessor (buddhiśālinaḥ).
inference: Others too sift reasons in pot-self-analysis: bare locus-form [carries] the conscious one's causehood.
uncertainties: Mid-verse gap (eva…); the carried predicate partly lost — read with prose, nothing restored.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: What whole is rightly Lord-made?
premises: Mutual-function-fit-locus-formed (anyonyārthakriyāyogyasaṃniveśaviśeṣitam) — that (tat), this (idam) whole (sakalam) world (viśvam).
Rightly (yuktam) Lord-made (īśvaranirmitam).
inference: The mutual-fit world-whole is rightly Lord-made.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: What strange way of helpers?
premises: Here it is replied (atrocyate): a strange way (gatiścitrā) of helpers (sahakāriṇām) is seen (dṛśyate).
Some (kecit) somehow (kathaṃcid) would join (eveyuḥ) with materials (upādānaiḥ) — a joining (samāgamam).
Metrically confirmed v15ab (8+8); atrocyate kept as verse-opening reply-formula.
inference: Reply-frame opened: helpers show a strange way — some joining with materials somehow.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: How do helpers picture effects?
premises: Helpers (hetumantaḥ), entering (praviśya) as others (anye), reaching (prāpya) material-form (upādānarūpatām).
They picture (citrayanti) effects (kāryāṇi) — like earth-water-juices (bhaumodakarasā iva).
inference: Helpers picture effects by entering-as-other and reaching material-form — like earth-juices.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: Are outward-changers capable?
premises: Others (anye), again (punar), in material (upādāne), outward-changing (bahirviparivartinaḥ).
For form-variety-yoking (rūpavaicitryayogāya) in effects (kāryeṣu) — not so (na tathā) capable (kṣamāḥ).
inference: Outward-changers in matter can't yoke form-variety in effects.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: Does imagined spread order all?
premises: There (tatra), if (yadi) the conscious one's spread (prasaraḥ) by name (nāma) be imagined (kalpyate).
Not (na) by that much alone (tāvataiva) does order (vyavasthā) hold everywhere (sarvatra) — thus (tathā ghaṭate).
inference: Imagined spread of the conscious doesn't alone order everywhere.

speaker: Sāṅkhya (pūrvapakṣin)
question: How is pradhāna proved?
premises: There is (asti), of this proved (prasiddhasya) pradhāna (pradhānasya), by anvaya and the rest (anvayādinā).
By denial (niṣedhena) of self-aims and the like (svārthatādi), person-aim-ness (puruṣārthatā) is proved (sādhitā).
Prose: Sāṅkhya's satkārya/anvaya apparatus — pradhāna established through concomitance, purposed to spirit.

speaker: Sāṅkhya (pūrvapakṣin)
question: How easy is change?
premises: Through that (tena), person's (puruṣasya) enjoyment-proving (bhogasaṃsiddhiḥ) — again and again (yathā yathā).
So (tathā tathā), change (pariṇatiḥ) would be (syāt) nothing (na kiṃcana) hard (durghaṭam).
inference: Change comes easy, again and again, for spirit's enjoyment.

speaker: Sāṅkhya (pūrvapakṣin)
question: What moves pradhāna?
premises: Hence indeed (ata eva), for ever-becoming (mahattvapariṇāminaḥ) pradhāna (pradhānasya).
No (na) nimitta-cause (nimittakāraṇaṃ) other (anyat) but (ṛte) person-aim-striving (puruṣārthodyamāt).
inference: Only person-aim-striving moves ever-becoming pradhāna.

speaker: Sāṅkhya (pūrvapakṣin)
question: What is own-nature for?
premises: Own-nature (svabhāvaḥ) indeed (eva) — and (ca) this (eṣaḥ) of this (asya).
From seeing the root-cause then (mūlahetoḥ tatekṣaṇāt); below mind-ground (cittabhūmer adharataḥ), toward body-ordaining (śarīrādi vidhim).
inference: Own-nature faces downward: from root-cause-seeing toward body's ordaining.
uncertainties: tatekṣaṇāt parsed then-seeing (tat+ekṣaṇāt); at-the-moment (tate+kṣaṇāt) equivalent in force — settled.

speaker: Sāṅkhya closing / siddhāntin opening (pivot)
question: As efficient cause (nimittakāraṇaṃ), karma (karma) could be (syāt) even (api) original-natured (ādya-svabhāvataḥ).

And (ca) thereby (tena): godless (anīśvaram) Sāṅkhya (sāṃkhyam).

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: What is conceived?

By pradhāna (pradhānasya) it is conceived (upakalpyate) as efficient (nimittakāraṇatvena).
inference: Conditional close: puruṣārtha-natured acts conceived efficient by pradhāna.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: Without what no pot?
premises: Without that (tat vinā) — without potter (kumbhakāreṇa) — even a pot (ghaṭo'pi).
How (katham) could it be (bhavet)?
inference: No pot without potter: how else could it be?

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: What of clay-lump nature?

Now (atha): own-nature (svabhāvaḥ) — this (eṣaḥ) of this (asya) — which (yat) looks to potter and the rest (kulālādi apekṣaṇam).
inference: Own-nature looks to potter etc.: clay-lump nature potter-watching.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: Can helpers entering matter arrange?
premises: Not (na) indeed (eva): by entering (praveśāt) inside the material cause (upādānahetvantaḥ), with helpers (sahakāribhiḥ).
Arrangement (saṃniveśaḥ) could (śakyaḥ) be made (kartum), they say (iti) — though able (kṣamam).
Prose: entering doesn't transfer arrangement-making; helpers stay helpers.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)

inference: No will, no wonders: mere grossness, never world-good.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)

person-aim-ness (puruṣārthatā).

inference: Compassion smuggles passion back; the view becomes passion-exhaustion doctrine.

inference: Arrangement-difference seals the design inference.

Not overpowered by reason-faults in the least (na hetudoṣaiḥ paribhūyate manāk).
Nor the rival's either — only this is said (paro'pi vā kevalam etad ucyate).
inference: The hetu stands aimed at the Lord; rivals answered, disputation closed.

question: Proved — yet for whom in vain?
premises: Though proved by a thousand blazing reasons (samujjvalan nyāyasahasrasādhito'py upaiti).
It succeeds not for the deluded-minded (siddhiṃ na vimūḍhacetasām).
Maheśvara, placed on the palm, yet flees the fate-struck — the true jewel (maheśvaraḥ pāṇitalasthito'pi san palāyate daivahatasya sanmaṇiḥ).
inference: Proof needs fitness; the jewel flees the fated.

speaker: Utpaladeva (signature)

premises: One's own self indeed — this — flashes forth: Īśvara within all breathers (svātmaivāyaṃ sphurati sakalaprāṇinām īśvaro'ntaḥ).
Maker and knower too (kartā jñātāpi ca).
Yet recognition of the beyond is to be effected (yadi paraṃ pratyabhijñāsya sādhyā).
And the joining is made by us elsewhere (sā cāsmābhir vihitaghaṭanānyatra).
But Īśvara-proved stands even in duality (kiṃ tv īśasiddhir dvaite'py asti).
Fitting, and more: fire shines at midnight (ity ucitam adhikaṃ bhāti vahnir niśīthe).

inference: Self-examination redoubled makes hymning effortless.

premises: Unscrutinized self never shares thing-knowing; unscrutinized, without grasping-course, it is not.

That within, in teaching-spread-course-become light: clearly in speech obtained — show the Lord's hymn now.
inference: Omniscience gained effortlessly; heart bidden to show the hymn in speech.

From varied self-swelling glory's rushing start, drinking things — O giver — mad-drunk am I, blissful.
