premises: In emitted thing-share outside, in extreme taste-bliss, You resort by rush to redness-made.
Then red goddess, Yours in all things — make me, by red-drinking-order-joined conclave, past-loathing.
inference: Rush to redness; past-loathing in red rite prayed.
uncertainties: ghṛṇā double sense (loathing/compassion) held; nanu as prayer-particle.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (devotee voice)
question: What shall the goddess grasp?
premises: To quit outer work, dwell in noble knowing-ground; show thing-nondifference, waves gone fickle.
Goddess grasps maintenance's end; may she ever grasp my wandering state's undoing, Lord.
inference: Quit outer, dwell noble, show undivided; grasp ends — maintenance's and mine.
uncertainties: vinaṣṭormicapalaḥ kept.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (devotee voice)
question: How is world-fear ground?
premises: Wishing calm by world-loosing: rule of doubt-fear, then ban — shown; Yama emitted.
Splitting doubt again — may the great goddess grind my world-fear.
inference: Rule-then-ban shown, Yama made, doubt split: grind world-fear.
uncertainties: vidhi/niṣedha pair kept.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (devotee voice)
question: What survives melting?
premises: Doubt-heap melted, conduct gone, glory gone, rule gone — all melted.
Hunger remains: to gulp the endless feast — strike, dissolution-named, my heart's split part.
inference: All melted but hunger: strike prayed.
uncertainties: laṃpaṭarasā kept raw.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (devotee voice)
question: Who makes death-dissolution?
premises: By goddesses at once, difference-glory split — thought-living one shines, knower-standing. Enough.
Considered in own heart, dissolution-formed, gracious — my death-loosing maker, blessed Lady.
inference: Goddesses split difference; thought shines; considered maker gracious.
uncertainties: mātṛsthiti kept.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (devotee voice)
question: What do the three ordain?
premises: So your three, by own-power-expanse-force obtained, six-wheel-course-made-step powers these.
By order, by unfolding, they ordain varied world-state; by these goddesses, devoted-hearted may I be, fear-gone.
inference: Three obtained ordain by unfolding; devotee prays fear-gone by them.
uncertainties: tisraḥ feminine (powers) kept.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (devotee voice)
question: What ground holds, and what conduct sports?
premises: This ground she holds — world-fear-splitting-dread-making; this wake-one-pointed-melted-taste-formed — ordained too.
So holding, melting, wiping inauspicious stretches, as-pleased conduct resorted — may she sport in my heart.
inference: Ground held dread-making; conduct as-pleased sporting in heart prayed.
uncertainties: rundhe/vidadhe middle voices kept.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (devotee voice)
question: What draws the sap, and what thins difference?
premises: On limited step, measurer's step gained, its spread by own-own gleam contracting — she who draws the all-sap of the station-yoked day-sun (mārtaṇḍasya normalized).
Drawing forcibly — may she thin my difference from world-fear.
inference: Sun-sap drawn forcibly; difference thinned from world-fear prayed.
uncertainties: mārtāṇḍasya normalization recorded.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (devotee voice)
question: How enter, and how be adorned?
premises: Whole garland, sequenceless, in self again entered — endless-inner-massed-great-ray-heaped.
Supreme, divine-bliss to grasp, noble-eager, gracious to me may she be — heart-path let her adorn. (Second hemistich recovered — T1 gap fixed.)
inference: Garland entered again; gracious heart-path-adornment prayed.
uncertainties: Recovered hemistich recorded; bhavet→bhūyāt corrected.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (devotee voice)
question: When does the goddess shine Śiva-made?
premises: In proof merged, by Śiva-step-shining-glory-force: body-breath-made, measured-made-knower-standing.
When time-cadre reaches dissolution-step of Yours — then the goddess who shines, mine — she would be Śiva-made.
inference: Measure merged in proof; time-cadre met: shining Śiva-made.
uncertainties: chivamayī print ch- noted.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (devotee voice)
question: How does cover spread, and time get made?
premises: Manifestation-named consciousness, sequenceless, from void-step, outside-merged — spreads utterly as covering.
Then too in inner-essence, by melted rush, sequencelessly — great Time-goddess, making all time (kalayantī emended; print kalayatāṃ fork live).
inference: Cover spread outside; time made within: Mahākālī.
uncertainties: kalayantī emendation with live fork (print anomalous).

speaker: Abhinavagupta (devotee voice)
question: What shall the mind resort?
premises: Then in the goddess in whom supreme-full-standing-enjoying: sequence cut, quickly, standing-minded-taste reflecting —
Proof, knower, measure, whole world this standing embraced — may my mind resort to this consciousness.
inference: Sequence cut in full goddess; all embraced; mind resort prayed.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (devotee voice)
question: Whom bow, unobstructed?
premises: Unobstructed, in self-made Lord, in great Lord abide pervading powers.
That power-possessor I venerate — god, churn-named, world-one-essence.
inference: Abiding powers; churn-named essence bowed.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (devotee voice)
question: What grace is asked?
premises: Thus own-power-ray-mass-praise-bonds heard — Lord, if You come to grace:
By that quickly all folk, by own-rule-rays, darkness-masses allayed — make ye.
inference: Heard praise-bonds; grace prayed; all-folk darkness-allayed bidden.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (dating seal, 991 CE)
question: When and by whom was Śiva praised?
premises: In the sixty-sixth year, on the ninth dark day, in Mārgaśīrṣa —
By me Abhinavagupta, Śiva was praised (colophon third-person, excluded).
inference: Dated seal: 66th year, 9th dark, Mārgaśīrṣa, Abhinavagupta.
uncertainties: Laukika 66 = 991 CE per research; colophon excluded as scribal.

speaker: Poet (maṅgala)
question: What is first worshipped?
premises: Homage to the world-formed, beyond the world.
To ever-divine-shining, self with unending power.
inference: The maṅgala names its object twice: the formed world transcended, the shining self whose power does not end.

speaker: Poet (identity)
question: Who are you, who am I?
premises: You alone are you; I alone am I; you alone are; I am not at all.
I and you as both are not: where homage, homage, homage.
inference: Identity and non-identity both refused: neither you alone nor I alone, nor both — only homage where the question lands.

speaker: Poet (seeking)
question: What is found inside?
premises: Sought inside the body by me always — you as self, and never seen is the self.
Whatever is seen is you alone, that.
inference: Seeking finds no self to see: whatever is seen is you alone — the sought turns out to be the seer.

speaker: Poet (recognition)
question: What does the devotee declare?
premises: Of your devotee who well knows your form, now again.
Having seen you as the self's form: to you homage, to me homage.
inference: Recognition declared both ways: seen as self, homage goes to you and to me — knower and known each honored.

speaker: Poet (method-question)
question: What finesse remains?
premises: What going-finesse, what to be done, thus, from the root.
Of yours, made of your magic power: by what, in what, whence the dissolving.
inference: Method questioned to its root: given your magic-nature, what instrument, what place, what origin could dissolving have.

speaker: Poet (non-duality)
question: Is there duality?
premises: I, you; you, I — thus: no duality of us anywhere.
Only the wish to grasp samādhi: abiding of difference is just that.
inference: Non-duality asserted, difference explained away: what looks like abiding difference is only the wish to grasp samādhi.

speaker: Poet (speech)
question: Where do words go?
premises: You-I and so-on, so endless, ever in you, never find a place.
Words, then — whence the world.
inference: Speech finds no room in you: if even I-and-you-talk cannot stay, whence a world of words.
uncertainties: Print variant so yamityādi nūnaṃ tāni noted; edition so'nantāni kept.

speaker: Poet (enough)
question: What is enough?
premises: Enough of difference-talk: from chewing the sap of devotion to you.
All this is one, at peace — even to say so is shy.
inference: Enough of talking difference: devotion chewed to sap leaves all as one, at peace — and even saying so is shy.

speaker: Poet (expansion)
question: What when you expand, what when you withdraw?
premises: Your own form expanding — you and I and the whole world.
Born its withdrawal — neither you nor I nor world indeed.
inference: Expansion holds all three; withdrawal holds none: being and nonbeing of you, me, world turn on your play.

speaker: Poet (actor)
question: Who shines like an actor yet stays partless?
premises: Waking-dream-deep-sleep and the rest, holding as own rays.
By own will you shine like an actor — partless, yet in truth.
inference: States held as own rays: shining by own will like an actor, yet partless in truth.
uncertainties: Print naTavan kept byte-true (probable slip for naṭavat actor-like); gloss follows sense.

speaker: Poet (derivation)
question: Whose is all this?
premises: From your waking, his waking; from your sleep, his rest.
Hence all is of your nature: the world as real-unreal.
inference: Waking and sleep derived: his waking yours, his rest yours — hence all is of your nature, real-and-unreal.

speaker: Poet (exhaustion)
question: What use are rites for the formless?
premises: The tongue is tired in your name; the mind is tired in remembering you.
Of the formless, what meditation; of the qualityless, what name.
inference: Rites exhausted at the start: tired tongue, tired mind — meditation with no form to hold, name with no quality to name.

speaker: Poet (kutaḥ)
question: Where is the seat for the all-based?
premises: Where is summoning for the full; where a seat for the all-based.
Foot-water and respects for the clean; sipping for the pure.
inference: The kutaḥ series opens: summoning, seating, washing, sipping — each rite asked where, for whom without place.

speaker: Poet (kutaḥ)
question: What bath, garment, scent, jewel?
premises: What bath for the stainless; what garment for the world-bellied.
What scent for the unanointed; what jewel for the lovely.
inference: Adornment rites interrogated: no bath, no garment, no scent, no jewel where stainless, world-full, unanointed, lovely.

speaker: Poet (kutaḥ)
question: What thread, flowers, incense, lamp?
premises: Sacred thread for the propless; flowers for the desireless.
Incense for the noseless, lamp for the eyeless — what use.
inference: Offering rites interrogated: thread, flowers, incense, lamp — each without a receiver.
uncertainties: Print variant apraṇasya (for-breathless) noted; edition aghrāṇa (noseless) kept.

speaker: Poet (kutaḥ)
question: What offering, circumambulation, obeisance?
premises: Food-offering for the ever-content, betel for the Lord — whence.
Circumambulation for the endless, obeisance for the non-dual — whence.
inference: Honorific rites interrogated: food, betel, circling, bowing — all without a needy recipient.

speaker: Poet (kutaḥ)
question: How is the hymn enjoined?
premises: Whence waving-lights for the self-shining Lord.
How is a hymn enjoined for the Veda-unspeakable.
inference: Even praise interrogated: lights for the self-shining, hymn for the unspeakable — enjoined how.

speaker: Poet (kutaḥ)
question: How sending-off, how oblation?
premises: How is sending-off for the full, inside and out.
And how is oblation for the difference-free, everywhere.
inference: Farewell and fire-offering interrogated: no going out for the full, no difference for the fire.

speaker: Poet (kutaḥ)
question: What fee, libation, dismissal, pardon?
premises: Where is the fee for the full; libation for the ever-content.
Dismissal for the all-pervading; pardon for the unseen.
inference: Closing rites interrogated: fee, drink, dismissal, pardon — none owed where full, content, everywhere, unseen.

speaker: Poet (seal)
question: What then is worship?
premises: Just so, indeed, the highest worship, in all states, always.
With nondual mind, yoke the mind to God as Lord of all.
inference: The answer after twenty negations: nondual mind yoked to the Lord of all, in every state, always — that is the highest worship.

speaker: author (devotional voice)
question: The whole duty is one act: pride offered on the Lord's feet; all else denied, and only immediate pleasure asked.
premises: What is true of my doing = one duty = offering of pride.
My all = this offering; anything other does not exist, for me.
Renunciation already accomplished (tyaktvā) grounds the plea: be pleased.
inference: Total offering of pride; plea for immediate pleasure.
uncertainties: Whether prasāda means 'pleasure' or 'grace' is unresolved.

speaker: author (devotional voice)
question: Speech becomes the offering: the word crying victory at the threshold is itself to become bliss-giving; having Maheśa as protector is to become being protected.
premises: Praise at the door is the offering.
The cry 'jaya jaya maheśa' is both act and instrument.
Status (sanātha) turns into request (make possessed of a protector).
inference: Speech becomes bliss-giving; request to be made protected.
uncertainties: Whether śivadā means 'bliss-bestowing' or 'Śiva-giving' is unresolved.

speaker: author (devotional voice)
question: Five refusals charged — speak, see, hear, come, support — and scripture converts the charge into doctrine: the Lord is sense-free.
premises: Five refusals charged: speak, see, hear, come, support.
Scripture converts the charge into doctrine: the Lord is sense-free.
prāyeṇa softens the unsupported claim.
inference: Complaint becomes doctrine: denial becomes declaration.
uncertainties: Whether the turn to śruti is sincere resolution or ironic resignation is unresolved.

speaker: author (devotional voice)
question: Against the silence stand two testimonies — the guru's word and fitting scriptural assurance — whose force wipes away piled-up reasonings; with doubt dissolved, the feet of the heart-sky Lord.
premises: Two testimonies: guru's word and fitting scriptural assurance.
Their force wipes away (not refutes) heaped reasonings.
Doubt-cloud dissolved, touch the feet of the heart-sky Lord.
inference: Two testimonies dissolve doubt; touch of feet follows.
uncertainties: Whether guru's word and scripture are two distinct sources or one twofold source is unresolved.

speaker: author (devotional voice)
question: Long dwelling-with and total grace received, yet repeated forgetting; the only request is no more absence.
premises: Long dwelling-with and total grace received.
Repeated forgetting admitted (kila).
Therefore no further staying-away requested.
inference: Confession and plea for presence.
uncertainties: prāsuvatkāyaḥ is obscure; glossed 'whose body has attained it'.

speaker: author (devotional voice)
question: Distinct from every lit thing, light itself does not shine as an object — too pervasive to appear; illumined-vs-illuminator is mere convention.
premises: Light itself does not shine as an object — too pervasive to appear.
Illumined-vs-illuminator is mere convention (vyavahāra).
What is, is light, unobjectifiable because everywhere.
inference: Light unobjectifiable; subject-object vocabulary demoted.
uncertainties: Whether 'iyat' (just this much) limits or affirms is unresolved.

speaker: author (devotional voice)
question: No thing stands dually apart from knowledge; in consciousness there is no difference; the individual, in the one abode of self-luminosity, stays undivided.
premises: No thing stands dually apart from knowledge.
In consciousness there is no difference.
The individual, in the one abode of self-luminosity, stays undivided.
inference: Non-duality: nothing apart from knowledge.
uncertainties: 'śatam' (hundredfold) vs 'satatam' (always) — print form kept, flagged.

speaker: author (devotional voice)
question: Dense, one own-consciousness is Śiva himself, the universe's supreme light — yet grasper-grasped division still shines within variegated power.
premises: Dense, one own-consciousness is Śiva himself, the universe's supreme light.
Yet grasper-grasped division still shines within variegated power.
Division shines without dividing the light.
inference: Positive declaration after denial; division within the undivided.
uncertainties: Whether 'ittham' (thus) refers back to p01-p02 or opens a new movement is unresolved.

speaker: author (devotional voice)
question: Difference is not cut off from its ground — free, most-clear, one-abode — then the bare list against the jewel-mirror: palace through mountain, just as from jewel-mirror and the like.
premises: Difference is not cut off from its ground — free, most-clear, one-abode.
Then the bare list: palace, elephant, horse, cloud, ocean, mountain.
Just as of jewel-mirror and the like — reflected things need no ground but the clear mirror.
inference: Difference uncut from its ground; the bare list its proof.
uncertainties: Whether the list is exhaustive or exemplary is unresolved.

speaker: author (devotional voice)
question: If even a common mirror shows prototype-with-reflection as mind-established, the free-consciousness mirror needs no other cause among things.
premises: If a common mirror shows prototype-with-reflection as mind-established...
...then the free-consciousness mirror needs no other cause among things.
Mukhura read as mukura (mirror) — print form kept, reading marked.
inference: A fortiori: mind-proven reflection needs no second cause.
uncertainties: Mukhura/mukura reading is an editorial decision, marked here.

speaker: author (devotional voice)
question: O consciousness-dense one: you indeed are supreme; in you the universes shine at once, flashing by glory-power; you stand as both their maker and their supreme Lord.
premises: O consciousness-dense one: you indeed are supreme.
In you the universes shine at once, flashing by glory-power.
You stand as both their maker and their supreme Lord.
inference: Address: all shining, flashing, making is in you.
uncertainties: Whether 'drāk' (at once) modifies shining or flashing is unresolved.

speaker: author (devotional voice)
question: Established yet unaccomplishable, non-lord yet lord, place-and-time full of own power — eternal, pervasive: Bhairava-Lord, I praise.
premises: Self-consciousness, primordially established, unaccomplishable.
Non-lord and lord at once — three incompatible predicates held.
Whose place and time are full of own power: eternal, pervasive — Bhairava-Lord, I praise.
inference: Paradox held without blinking; praise, not proof.
uncertainties: 'vadeśakālam' is obscure; glossed neutrally, marked here.

speaker: author (devotional voice)
question: The conduct-septad remembered in the heart; the abode entered again; the discussion itself known — the hymn names its own close.
premises: The conduct-septad remembered in the heart by those whose other thoughts are dissolved.
Those enter the supreme abode again, and know the ultimate-thing-discussion.
The hymn names itself at the close.
inference: Remembered, entered, known — the hymn closes by naming itself.
uncertainties: Whether 'bhairavīya' is vocative address or genitive is unresolved.

speaker: Poet (maṅgala)
question: What is enjoined first?
premises: Enjoy peace always; with few words stop the chatter-course.
By its stopping-way ask what-how-this-who-I; don't doubt.
inference: The maṅgala injunction: peace, brevity, cessation as the gate; self-questioning without doubt.

speaker: Poet (dialectician)
question: What follows from the condition?
premises: If reality reached only by first rejecting non-reality, that is non-reality.
If non-reality is then reality itself — not reality, not such.
inference: Conditional refutation: mediated attainment collapses into its means; identity-claims about tattva fail both ways.

speaker: Poet (dialectician)
question: What shines?
premises: Whatever shines, not apart from shining; even difference claimed to shine does not shine in shining.
Abandon the grasping of breaking-ways; dream become dream-ness, mere play, no fright-maker.
inference: Non-difference of appearance and awareness: difference is not a second shining; grasping modes of breaking is abandoned.

speaker: Poet (dialectician)
question: What distinguishes from the inert?
premises: Resolving first on knowledge-action-measuring; whatever declared — what distinction from the inert.
Quivering, even the inert — is it not the nondual-awareness-abode.
inference: The inert quivers too: if it moves, what excludes it from the advaya-awareness-abode — beginningless, eternal, ungraspable, true-formed?

speaker: Poet (dialectician)
question: What if the illuminator is smeared?
premises: Illuminator of beings, if smeared by them — what is that to you.
If it shines, hail: unbroken greatness even there; if not, it is not — both ways ever-awake.
inference: Smearing cannot touch the illuminator: shining or not, greatness stays unbroken; both alternatives dissolve into ever-awake being.

speaker: Poet (gaze-practice)
question: Where should sight go?
premises: Send sight outward past the target-path; Bhairava-mimicry would be mere fraud.
No outside for nondual-waking sky; no inside for spaceless-unfolding-abode.
inference: Gaze sent past every target: inner and outer denied alike; imitating the state without being it is fraud.

speaker: Poet (desire-practice)
question: What is watched?
premises: When desire-spread-delusion rises, whatever flashes — watch just that.
In beginning, middle, ends, if there — shining, shining, all dissolves into you.
inference: Desire-practice: attend the flash itself at every phase; the watcher shining, all melts into you.

speaker: Poet (cosmologist)
question: Where does delusion rest?
premises: Delusion dense with suffering, conjecture, piling thought, error-chains, mirage-city-like.
If it does not shine in consciousness-sky, ground of dual-nondual-thought — where else the highest rest.
inference: Delusion has no other seat: failing to appear in consciousness-sky, no highest rest stands anywhere — even for the many-selfed.

speaker: Poet (three-state survey)
question: What of dream and waking?
premises: In dream the unreal itself is road; in deep sleep manifestation; beyond that, conditionless consciousness-sky — what grasp.
In waking, earth-firm heap even for a moment — then by knowing, past that, this apart: what refutation.
inference: Three-state survey ending in unrefutability: dream-road, sleep-show, waking-heap — each passed beyond by knowing, none refuted from inside.
uncertainties: Print variants v9 (saraṇa/sauṣupta vs maraṇa/sauṣumna) recorded; edition followed.

speaker: Poet (identity)
question: Who shines?
premises: Whatever lights in me, in highest sky room-found — shine in me in eternal glory undistinguished.
I am He: unfeigned, eternal, unbroken-measured, infinite, true, free — foe-pair darkness dispelled.
inference: All lights mine, shining in me without division: so'ham as infinite true free dispeller of the foe-pair's darkness.

speaker: Poet (permission)
question: What may play?
premises: Let time reckon, creator create, love churn under command.
Play-pomp sky-abiding as it were, self-drawn lines, body-abiding; in delusion's evil — what unseen.
inference: Cosmic permission: time, creation, desire all let be; the play abides in body; nothing unseen even in delusion's evil.

speaker: Poet (devourer)
question: Whom to devour?
premises: Who here sir whom I devour; whom suddenly slay.
Whom — supreme-waking-abode-devouring-frenzied — I drink.
inference: Triple devouring of otherness: devour, slay, drink — incorporation of all as supreme-waking-abode.
uncertainties: Print variant ko'tra bhor ahaṃ (I devour/slay/drink) vs edition ko'tra bhor yaṃ (whom); edition kept, variant noted.

speaker: Ramyadeva (seal)
question: How does it close?
premises: Becoming-born fear shattered, jackals scared; on wisdom's yoke, even of wise, for once what awakening.
From beyond-contentment upsurge in dense-forest wandering, Hari Rāmyadeva made non-difference-elephant trumpet.
inference: Seal by another's hand: Ramyadeva's verse — fear routed, awakening once, non-difference trumpeted.

speaker: Śiṣya (student, invoking)
question: To whom take refuge?
premises: Supreme, beyond-abiding, depthless, beginningless, one, cave-entered manifoldly.
All-abode, all-moving-unmoving-abiding: to You, Śambhu, to refuge I resort.
inference: Refuge taken in all-abiding Śambhu.

speaker: Śiṣya (student, asking)
question: Who asks, and of whom?
premises: Womb-to-death sorrow-wheel-whirled, the student asked the blessed Lord, the support: the supreme truth.
inference: Whirled student asks support-Lord the truth.

speaker: Guru (answering)
question: How answered?
premises: By support-verses the teacher addressed him, its essence.
Abhinavagupta tells, by Śiva-teaching-view-yoga.
inference: Teacher answers in verses; Abhinavagupta retells Śaiva-wise.

speaker: Guru (teaching)
question: What fourfold, by whom manifested?
premises: By own-power-glory-weight, this egg-fourfold in division.
Power, Māyā, nature, earth — thus manifested by the Lord.
inference: Fourfold manifested by Lord's power-weight.

speaker: Guru (teaching)
question: Who enjoys therein?
premises: Therein within, this universe: varied body-faculty-world continuum.
And therein the enjoyer, embodied: Śiva indeed, fettered-state-taken.
inference: Enjoyer embodied is Śiva fettered.

speaker: Guru (teaching)
question: How contain all forms?
premises: As stainless crystal assumes various sorts' form, so the Lord too: god-man-beast-plant form-ness.
inference: Lord contains all forms as crystal takes colors.

speaker: Guru (teaching)
question: How move and rest with the world?
premises: As water moves, moves; moon-disc in stillness, stillness goes.
So this self, great Lord, in body-faculty-world mass.
inference: Self moves/rests with world-mass as moon with water.

speaker: Guru (teaching)
question: How perceived everywhere?
premises: As invisible Rahu, moon-disc-abiding, shines, so the all-going self, by object-resorting, in mind-mirror.
inference: Everywhere-self perceived in mind-mirror by objects.

speaker: Guru (teaching)
question: How manifest in purified mind?
premises: As in dirt-free mirror face shines, so this self, in Śiva-grace-pure mind-principle, shines light-formed.
inference: Grace-pure mind mirrors light-formed self.

speaker: Guru (teaching)
question: What replete with powers?
premises: Light-formed, complete, in own self from resting, great-bliss, by will-knowing-acting filled, endless-power-complete.
inference: Rest-replete self filled with will-knowing-acting powers.

speaker: Guru (teaching)
question: What shines, thought-free?
premises: All-thought-free, pure, peaceful, dissolution-rise-free: which supreme principle, therein shines the thirty-six-selfed world.
inference: Thought-free principle shines 36-fold world.

speaker: Guru (teaching)
question: How shine undivided yet divided?
premises: In mirror-orb, as city-village-etc.-varied, undivided, shines; in division indeed, mutually, from mirror too.
inference: Undivided shines divided, mutually mirrored.

speaker: Guru (teaching)
question: Whence divided shining?
premises: From purest supreme Bhairava-knowing, so, though division-void: mutually, thence too, divided shines this world.
inference: Divisionless source, divided shining.

Objection 2 (veiling by likeness) → reply: the veil destroys itself; never veiled; life-breath cannot throttle.
inference: Effecthood means shining-dependence; likeness cannot veil — the world His life-breath.
uncertainties: Kāryatva replaced by shining-talk — noted, not imported beyond text.

etad = the aforementioned doership/Vimarśa (Pradipaka comparison); tirodhīyate print (Pradipaka's nirodh- variant noted).

speaker: Poet (moonlight)
question: What is asked at moonrise?
premises: Ever-risen, blessed, all-auspicious, Śiva-giving, in-Śiva's-heart-dwelling, O Śivā.
Moonlight opening night-lotus for the worshipping mind: twice-born, make my going in heaven supreme.
inference: Moonlight-prayer for the twice-born mind: opened like night-lotus, made to go supreme in heaven.

speaker: Poet (litany)
question: Who alone is supreme?
premises: Be gracious, all-auspicious Śivā, Śiva's beloved.
Umā, Ramā, Sarasvatī — you alone are the supreme goddess.
inference: Direct address collapsing names into one: Umā, Ramā, Sarasvatī — you alone the supreme goddess.

speaker: Poet (fierce forms)
question: To whom surrender?
premises: O mother, Ambikā, formless, nameless, Umā, Raudrī, Vāmā, Mahālakṣmī, Māyā.
Supreme goddess sporting the five acts, auspicious Bhairavī, glorious — I surrender to you.
inference: Fierce-form litany gathered into surrender: formless, nameless, many-named — five-act-sporting Bhairavī.

speaker: Poet (throbbing)
question: How is she meditated?
premises: Māyā, Vidyā, Mātṛkā, Mālinī — you throb in every body as awareness-spark-self.
How shall I meditate you self-flashing? I meditate you as inward-resounding speech.
inference: Throbbing-in-every-body as the meditation object: self-flashing answered by inward-resounding speech.
uncertainties: Print reads mālini (kept); reference books cite mānini — Tantraloka 15.333 supports mālinī; single surface, no live fork.

speaker: Poet (body-churn)
question: Whom does Māyā plunge?
premises: In the skin-blood-flesh-fat-marrow-bone-bodied, ever-deluded body.
Māyā, you plunge knowing-and-unknowing folk who know not your greatness.
inference: The body catalogued as delusion's house; knowing and unknowing alike plunged for not knowing her greatness.

speaker: Poet (set-up gods)
question: What of set-up gods?
premises: Gods set up in metal-drawn images — seeing them, 'hā hā alas' say the unfulfilled.
For body-dwellers proud with body-I-ness — what delusion does Māyā not birth.
inference: Installed images leave seers unfulfilled: body-I-ness breeds every delusion.

speaker: Poet (protection)
question: What protects from falling?
premises: From delusion-play-arisen voided-intellect, body-and-all I-ness-born all.
Protect from falling, supreme goddess, self-awareness-formed through effort.
inference: Protection-begging from the all born of delusion-play: effort-born self-awareness as the guard against falling.

speaker: Poet (wonder)
question: How is power beheld?
premises: Terrible-natured, most terrible, non-terrible; higher-and-lower-called, neither lower nor higher.
Manifold-formed Śiva's power — seeing it, abiding in wonder.
inference: Beholding the manifold power — terrible and not — ends in wonder-abiding, not doctrine.

speaker: Poet (no-insistence)
question: What insistence remains?
premises: Dwelling mid the rays of higher-and-lower.
No insistence of mine on being-nonbeing-being-nonbeing judgments.
inference: Mid-ray dwelling dissolves insistence: no grip on any being-nonbeing judgment.

speaker: Poet (both remembered)
question: What is remembered?
premises: Your unsurpassed form flashes, and the other world-made one, O mother.
Remembering both — to the good, fear-giving, boon-giving, supreme goddess.
inference: Both forms remembered together: unsurpassed and world-made — to the good, fear and boon from one goddess.

speaker: Poet (five acts)
question: What is asked of the five-act lady?
premises: Lady of the five acts, supreme-knowing-formed Pārvatī, be gracious.
Lift the fallen beast-fettered one; soothe the child with cool glances.
inference: Double petition: lift the fallen fettered one; soothe the child — cool glances for heat.

speaker: Poet (seal)
question: Who utters these?
premises: Having bowed to perfected gurus, gods, goddess, then yogins.
By Abhinavagupta these fifteen verses uttered.
inference: Lineage-bow then authorship claim: perfected ones first, then the fifteen verses as Abhinavagupta's uttering.

speaker: Teacher (enumerating)
question: What is the Śākta doctrine?
premises: Thirteen named members: place, entry, form, mark, sign, raising, awakening, wheel-rest, stage-arrival, final state, rest, transformation, return.
The whole set is one supreme esoteric doctrine (vijñāna, sdv), not thirteen separate techniques.
Every Trika treatise carries it by Śambhu's own indication — lineage authority closes the list.
inference: The thirteen-member Śākta doctrine is complete and Trika-scriptural, revealed by Śambhu himself.

speaker: Teacher (enumerating)
question: What completes the thirteen?
premises: Second list-half: stage-arrival, final state, rest, transformation, return.
Verse-closing ca members bind vv1-2 into one thirteenfold sentence.
Nothing outside the thirteen belongs to the doctrine.
inference: The ascent continues through rest, transformation, and return — the list is a closed thirteen.

speaker: Teacher (authorizing)
question: Why supreme?
premises: Thirteenfold, Śākta, supreme knowledge: three predicates of one vijñāna.
Indicated in all Trika treatises — ubiquity across the corpus.
By Śambhu himself — no intermediary lineage dilutes the claim.
inference: The doctrine's authority is direct revelation, hence supreme.

speaker: Teacher (locating)
question: Where is the standing place?
premises: Two finger-measures triangulate the site: five below the navel, two above the member.
The midpoint is the kanda (bulb).
Two names: bulb-named and wheel-place — remembered (traditional) designation.
inference: The standing place is a measurable bodily site with two traditional names.

speaker: Teacher (instructing)
question: How is entry made?
premises: Means: restraint of in-breath and out-breath.
Act: mind cast right there (the kanda).
Sequence: conquer the wind-course fully, then lead it middle-going.
inference: Entry is breath restrained and mind cast exactly there, then led into the middle.

speaker: Teacher (showing)
question: What is the form?
premises: Entry concluded by traditional call (thus they call it).
Form promised now by the teacher's own voice (I will tell).
The seen object: triangle-pond-like, six-spoked, further firm.
inference: The form is a seen wheel: triangular, six-spoked, firm.

speaker: Teacher (showing)
question: What color is the form, and what is it?
premises: Color-image: like a pomegranate blossom, red by nature.
Declared third: rūpa's rank in the thirteen.
Consisting of contemplation: form is not a shape but a seeing (sdv: rūpa = contemplation).
inference: The bulb in form-vision is pomegranate-red, and form is the third member, consisting of contemplation.

speaker: Teacher (instructing)
question: When is the mark?
premises: Place mind in the middle until steadied there.
Obstruction left behind once the wind is worked.
Then the mark is pointed out — prescription, not description.
inference: The mark is assigned when mind is steadied there and the wind handled.

speaker: Teacher (showing)
question: What is the sign?
premises: Locus: standing in the middle of the bulb-wheel.
Nature: consisting of the unstruck (heart-sound).
Shape: joined with lines above and below, coiled like a serpent — kuṇḍalinī unnamed but present (sdv).
inference: The sign is the unstruck digit seen serpent-coiled in the bulb-wheel.

speaker: Teacher (praising)
question: How does she abide?
premises: Span: her abiding-state runs up-down (both channels).
Pair: sun and moon both (the two side-channels, sdv on v10).
Radiance: truly shining forth, thousand-sun-equal in splendor.
inference: She abides spanning up and down, sun and moon both, thousand-sun radiant.

speaker: Teacher (instructing)
question: How is the sign observed?
premises: Act: gaze at śakti with slight kumbhaka-mode.
Formula: this is the sign pointed out.
Sequence: from here, raising lies beyond.
inference: Gazing at her with light breath-hold defines the sign; raising begins beyond it.

speaker: Teacher (instructing)
question: How is she raised?
premises: Breath: practised exhale-mode carries the utterance.
Speech: mantra uttered on the exhale.
Vision: śakti contemplated as already awakened, staff-straight, Supreme Goddess.
inference: On the exhale utter mantra and contemplate her awakened, risen rod-straight as Supreme Goddess.

speaker: Teacher (sealing)
question: Where does raising end?
premises: Path: come from the base-middle, resorted to the suṣumnā.
Closure: raising is declared (sixth member complete).
Opening: awakening beyond thus (seventh member announced).
inference: Raising is declared in her path from base to channel; awakening lies beyond.

speaker: Teacher (climbing)
question: What does the piercing climb?
premises: Start: standing in the bulb, pierce the navel.
Middle: then the heart-dwelling grandsire.
Crown of the verse: throat-dwelling unfallen, Rudra face to face on the palate-surface.
inference: Awakening pierces upward station by station: navel, heart, throat, palate.

speaker: Teacher (arriving)
question: Where does the climb arrive?
premises: Brow: gone to the brow-middle — Īśa.
Door: at the brahma-door — Sadāśiva.
Flight: having awakened them, go swiftly to the unsupported Śiva state.
inference: The climb ends past brow and brahma-door in the unsupported Śiva state.

speaker: Teacher (resting)
question: What is wheel-rest like?
premises: Seal: this awakening is pointed out (seventh member complete).
Opening: wheel-resting then (eighth member announced).
Texture: natural petal, blazing, flowing, like the steady sky.
inference: Awakening closed; wheel-resting opens as natural, blazing, flowing, sky-steady.

speaker: Teacher (counting)
question: How many wheels?
premises: Names: nectar, crest, śakti-brahmā, drop-sound — members of the twelve.
Proclamation: thus proclaimed (received formula).
Attribution: tradition says (kila) — doctrine received, not invented.
inference: The wheel is twelvefold, proclaimed by tradition — nectar, crest, śakti-brahmā, drop-sound among its names.

speaker: Teacher (beholding)
question: Who rests in the wheels?
premises: Agency: she pierces, in order, wheel in wheel.
Tempo: each moment — no wheel skipped, no pause.
Fruit: she, the Great Goddess, should rest — wheel-rest supreme.
inference: She pierces in order and rests in every wheel, each moment — that rest is supreme.

speaker: Teacher (diagnosing)
question: What are the first signs?
premises: Heart trembles first — priority of the cardiac sign.
Palate-gate joins it; the head whirls.
The three together are the sign of sight-transmission (Timirodghāṭana term, sdv).
inference: The stage-signs begin in the body: trembling heart, palate gate, whirling head — the mark of sight-transmission.

speaker: Teacher (diagnosing)
question: How far does the whirling go?
premises: Scope: each single limb, down to limb-sub-limb joints.
Agent: the power of true vidyā (causative kept — she whirls, limbs are whirled).
Intensification: the heart swirls — trembling grown into churning.
inference: True knowledge whirls every limb in its joints; his heart swirls by that power.

speaker: Teacher (reassuring)
question: Must the changes be feared?
premises: Whatever changes the state makes in a being — total scope, doubled.
In those very changes: no fear (gerundive of fearlessness).
Ground: she plays — her play (krīḍā) is the fear's antidote, not its cause.
inference: No produced change is to be feared, because the Supreme Goddess plays.

speaker: Teacher (explaining)
question: Why do the changes multiply?
premises: State: intoxicated in nectar — her unmattā as method, not lapse.
Act: she makes many changes (the vidyā-power churning of v20 continued).
Material: what was done in many births under the triple stain.
inference: Drunk on nectar she multiplies changes — the residue of many births' stained doing.

speaker: Teacher (sealing)
question: What does the shaking accomplish?
premises: Liberation: shakes off the stained ones from the bond.
Agency: arisen from the supreme power (her own source).
Seal and pivot: stage-arrival proclaimed; final state thus told.
inference: She shakes the stained ones off from bondage — that is stage-arrival; the final state is told next.

speaker: Teacher (witnessing)
question: How does transmission feel?
premises: Onset signs: hair-thrill, tear-fall, yawn-onset, faltering speech within.
Deep signs: knot-bursting, divine thrill of touch.
Crown sign: drop-throbbings throb forth from the navel bulb (plural verb — many drops).
inference: At transmission the body testifies: thrill, tears, yawning, faltering voice, burst knots, throbbing drops from the navel bulb.
uncertainties: giro 'ntaḥ parsing ('of voices within') stays literal and uncertain — flagged, not smoothed.

speaker: Teacher (naming)
question: What was all that?
premises: The yat of v24 resolves here: the sign-list was the final state.
Declared (seal of the tenth member).
Pivot: rest (eleventh) is told next, conditioned on her awakening from the navel wheel.
inference: That is the final state declared; and rest is told next, when śakti wakes from the navel wheel.

speaker: Teacher (describing)
question: What sets in repose?
premises: Setting: the whole sense-village stands set outside (like the sun gone down).
Condition: when she, the supreme power, is well dissolved.
Locus: in the supreme state (dissolution, not sleep).
inference: In repose the whole outer sense-host sets; she lies well dissolved in the supreme state.

speaker: Teacher (defining)
question: What is rest?
premises: Negation: the subject finds nothing, no other object (ellipsis kept).
Union: in Śiva she is rested (passive — she is rested, not rests).
Naming: śakti-then is rest called (eleventh member sealed).
inference: The subject finds no other object; rested in Śiva is śakti — that is called rest.

speaker: Teacher (directing)
question: Where should the mind go?
premises: Locus: where the resting of śakti is, there the mind.
Act: should go to dissolution (optative prescription).
Fruit: the self is to be known in supreme-selfness — by the firm-souled (not by all).
inference: Where her resting is, there the mind should dissolve; the self is then known in supreme-selfness by the firm-souled.

speaker: Teacher (proclaiming)
question: What is transformation?
premises: Thesis: become Śiva, the self becomes (the work's pivot sentence).
Naming: that indeed is transformation (twelfth member sealed).
Overflow: always he rains divine nectar — and the nectar is creature-life.
inference: Become-Śiva is the self — that is transformation; and he rains divine nectar, creature-life.

speaker: Teacher (closing)
question: How does the doctrine close?
premises: Preparation: mind held there (gerund prior act).
Return: the goddess again should enter — she re-enters (āgamana enacted).
Closure: return proclaimed thus — fully thirteen (the v3 iti frame sealed).
inference: Mind held there, the goddess re-enters — that return, fully thirteen, closes the doctrine.

speaker: Utpaladeva (maṅgala, praise voice)
question: Under what auspice does the inquiry into relation open?
premises: With relation whose self is difference-and-non-difference (bhedābhedātmasaṃbandhasaha).
By whom all things are proved (sarvārthasādhitā); world-traffic (lokayātrā) is whose work (kṛtiḥ).
Him, Śiva, by own will (svecchayā), we praise (stumaḥ).
inference: Auspice: the Lord whose will works world-traffic proves all things with difference-and-non-difference-relation.
uncertainties: Feminine adjectives (saha, sādhitā) lack an overt noun — implied śakti, or absolute construction; held open.
svecchayā's agency (his will grounding relation vs our will in praising) held open; read as his (svātantrya seed).

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: What is relation, at the opening thesis?
premises: Dawning (unmiṣan) by his body (vapuṣā) made of relation (mayena) through being, difference, and the rest (bhāvabhedādi).
Conquering (jayati) though one (ekaḥ api): world-self (viśvātmā), light (prakāśaḥ), supreme Lord (parameśvaraḥ).
inference: Thesis stated: relation is the Lord's dawning body-form, not an accident of things.
uncertainties: kha reads bhedātma (whose self is difference) for bhedādi; main text followed, variant in NOTE.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: Are awaiting or dependence the relation of inert things?
premises: Awaiting (apekṣā) and dependence (pāratantryam) are no relation (na saṃbandhaḥ) for the two inert (jaḍātmanoḥ).
From impossibility (asaṃbhavāt): even where selfhood is won (ātmalābhe'pi), it is metaphor (upacāraḥ), not definition (lakṣaṇā).

Prose (p.2-3): the sprout 'awaits' the seed only by courtesy; awaiting, longing-for-the-other's-disposal, checking one's own will are will-determinations (saṃkalpaviśeṣa) — and will is consciousness's.
inference: First reduction fails: awaiting-language smuggles in the conscious relatum it should supply.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: Is 'residing-in-two' the relation?
premises: From stating self-obtaining of non-beings (asatām ātmalābhokteḥ), two-seatedness (dviṣṭhatā) is likewise abandoned (hīyate).
Form-fusion alone (rūpasaṃśleṣa eva) thus stands (sthitaḥ) as relation's sense (saṃbandhārthaḥ).
Prose (p.2): duality and mutual separateness would be relations too; 'residing-in-two' is said of the pair, not the relation — state it plainly in its own form.
inference: Second reduction fails: two-seatedness describes relata, never the relation; form-fusion stands in its place.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: Is uninterruptedness the relation — and what positively is it?
premises: Not uninterruptedness (na ānantaryam): it misses relation (asaṃbandhāt) — else it would hold of iron bars (ayaḥśalākayoḥ).
Prose (p.2): distant father-son lack it, adjacent iron bars (even pervading substances) have it — neither necessary nor sufficient.
Hence (tena): fusion (śleṣaḥ) of the many's form — that alone is one-selfhood (aikātmyam eva).
inference: Third reduction fails (with the iron-bars counterexample); positive thesis: relation is the many's form-fused one-selfhood.
uncertainties: asaṃbandhāt parsed as 'missing relation' (the mark fails to track); the grammar also allows 'from non-relation' — sense identical.

speaker: Opponent (Dharmakīrtian; SP 5cd per MacCracken/Jha)
question: Do the many need any unity at all?
premises: No barring (bādhaḥ) of the many even in one's unity (ekasyaikye'pi) — they say, as others do.
Things unmixed in themselves (amiśrāḥ svayaṃ bhāvāḥ) — thought (kalpanā) joins them (yojayati).
Witness: Dharmakīrti's Sambandhaparīkṣā v.5cd (Jha Philosophy of Relations; MacCracken) — the opponent's proof-text, quoted against him.
inference: The Buddhist position in its own voice: unmixed things, thought-joined; unity needs no seat.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: Is the joining only thought's fabrication?
premises: This (etat) is no mere thought (na kalpanāmātram): it cannot be warded off (avāraṇāt).
Like snake-error (sarpabhrānteḥ iva): its remedy fails (nivāraṇam) through clinging to a shining (ābhāsalagnatvāt).
Prose (p.5): even your side admits error clinging to thing-shining, unuprootable by refutation.
inference: Retorsion begins: unwardability proves the joining is no mere fabrication.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: What makes error stick?
premises: Clinging-to-shining (ābhāsalagnatvam) is not thing-resembling-shining (ābhāsasadṛśārthatā).
It is following-after-shining (ābhāsānusāritvaṃ): error is just that — an erred shining (bhrānta ābhāsa eva tat).
Prose (p.5): all errors concern resembling — but beyond resembling, errors hold by shining-clinging; else the silver-shell could not guide. Transaction-guiding seeming must follow the shining.
inference: Error sticks by following shining, not resembling things: seeming that guides must trail being.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: Can this justification be stated?
premises: Thus (ittham), in this very shining (asmin), such unity-seeing of the many (anekasyaikatādṛśi).
Its statable justification (vācyopapattiḥ) too is told (uktā), clearly (sphuṭam), in recognition's path (pratyabhijñānaye).
inference: Warrant claimed: the many-seen-as-one is statable inside the Pratyabhijñā, plainly.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: What of consciousness-bodied beings?
premises: Thus (evam), of beings (vastūnāṃ), of consciousness-bodied (cinmātravapuṣāṃ), of beings (satām).
Of Māyā-made-difference (māyānirmitabhedānām) even (api), unity (ekatvam) is not hard to effect (adurghaṭam).
inference: Even Māyā-differenced beings take unity without strain — for the consciousness-bodied.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: What is reflection's object for the worldly?
premises: Therein too (tatrāpi), what (yaḥ) is reflection's object (parāmarśaviṣayaḥ) for the worldly (laukikasya).
That (saḥ): of the knower (vedituḥ) whose pith (sāra) is difference (bheda) of non-difference-shining form (cidabhedaprathārūpa).
inference: The worldly one's reflection-object is the knower whose pith is difference in non-difference-shining form.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: Does blocked activity touch another thought?
premises: Activity (vyāpāraḥ) by this (anena) blocked (ruddhaḥ) — it (asau) should touch (spṛśet) no other thought (vikalpāntaram).
For on touching another thought (vikalpāntarasaṃsparśe) follows knower-difference (mātṛbhedaprasaṅgataḥ).
inference: One reflection's business touches no other thought, or knowers multiply.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: How do the many reach unity?
premises: Abiding in that-one-reflection (tadekāmarśavarti), by one-word-superimposition force (ekaśabdādhyāsavaśāt).
The many (anekaḥ) too would go (vrajet) to unity (ekatām) — as pot-cloth (ghaṭapaṭau) means (iti).
Prose: dvandva discussed at length — one reflection makes one word, one word one thing.
inference: Many reach oneness through one-word superimposition — 'pot-cloth'.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: Is there another relation?
premises: Thus (iti) there is (asti) also (tāvat?) another (anyaḥ): qualifier-qualified (viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyayoḥ) relation (saṃbandhaḥ).
For helping (upakārārthaḥ); it serves (upayujyate) for knowing (jñātum).
inference: A second relation stands: qualifier-qualified, for helping, serving knowledge.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: Is there twoness in manyness?
premises: Even in manyness (bahutve'pi), twoness (dvitvam) would be (bhavet).
From double-reflection birth (dvivimarśabhuvaḥ) — as the king's horses-chariots-men (rājño'śvarathapattayaḥ).
inference: Manyness still yields twoness, double-reflection-born — like the king's retinue.
uncertainties: dvivimarśabhuvaḥ case read ablative (from); genitive ('of') equivalent in sense — settled.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: How do the two reflections divide?
premises: Reflection (vimarśaḥ) 'of king' (rājñaḥ iti) is one (ekaḥ), facing own-generality (svasāmānyonmukhaḥ).
The other (paraḥ) — 'man' (puruṣaḥ iti), this (ayam), with master-generality-relation (svāmisāmānyasaṃbandhasahaḥ).
inference: 'King' faces own-generality; 'man' faces the master's — two reflections, one relation.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: How many thinkings?
premises: 'The king's man' (rājñaḥ puruṣaḥ iti) — this (eṣaḥ), after (paścāt), in relation's range (saṃbandhagocaraḥ).
Is to be thought (kalpyaḥ) by this (anena); or the former two to be thought (kalpyau) — those three (trayaḥ) in every way (sarvathā).
Prose: whole-thought after relation, or part-thoughts — three thinkings, all told.
inference: Three thinkings: whole after relation, or the former two — all told.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: Where does genitive-relation settle?
premises: Genitive-stated (ṣaṣṭhyādivācyaḥ) relation (saṃbandhaḥ), settled (viniviṣṭaḥ) in qualifier (viśeṣaṇe).
Reaching qualified-oneness (viśeṣyaikatvamāpanne), yet not abandoning (anujjhati) own form (svaṃ rūpam).
inference: Genitive-relation settles in the qualifier, reaches oneness, keeps own form.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: How do secondaries fit the chief?
premises: With one short (ekahānyā) — by the pure (śuddhena), by the chief (pradhānena) — mutual fitness (anyānyayogitā) would be (syāt) of the secondary (guṇasya).
As (yathā) the king's (rājñaḥ) man (puruṣaḥ), and (ca) the brahmin's.
Prose: chief/secondary pairs measured against king/man, brahmin/[kṣatriya?].
inference: Secondaries fit the chief one-short of pure: king's man, brahmin's.
uncertainties: ekahānyā obscure (with-one-short? one short of what?) — held open as printed; no smoothing.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: What other unity?
premises: So (tathā) by another (anyena) chief (pradhānena) — what (yā) other (anyā) unity (ekatā), or (vā) by still another (apareṇa).
Relation-called (saṃbandhākhyā) of the secondary (guṇasya) would be (syāt) — as (yathā) the king's horse (rājñaḥ aśvaḥ), man (puruṣaḥ).
inference: Other chiefs, other unities: secondary's relation-called — king's horse, man.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: What course is told?

speaker: Teacher (use announced)
question: What is set forth?
premises: athādhvano 'sya prakṛta upayogaḥ prakāśyate — now the use of this path, our present subject, is set forth: the āṇava arc's application chapter opens.
inference: The charter: application (upayoga) of the sixfold path.

speaker: Teacher (path rests in consciousness)
question: Where does the whole path rest?
premises: itthamadhvā samasto 'yaṃ yathā saṃvidi saṃsthitaḥ — this whole path as it rests in consciousness.
taddvārā śūnyadhīprāṇanāḍīcakratanuṣvatho — through that, in void, intellect, breath, channel-wheels, bodies too: consciousness as the door.
inference: Consciousness first; body-channels second, through it.

speaker: Teacher (outside too)
question: Where outside?
premises: bahiśca liṅgamūrtyagnisthaṇḍilādiṣu sarvataḥ — outside too, everywhere in liṅga, image, fire, altar and the rest.
tathā sthitaḥ samastaśca vyastaścaiṣa kramākramāt — whole and part-wise, in sequence and all-at-once: every mode of presence.
inference: The path saturates outer ritual objects in every mode.

speaker: Teacher (nondual contemplation)
question: How is oneness contemplated?
premises: āsaṃvittattvamābāhyaṃ yo 'yamadhvā vyavasthitaḥ — laid from consciousness-principle to the outer.
tatra tatrocitaṃ rūpaṃ svaṃ svātantryeṇa bhāsayet — at each level make one's own form shine, by own freedom, in fitting form (abhedabhāvanā).
inference: Abhedabhāvanā: shine as each level, freely, fittingly.

speaker: Teacher (no exclusion)
question: Why can nothing be excluded?
premises: sarvaṃ sarvatra rūpaṃ ca tasyāpi na na bhāsate — everything's form everywhere shines, even his (double negative).
nahyavaccheditāṃ kvāpi svapne 'pi viṣahāmahe — we cannot bear exclusion anywhere, even in dream: non-exclusion as first-person avowal.
inference: No cutting-off anywhere — exclusion is unbearable, even dreamed.

speaker: Teacher (behold the body)
question: What is the body seen as?
premises: evaṃ viśvādhvasaṃpūrṇaṃ kālavyāpāracitritam — filled with the universe-path, painted by time's activity.
deśakālamayaspandasadma dehaṃ vilokayet — the body as abode of space-time pulsation: behold it so.
inference: The body beheld as universe-path-filled, time-painted, pulse-housed.

speaker: Teacher (beheld, freed)
question: What happens to the so-beheld?
premises: tathā vilokyamāno 'sau viśvāntardevatāmayaḥ — so beheld, he is made of the deities within the universe.
dhyeyaḥ pūjyaśca tarpyaśca — to be meditated, worshipped, libated: the practitioner becomes the ritual object.
tadāviṣṭo vimucyate — entered then, one is freed.
inference: Beheld-as-deity-filled, he becomes worship's object — and is freed.

speaker: Teacher (oneness with the seen)
question: What practice with outer things?
premises: itthaṃ ghaṭaṃ paṭaṃ liṅgaṃ sthaṇḍilaṃ pustakaṃ jalam — pot, cloth, liṅga, altar, book, water.
yadvā kiṃcitkvacitpaśyettatra tanmayatāṃ vrajet — or whatever seen anywhere: reach identity-with-that there.
inference: Whatever seen, become it there: the tanmayatā rule.

speaker: Teacher (worship and meditation redefined)
question: What are worship and meditation now?
premises: tatrārpaṇaṃ hi vastūnāmabhedenārcanaṃ matam — offering of things is worship through non-difference.
tathā saṃpūrṇarūpatvānusaṃdhirdhyānamucyate — contemplation of full-formedness is called meditation.
inference: Arcana = non-dual offering; dhyāna = fullness-contemplation.

speaker: Teacher (firmness and mantra-vessel)
question: What do they yield?
premises: saṃpūrṇatvānusaṃdhānamakampaṃ dārḍhyamānayat — unshaking fullness-contemplation brings firmness.
tathāntarjalpayogena vimṛśañjapabhājanam — and through inner-mutter practice, reflecting, a mantra-vessel.
inference: Firmness from contemplation; mantra-fitness from inner muttering.
uncertainties: japabhājanam sense — flagged lightly.

speaker: Teacher (fire-rite giving)
question: What is given in the fire-rite?
premises: tatrārpitānāṃ bhāvānāṃ svakabhedavilāpanam — melting of self-difference of the offered beings.
kurvaṃstadraśmisadbhāvaṃ dadyāddhomakriyāparaḥ — their ray-rich being he bestows, devoted to the fire-rite.
inference: Melt self-difference, bestow ray-being: the inner homa.

speaker: Teacher (pure vow of equality)
question: What is the pure vow?
premises: tathaivaṃkurvataḥ sarvaṃ samabhāvena paśyataḥ — for one so acting, seeing all with equal eye.
niṣkampatā vrataṃ śuddhaṃ sāmyaṃ nandiśikhoditam — unwaveringness is the pure vow: evenness taught in the Nandiśikhā.
inference: Sāmya: unwavering equal-seeing as the pure vow (Nandiśikhā).

speaker: Teacher (samādhi of old)
question: What did the old gurus call complete?
premises: tathārcanajapadhyānahomavratavidhikramāt — through worship-japa-meditation-homa-vow-rule in sequence.
paripūrṇāṃ sthitiṃ prāhuḥ samādhiṃ guravaḥ purā — the complete state the old gurus called absorption.
inference: The ordered sixfold practice completed is samādhi.

speaker: Teacher (no rule on materials)
question: What governs ritual materials?
premises: atra pūjājapādyeṣu bahirantardvayasthitau — here in worship, japa and the rest, outward or inward.
dravyaughe na vidhiḥ ko 'pi na kāpi pratiṣiddhatā — no rule at all about materials, nor any prohibition: radical freedom of means.
inference: Materials: neither enjoined nor prohibited.

speaker: Teacher (sacrifice arises)
question: What of set rites?
premises: kalpanāśuddhisaṃdhyādernopayogo 'tra kaścana — no use here for visualization, purification, twilight-rites.
uktaṃ śrītrikasūtre ca jāyate yajanaṃ prati — and the Trika Sūtra says sacrifice arises toward the rite (occasion summons it).
inference: Set rites unused; sacrifice arises from occasion (Trika Sūtra).
uncertainties: yajanaṃ prati compression — flagged.

speaker: Teacher (consciousness decides)
question: Who decides rule and enjoyment?
premises: avidhijño vidhijñaścetyevamādi suvistaram — not-knowing-rule, knowing-rule, 'thus' and so on at length (positions listed, not judged).
yadā yathā yena yatra svā samvittiḥ prasīdati — when, as, by which, where one's own consciousness is gracious: grace as the only criterion.
inference: Consciousness's grace decides — not rule-knowledge.

speaker: Teacher (all employed)
question: What follows grace?
premises: tadā tathā tena tatra tattadbhogyaṃ vidhiśca saḥ — then, so, by that, there: each enjoyable, and that is the rule.
laukikālaukikaṃ sarvaṃ tenātra viniyojayet — all, worldly and unworldly, employ here by that (grace).
inference: Grace converts every enjoyable into rule; employ all.

speaker: Teacher (tremor reduced)
question: What of tremor in steadiness?
premises: niṣkampatve sakampastu kampaṃ nirhrāsayedbalāt — in steadiness: the trembler should forcibly diminish tremor.
yathā yenābhyupāyena kramādakramato 'pi vā — as, by whatever means, in sequence or all-at-once: kampahrāsa by any means.
inference: Tremor diminished by force, by any means, sequential or sudden.

speaker: Teacher (doubt melts, goddesses fed)
question: How does doubt end?
premises: vicikitsā galatyantastathāsau yatnavānbhavet — doubt melts within; so he should strive.
dhīkarmākṣagatā devīrniṣiddhaireva tarpayet — the goddesses in mind, rite, senses — with forbidden things indeed libate (Kaula substance).
inference: Doubt melts; striving libates the sense-goddesses even with forbidden substances.

speaker: Teacher (hero-vow and doubt's nature)
question: What vow, and what is doubt?
premises: vīravrataṃ cābhinandediti bhargaśikhāvacaḥ — and the hero-vow salute — thus the Bhargaśikhā word.
tathāhi śaṅkā mālinyaṃ glāniḥ saṃkoca ityadaḥ — for doubt is impurity, weariness, contraction: doubt diagnosed threefold.
inference: Hero-vow saluted; doubt = impurity-weariness-contraction.

speaker: Teacher (prison and purity)
question: What binds, and what is pure?
premises: saṃsārakārāgārāntaḥ sthūlasthūṇāghaṭāyate — inside the world-prison it forges gross-post shackles.
mantrā varṇasvabhāvā ye — mantras are letter-natured (no impurity possible).
dravyaṃ yatpāñcabhautikam — substance is five-elemented (no impurity possible).
inference: Doubt shackles; mantra and substance cannot be impure by nature.
uncertainties: denominative ghaṭāyate — flagged lightly.

speaker: Teacher (no mixture)
question: Where is impurity, then?
premises: yaccidātma prāṇijātaṃ — the breathing kind, consciousness-selfed.
tatra kaḥ saṃkaraḥ katham — where is mixture there, how?
saṃkarābhāvataḥ keyaṃ śaṅkā tasyāmapi sphuṭam — with mixture absent, what is this doubt — even hers clearly baseless.
inference: No mixture anywhere in the conscious living: doubt has no object.
uncertainties: tasyām api scope — flagged lightly.

speaker: Teacher (disregard dissolves)
question: What dissolves doubt?
premises: na śaṅketa — one should not doubt (the prescription).
tathā śaṅkā vilīyetāvahelayā — thus doubt dissolves through disregard.
śrīsarvācāravīrālīniśācarakramādiṣu — in the Sarvācāra, Vīrālī, Niśācara, Krama and the rest (the stocked canon).
