speaker: Teacher (vikalpa-sattarka-sakti doctrine)
question: What is the fierce argument about purity-rules?
premises: sarve hi heya eva upādeyabhūmirūpaṃ viṣṇutaḥ prabhṛti śivāntam — all see Viṣṇu-to-Siva as to-be-rejected ground-form.
tac ca mithyādarśanam avaśyatyājyam anuttarayogibhir — that false-view necessarily abandoned by unsurpassable-yogins.
tadartham eva vidyādhipateḥ anubhavastotre mahān saṃrambhaḥ — hence the knowledge-Lord's great fervour in hymn-of-experience.
yathā yathā bhavati tathaiva ācaret — as it becomes, so let him practise.
na tu bhakṣyābhakṣyaśuddhyaśuddhyādivivecanayā vastudharmojjhitayā kalpanāmātrasārayā svātmā khedanīyaḥ — not by purity-discriminations tormenting self by fancy-essence.
na hi śuddhiḥ vastuno rūpaṃ nīlatvavat anyatra — purity is not a thing-form like blueness elsewhere.
dānasyeva dīkṣitatve codanātaḥ — like gift's command in initiation.
codanāntare 'pi tulyam ... na śivacodanāyā eva bādhakatvaṃ — other-commands equal; Siva's-command alone obstructs.
yuktisiddhaṃ sarvajñānottarādyanantāgamasiddham ca — established by reason and endless scripture; we will say.
inference: Purity-rules are command-relative (codanā-vaśa), not thing-intrinsic; mithyā-darśana of heya/upādeya is what must go — the anubhava-stotra's fervour targets exactly this.

speaker: Teacher (vikalpa-sattarka-sakti doctrine)
question: Do Vedic and other śāstra-restraints bind here?
premises: tasmāt vaidikāt prabhṛti pārameśvarasiddhāntatantrakulocchuṣmādiśāstrokto 'pi — from Vedic through Pārameśvara/tantra/clan/Ucchuṣma scriptures.
yo niyamo vidhiḥ vā niṣedhaḥ vā — whatever restraint, injunction, prohibition.
so 'tra yāvad akiṃcitkara eva — here it is of no effect whatsoever.
iti siddham — established.
inference: Radical scope: all hetero-scriptural restraint is akiṃcitkara within this system — only śiva-codanā binds.

speaker: Teacher (vikalpa-sattarka-sakti doctrine)
question: Where does the authority point?
premises: tathaiva ca uktaṃ śrīpūrvādau — likewise said in Śrīpūrva-and-rest.
vitatya tantrālokāt anveṣyam — spread, from Tantrāloka to be sought.
inference: Forward/backward pointer: cross-search Tantrāloka for the full spread of this claim.

speaker: Teacher (dhyāna-uccāra-varṇa doctrine)
question: When does vikalpa itself become the upāya?
premises: yadā vikalpaḥ svayam eva saṃskāram ātmani kartuṃ prabhavati — when concept can itself impress the self.
upāyāntaranirapekṣatayā — independent of other means.
pāśavavyāpārāt pracutaḥ, śuddhavidyānugraheṇa parameśaśaktirūpatām āpannaḥ — fallen from bonded activity, by pure-knowledge grace attaining Lord-power-form.
upāyatayā avalambyamānaḥ śāktaṃ jñānam āvirbhāvayati — relied on as means, it brings forth śākta knowledge.
inference: Self-powered vikalpa = the śākta upāya: no external instrument, power-form as the means itself.

speaker: Teacher (dhyāna-uccāra-varṇa doctrine)
question: Where is this settled?
premises: tad etac ca nirṇītam anantara eva āhnike — settled in the very next ahnika.
inference: Cross-reference only: the proof lives ahead, not here.

speaker: Teacher (dhyāna-uccāra-varṇa doctrine)
question: What happens when vikalpa depends on another means?
premises: yadā tu upāyāntaram asau svasaṃskārārtham vikalpo 'pekṣate — when it depends on another means for own impression.
buddhiprāṇadehaghaṭādikān parimitarūpān upāyatvena gṛhṇan — taking mind/breath/body/pot as limited means.
aṇutvaṃ prāpta āṇavaṃ jñānam āvirbhāvayati — reaching subtlety, it brings forth āṇava knowledge.
buddhiḥ dhyānātmikā, prāṇaḥ sthūlaḥ sūkṣmaś ca, dehaḥ saṃniveśaviśeṣātmā, ghaṭādayaḥ bāhyāḥ — the means typed: meditation-mind, gross/subtle breath, arranged body, external pots.
inference: Instrument-dependent vikalpa = the āṇava upāya: each means limited-form, each typed by its sound (varṇa/karaṇa/ghaṭa).

speaker: Teacher (dhyāna-uccāra-varṇa doctrine)
question: What is the dhyāna taught here?
premises: svaprakāśaṃ sarvatattvāntarbhūtaṃ paraṃ tattvam — the self-luminous supreme tattva in all tattvas.
nijahṛdayabodhe dhyātvā — meditated in own-heart-knowing.
pramātṛpramāṇaprameyarūpasya vahnyarkasomatritayasya saṃghaṭṭaṃ dhyāyet — union of knower-instrument-known, fire-sun-moon triad.
yāvat asau mahābhairavāgniḥ dhyānavātasamiddhākāraḥ sampadyate — until great-Bhairava-fire, meditation-wind-fanned.
cakrātmanaḥ suṣiradvāreṇa niḥsṛtasya bāhye grāhyātmani viśrāntaṃ cintayet — the wheel-emergent rests in external graspable-self.
somarūpatayā sṛṣṭi, arkarūpatayā sthiti, saṃhāravahnirūpatayā vilāpa, anuttarātmatām āpāditaṃ dhyāyet — four-fillings: moon-creation, sun-preservation, fire-dissolution, anuttara-selfhood.
inference: The dhyāna is triadic-union plus four-stage cosmic filling — meditation ends where anuttara-selfhood is caused.

speaker: Teacher (dhyāna-uccāra-varṇa doctrine)
question: What does the wheel become?
premises: evaṃ tac cakraṃ samastabāhyavastvabhedaparipūrṇaṃ sampadyate — complete with all external-thing divisions.
inference: Completion criterion: the wheel holds every bāhya-vastu-bheda.

speaker: Teacher (dhyāna-uccāra-varṇa doctrine)
question: What is meditated with that wheel?
premises: tato vāsanāśeṣān api bhāvān tena cakreṇa itthaṃ kṛtān dhyāyet — residual habit-states, made thus, with that wheel.
inference: Vāsanā-cleanup rides the same cakra: residue-states included, not excluded.

speaker: Teacher (dhyāna-uccāra-varṇa doctrine)
question: What does the unceasing meditator gain at once?
premises: anavarataṃ dhyāyinaḥ svasaṃvinmātraparamārthān sṛṣṭisthitisaṃhāraprabandhān — own-consciousness-merely-real series of creation-preservation-dissolution.
sṛṣṭyādisvātantryaparamārthatvaṃ ca svasaṃvido niścinvataḥ — determining creation-autonomy-supremacy from own consciousness.
sadya eva bhairavībhāvaḥ — at once Bhairava-state.
inference: Bhairava-bhāva is immediate (sadya), not gradual — the reward of niścaya on saṃvid grounds.

speaker: Teacher (dhyāna-uccāra-varṇa doctrine)
question: What does practice yield?
premises: abhyāsāt tu sarvepsitasiddhyādayo 'pi — by practice, all desired attainments and rest.
inference: Siddhis ride abhyāsa — subordinate, listed without elaboration.

speaker: Teacher (dhyāna-uccāra-varṇa doctrine)
question: What triad is placed antaḥ?
premises: svaprakāśaṃ samastātmatattvaṃ mātrādikaṃ trayam — self-luminous all-self-tattva, measure-and-rest triad.
inference: The triad = svaprakāśa + samastātma-tattva + mātrādi: the content of inward placement.

speaker: Teacher (dhyāna-uccāra-varṇa doctrine)
question: Where does the meditator stand?
premises: antaḥkṛtya sthitaṃ dhyāyed dhṛdayānandadhāmani — having entered, standing, meditate in heart-bliss-abode.
inference: The locus is dhṛdaya-ānanda-dhāman: entry, stance, meditation in one clause.

speaker: Teacher (dhyāna-uccāra-varṇa doctrine)
question: What is that object?
premises: tad dvādaśamahāśaktiraśmicakreśvaraṃ vibhum — the twelve-great-power-ray-wheel-Lord, all-pervading.
inference: The heart-object = dvādaśa-mahā-śakti-cakra-īśa, vibhu.

speaker: Teacher (dhyāna-uccāra-varṇa doctrine)
question: How is it seen outside?
premises: vyomabhir niḥsarad bāhye dhyāyet sṛṣṭyādibhāvakam — emerging by ethers outside, meditate it bearing creation-states.
inference: Vyomadhāra carries the cakra outward as sṛṣṭy-ādi-bhāva-kam.

speaker: Teacher (dhyāna-uccāra-varṇa doctrine)
question: What mandala is placed in self?
premises: tad grastasarvabāhyāntarbhāvamaṇḍalam ātmani — that swallowing all outer-inner being mandala, in self.
inference: Placement reverses the outward flow: the grasta-maṇḍala rests in ātman.

speaker: Teacher (dhyāna-uccāra-varṇa doctrine)
question: What does the yogin thereby become?
premises: viśrāmyan bhāvayed yogī syād evam ātmanaḥ prathā — resting, contemplating, the yogin becomes the spread of self.
inference: The result is prathā of ātman: rest-then-contemplate, identity-as-spread.

speaker: Teacher (dhyāna-uccāra-varṇa doctrine)
question: What closes the dhyāna section?
premises: iti saṃgrahaślokāḥ — these are the summary-verses.
inference: Colophon: the preceding four (u9-14) are saṃgraha-ślokas in verse form.

speaker: Teacher (dhyāna-uccāra-varṇa doctrine)
question: What section ends here?
premises: iti dhyānam — thus meditation.
inference: Section boundary: dhyāna-āhnika closes.

speaker: Teacher (dhyāna-uccāra-varṇa doctrine)
question: What is the prāṇa-uccāra sequence?
premises: prāṇam uccicārayiṣuḥ pūrvam hṛdaya eva śūnye viśrāmyati — first rests in heart-emptiness.
tato bāhye prāṇodayāt — then outside from breath-arising.
tato 'pi bāhyaṃ prati apānacandrāpūraṇena sarvātmatāṃ paśyati — then toward external by apāna-moon-filling, seeing all-selfness.
tataḥ anyanirākāṅkṣo bhavati — then desiring no other.
tataḥ samānodayāt saṃghaṭṭaviśrāntim anubhavati — from samāna-arising, union-rest.
tata udānavahnyudaye mātṛmeyādikalanāṃ grasate — from udāna-fire, the measure-measured construction.
inference: Six-stage articulation: hṛdaya-śūnya → prāṇodaya → apāna-candra → anya-nirākāṅkṣā → samāna-saṃghaṭṭa → udāna-kalanā.

speaker: Teacher (dhyāna-uccāra-varṇa doctrine)
question: What flashes at vyāna?
premises: tadgrāsakavahnipraśame vyānodaye sarvāvacchedavandhyaḥ sphurati — at swallowing-fire pacification, vyāna-arising, devoid of all limitation, it flashes.
inference: Vyāna = the unbounded flash (sarvāvaccheda-vandhya), seventh moment of the sequence.

speaker: Teacher (dhyāna-uccāra-varṇa doctrine)
question: What six bliss-levels are taught?
premises: śūnyāt prabhṛti vyānāntam — from emptiness to vyāna.
nijānandaḥ nirānandaḥ parānandaḥ brahmānandaḥ mahānandaḥ cidānanda iti ṣaṭ ānandabhūmayaḥ — six levels named.
yāsām ekaḥ anusaṃdhātā udayāstamayavihīnaḥ antarviśrāntiparamārtharūpo jagadānandaḥ — one connector without arising-setting, inner-rest-truth-form: world-bliss.
inference: Six bhūmis plus a seventh (jagad-ānanda) that unites them as the connector beyond rise-and-set.

speaker: Teacher (dhyāna-uccāra-varṇa doctrine)
question: What is attained in the uccāra-bhūmis?
premises: etāsu uccārabhūmiṣu pratyekaṃ dvyādiśaḥ sarvaśo vā viśramya — resting each two-wise or wholly in articulation-levels.
anyat taddehaprāṇādivyatiriktaṃ viśrāntitattvam āsādayati — attains rest-tattva apart from body-breath.
inference: Rest-position determines attainment: viśrānti-tattva, distinct from body-prāṇa, is the uccāra-bhūmi prize.

speaker: Teacher (dhyāna-uccāra-varṇa doctrine)
question: What secret is kept in mind, and how many states per rest?
premises: tad eva sṛṣṭisaṃhārabījoccāraṇarahasyam anusaṃdadhat vikalpaṃ saṃskuryāt — keep the creation-dissolution-seed-articulation secret, impress the concept.
āsu ca viśrāntiṣu pratyekaṃ pañca avasthā bhavanti praveśatāratamyāt — in rests, five states each, by depth-of-entry.
inference: The bīja-rahasya governs uccāra; each viśrānti carries five avasthās scaled by entry-depth.

speaker: Teacher (dhyāna-uccāra-varṇa doctrine)
question: What are those states in the first rest?
premises: prāg ānandaḥ pūrṇatāṃśasparśāt — first bliss, from fullness-portion contact.
tata udbhavaḥ kṣaṇaṃ niḥśarīratāyāṃ rūḍheḥ — then arising, a moment, in embodimentlessness of the accustomed.
tataḥ kampaḥ svabalākrāntau dehatādātmyaśaithilyāt — then tremor, self-power-overpowering, loosening body-identity.
tato nidrā bahirmukhatvavilayāt — then sleep, from dissolution of outwardness.
inference: Four named states here (ānanda, udbhava, kampa, nidrā) — the fifth (ghūrṇi) arrives in the next verse.

speaker: Teacher (dhyāna-uccāra-varṇa doctrine)
question: What is the fifth state?
premises: ittham anātmani ātmabhāve līne — non-self-being dissolved in self-being.
svātmanaḥ sarvamayatvāt ātmani anātmabhāvo vilīyate — from all-pervasiveness, the non-self dissolves in self.
ato ghūrṇiḥ mahāvyāptyudayāt — therefore whirling, from arising of great-pervasion.
inference: Ghūrṇi completes the pañca-avasthā: dissolution-of-non-self into sarvamaya ātman.

speaker: Teacher (dhyāna-uccāra-varṇa doctrine)
question: What levels are these?
premises: tā etā jāgradādibhūmayaḥ turyātītāntāḥ — these are waking-and-rest levels, beyond-fourth-to-limit.
inference: The five states span jāgrad to turyātīta: the full bhūmi-range.

speaker: Teacher (dhyāna-uccāra-varṇa doctrine)
question: Where do these levels occur?
premises: etāś ca bhūmayaḥ trikoṇakandahṛttālūrdhvakuṇḍalinīcakrapraveśe bhavanti — they occur in entry of triangle-root-heart-pace-upward-kuṇḍalinī-wheel.
inference: Locative map: the bhūmis live at the kuṇḍalinī-cakra entry-points named in the compound.

speaker: Teacher (dhyāna-uccāra-varṇa doctrine)
question: What is the triad of liṅgas in uccāra-rest?
premises: uccāraviśrāntau yat paraṃ spandanaṃ galitāśeṣavedyaṃ — supreme pulsation, dissolved-rest-knowable.
yac ca unmiṣad vedyaṃ — dawning knowable.
yac ca unmiṣitavedyaṃ — already-dawned knowable.
tat eva liṅgam iti vakṣyāmaḥ svāvasare — that triad of marks we will say at the proper time.
inference: Three liṅgas: para-spandana (past-dissolved), unmiṣat (present-dawning), unmiṣita (already-dawned) — deferred exposition.

speaker: Teacher (dhyāna-uccāra-varṇa doctrine)
question: What is the supreme liṅga here?
premises: paraṃ cātra liṅgaṃ yoginīhṛdayam — the supreme mark here: yogini-heart.
inference: Yoginī-hṛdaya = para-liṅga of the uccāra system.

speaker: Teacher (dhyāna-uccāra-varṇa doctrine)
question: What is the primary spanda-rūpatā?
premises: mukhyā spandanarūpatā saṃkocavikāsātmatayā — primary pulsation-form, contraction-expansion-natured.
yāmalarūpatodayena — by pair-form arising.
visargakalāviśrāntilābhāt — from gaining visarga-portion-rest.
ity alam — enough.
inference: Spanda = saṃkoca-vikāsa as yāmala-pair, reaching visarga-kalā; the section stops here (alam).

speaker: Teacher (dhyāna-uccāra-varṇa doctrine)
question: What kind of entry is this?
premises: aprakāśaḥ atra anupraveśaḥ — non-luminous: here entry.
inference: This anupraveśa is aprakāśa: entry without manifestation — a marked distinction.

speaker: Teacher (dhyāna-uccāra-varṇa doctrine)
question: What is the order of completion?
premises: pūrvam svabodhe — first in own-knowing.
tadanu prameye viśramya — then resting in the knowable.
meyaṃ paripūrayeta — let him complete the knowable.
inference: svabodha → prameya-viśrānti → meya-paripūraṇa: knowing first, object completed last.

speaker: Teacher (dhyāna-uccāra-varṇa doctrine)
question: What happens at completion?
premises: pūrṇe 'tra viśrāmyati mātṛmeyavibhāgam — in the complete, here he rests: the measurer-measured distinction.
āśv eva sa saṃhareta — quickly let him withdraw.
inference: Rest at pūrṇa holds the mātṛ-meya-bheda; withdrawal is swift (āśu) — no lingering.

speaker: Teacher (dhyāna-uccāra-varṇa doctrine)
question: What are the six means-levels?
premises: vyāptyātha viśrāmyati — having pervaded, then he rests.
tā imāḥ syuḥ śūnyena sākaṃ ṣaḍupāyabhūmyaḥ — those would be with emptiness: the six means-levels.
inference: Ṣaḍ-upāya-bhūmis stand with śūnya: pervasion-rest is their condition.

speaker: Teacher (dhyāna-uccāra-varṇa doctrine)
question: What is prāṇa's position among the levels?
premises: prāṇādayo vyānanapaścimās — breath-and-rest are not-after-vyāna.
tallīnaś ca jāgrat prabhṛti prapañcaḥ — dissolved-in-it: waking-from-beginning manifestation.
inference: Prāṇa-ādis follow vyāna and are dissolved in it — the manifest series (jāgrat onward) rides that order.

speaker: Teacher (dhyāna-uccāra-varṇa doctrine)
question: What grows for the abhyāsa-niṣṭha?
premises: abhyāsaniṣṭho 'tra tu sṛṣṭisaṃhṛdvimarśadhāmany acireṇa rohet — established-in-practice here, in creation-dissolution-contemplation-abode, grows before long.
inference: Abhyāsa-niṣṭha grows (rohati) in the vimarśa-dhāman — growth, not acquisition.

speaker: Teacher (dhyāna-uccāra-varṇa doctrine)
question: What closes this inner section?
premises: iti āntaraślokāḥ — these are the inner-verses.
inference: Colophon: u30-34 are āntara-ślokas.

speaker: Teacher (dhyāna-uccāra-varṇa doctrine)
question: What section ends?
premises: iti uccāraṇam — thus articulation.
inference: Section boundary: uccāraṇa closes (u17-36).

speaker: Teacher (dhyāna-uccāra-varṇa doctrine)
question: What is the varṇa-rahasya of this uccāra?
premises: asmin eva uccāre sphuran avyaktānukṛtiprāyo dhvaniḥ varṇaḥ — in this articulation flashes sound-letter, almost-imitation-of-unmanifest.
tasya sṛṣṭisaṃhārabīje mukhyaṃ rūpaṃ — its primary form in the creation-dissolution-seed.
tadabhyāsāt parasaṃvittilābhaḥ — from its practice, gain of supreme-consciousness.
kādau mānte sācke anacke vā — examples: kā, mā-end, sācke, anacke.
samayānapekṣitvāt paripūrṇaḥ — from disregard-of-convention, complete.
ekīkṛtahṛtkaṇṭhoṣṭho dvādaśāntadvayaṃ hṛdayaṃ ca ekīkuryāt — unified heart-throat-lips, twelve-end-pair and heart let him unify.
iti varṇarahasyam — letter-secret.
inference: The letter's dhvani is avyaktānukṛti-prāya; practice in the bīja gives parasaṃvitti; the method unifies hṛt-kaṇṭha-oṣṭha + dvāsaśānta-dvaya + hṛdaya — varṇa-rahasya.

speaker: Teacher (dhyāna-uccāra-varṇa doctrine)
question: What do some say about the varṇa?
premises: antaḥsparśadvimarśānantarasamudbhūtaṃ sitapītādyāntaraṃ varṇam — white-yellow-and-rest inner letter born after inner-touch-contemplation.
udbhāvyamānaṃ saṃvidam anubhāvayati — being manifested, consciousness causes to experience.
iti kecit — so some.
inference: A minority view (kecit): the inner varṇa manifests white/yellow etc. as saṃvid-experience — recorded, not adopted.

speaker: Teacher (dhyāna-uccāra-varṇa doctrine)
question: What conditions the spanda without vācya?
premises: vācyaviraheṇa saṃvitspandāt — from consciousness-pulsation in absence of expressible.
indvarkagatinirodhābhyām — by moon-sun-motion checks.
inference: Without expressible content, the spanda runs on indv-arka-gati-nirodha: two checked motions.

speaker: Teacher (dhyāna-uccāra-varṇa doctrine)
question: What completes the cid-bīja varṇa?
premises: yasya tu samasaṃpraveśāt — by equal entry of which.
pūrṇāṃ cidbījapiṇḍavarṇavidhau — complete in consciousness-seed-mass-letter-form.
inference: Equal entry (sama-saṃpraveśa) yields the pūrṇā cid-bīja-piṇḍa-varṇa-vidhā.

speaker: Teacher (dhyāna-uccāra-varṇa doctrine)
question: What closes the inner material?
premises: iti āntaraślokaḥ — this is the inner-verse.
inference: Colophon for the closing verse.

speaker: Teacher (dhyāna-uccāra-varṇa doctrine)
question: What section ends?
premises: iti varṇavidhiḥ — thus letter-rule.
inference: Section boundary: varṇa-vidhi closes (u37-42).

speaker: Teacher (dhyāna-uccāra-varṇa doctrine)
question: What comes next?
premises: karaṇaṃ tu mudrāprakāśane vakṣyāmaḥ — the operation of mudrā-revelation we will say.
inference: Forward reference: mudrā-prakāśana is the next topic — aṇava/mudrā operation.

speaker: Teacher (seat-fixing charter)
question: What is the seat, and what is time?
premises: sa eva sthānaprakalpanaśabdena uktaḥ — called by the seat-fixing word.
tatra tridhā sthānaṃ prāṇavāyuḥ śarīraṃ bāhyaṃ ca — three seats: breath, body, outer.
tatra prāṇe tāvat vidhiḥ — first the breath-method.
sarvaḥ asau vakṣyamāṇaḥ adhvā prāṇasthaḥ kalyate — the whole course to be stated is reckoned breath-resting.
tasya kramākramakalanaiva kālaḥ — its sequence/non-sequence counting alone is time.
sa ca parameśvara eva antarbhāti — it shines within the Lord alone.
tadbhāsanaṃ ca devasya kālī nāma śaktiḥ — its shining is the God's power Kālī.
bhedena tu tadābhāsanaṃ kramākramayoḥ prāṇavṛttiḥ — with division, its appearing is breath-movement.
inference: Charter: three seats; breath first; course reckoned in breath; time = counting; Kālī within, breath-movement without.

speaker: Teacher (consciousness to breath)
question: How does consciousness become breath?
premises: saṃvid eva hi prameyebhyo vibhaktaṃ rūpaṃ gṛhṇāti — consciousness takes an apart-form from objects.
ata eva ca avacchedayogāt vedyatāṃ yāntī nabhaḥ — bounded, going to knowability: the void.
tataḥ svātantryāt meye svīkārautsukyena nipatantī — by freedom falling on the object, eager to seize.
kriyāśaktipradhānā prāṇanārūpā jīvasvabhāvā — action-led, breathing-formed, living-natured.
pañcabhī rūpaiḥ dehaṃ yataḥ pūrayati tato 'sau cetana iva bhāti — filling the body with five forms, it shines as if conscious.
inference: Descent: consciousness → apart-form → void → seizing-fall → breathing → seeming-conscious body.

speaker: Teacher (course map)
question: How are the courses placed?
premises: tatra kriyā śaktau kālādhvā — in power, action is time-course.
prācyabhāge uttare tu mūrtivaicitryarūpo deśādhvā — east and north: varied-form place-course.
tatra varṇamantrapadādhvanaḥ kālādhvani sthitiḥ parasūkṣmasthūlarūpatvāt — letter-mantra-word courses stand in time-course, beyond-subtle-gross.
inference: Placement: action=time-course in power; varied place-course east/north; letter-courses stand in time.

speaker: Teacher (deferral)
question: Where is place-course detail?
premises: deśādhvasthitis tu tattvapurakalātmanā — place-standing as tattva-person-ray-natured.
iti bhaviṣyati svāvasare — will be in its own place.
inference: Place-course deferred to its own place.

speaker: Teacher (why breath first)
question: Why describe from the heart?
premises: tatra yady api dehe sabāhyābhyantaram otaprotarūpaḥ prāṇaḥ — though in the body, warp-and-woof, is breath.
tathāpi prasphuṭasaṃvedyaprayatnaḥ asau hṛdayāt prabhṛti — yet distinctly felt effort starts from the heart.
iti tata eva ayaṃ nirūpaṇīyaḥ — hence described from there alone.
inference: Felt effort starts at the heart; description starts there.

speaker: Teacher (breath drivers)
question: What moves breath?
premises: tatra prabhuśaktiḥ ātmaśaktiḥ yatna iti tritayaṃ prāṇeraṇe hetuḥ — lord-power, self-power, effort: triad cause of breath-driving.
guṇamukhyabhāvāt — through secondary-primary states.
inference: Triad of drivers in ranked states.

speaker: Teacher (breath measure)
question: How long is the breath-course?
premises: tatra hṛdayāt dvādaśāntāntaṃ svāṅgulaiḥ sarvasya ṣaṭtriṃśadaṅgulaḥ prāṇacāraḥ — heart to twelve-end's end: 36 fingers by own fingers.
nirgame praveśe ca svocitabalayatnadehatvāt sarvasya — out and in, each fitted.
inference: 36-finger course, self-measured, out and in.

speaker: Teacher (time completed)
question: How is all time in breath?
premises: tatra ghaṭikā tithiḥ māso varṣaṃ ca varṣasamūhātmā iti samastaḥ kālaḥ parisamāpyate — clock, lunar day, month, year, year-groups: all time completed.
tatra sapañcāṃśe aṅgule caṣaka iti sthityā ghaṭikodayaḥ — finger-and-a-fifth = caṣaka: ghaṭikā-rise.
ghaṭikā hi ṣaṣṭyā caṣakaiḥ tasmāt dvāsaptatyaṅgulā bhavati — 60 caṣakas = 72 fingers.
inference: Whole time completed in breath; caṣaka rule; 72-finger ghaṭikā.

speaker: Teacher (next topic)
question: What next?
premises: atha tithyudayaḥ — now lunar-day rise.
inference: Tithi section opened.

speaker: Teacher (tuṭi)
question: What is a tuṭi?
premises: sapādam aṅguladvayaṃ tuṭiḥ ucyate — 2¼ fingers called tuṭi.
tāsu catasṛṣu praharaḥ — four make a watch.
tuṭyardhaṃ tuṭyardhaṃ tatra saṃdhyā — half each end: twilight.
evaṃ nirgame dinaṃ praveśe rātriḥ iti tithyudayaḥ — out-breath day, in-breath night.
inference: Tuṭi measure; watch; twilight; day-night breathing.

speaker: Teacher (next topic)
question: What next?
premises: atha māsodayaḥ — now month rise.
inference: Month section opened.

speaker: Teacher (fortnight)
question: How is the fortnight built?
premises: tatra dinaṃ kṛṣṇapakṣaḥ rātriḥ śuklaḥ — day dark fortnight, night bright.
tatra pūrvaṃ tuṭyardham antyaṃ ca tuṭyardhaṃ viśrāntiḥ akālakalitāḥ — first and last half-tuṭi: untimed rest.
madhyās tu pañcadaśa tuṭaya eva tithayaḥ — middle fifteen alone: lunar days.
tatra prakāśo viśrāntiś ca iti ete eva dinaniśe — light and rest: just these are day-night.
inference: Untimed rests at ends; fifteen middle tuṭis are the days.

speaker: Teacher (day-night doctrine)
question: What are day and night?
premises: tatra vedyamayatāprakāśo dinaṃ — knowable-light is day.
vedyasya vicārayitari layo rātriḥ — knowable dissolved in the dissolver: night.
te ca prakāśaviśrāntī cirāciravaicitryāt anantabhede — light-rest through quick-slow variety in endless difference.
tatsāmye tu viṣuvat — in sameness: equinox.
inference: Day = knowable-light; night = dissolution; variety endless; sameness = equinox.

speaker: Teacher (waxing)
question: How does the moon fill?
premises: tatra kṛṣṇapakṣe prāṇārke apānacandra āpyāyikām ekām ekāṃ kalām arpayati — in dark fortnight, in breath-sun, in-breath-moon offers each fattening digit.
yāvat pañcadaśyāṃ tuṭau dvādaśāntasamīpe kṣīṇapṛthagbhūtakalāprasaraḥ candramāḥ prāṇārka eva līyate — by the fifteenth, near the twelve-end, the thinned moon dissolves into breath-sun.
inference: Fifteen digit-offerings; thinned moon dissolves at the end.

speaker: Teacher (joint)
question: What is pakṣasaṃdhi?
premises: tadanantaraṃ yat tuṭyardhaṃ sa pakṣasaṃdhiḥ — right after, the half-tuṭi: fortnight-joint.
inference: Half-tuṭi after the fifteenth = joint.

speaker: Teacher (joint halves)
question: How is the joint divided?
premises: tasya ca tuṭyardhasya prācyam ardham āmāvasyam dvitīyaṃ prātipadam — eastern half new-moon, second first-day.
inference: Joint halves: new-moon and first-day.

speaker: Teacher (eclipse)
question: What is the seizure?
premises: tatra prātipade tasmin bhāge yadā ... tithicchedāt viśati — on that first-day part, when from tithi-cutting it enters.
tadā tatra grahaṇam — then seizure.
tatra ca vedyarūpasomasahabhūto māyāpramātṛrāhuḥ — the Māyā-knower-Rāhu, co-born with the object-moon.
svabhāvatayā vilāpanāśaktaḥ kevalam ācchādanamātrasamarthaḥ — by nature unable to dissolve, merely covering-capable.
sūryagataṃ cāndram amṛtaṃ pibati — drinks the lunar nectar gone to the sun.
kāsaprayatnāvadhānādikṛtāt — from observance-effort.
inference: Eclipse doctrine: Rāhu covers but cannot dissolve; drinks the nectar.

speaker: Teacher (holy time)
question: Why is it holy?
premises: pramātṛpramāṇaprameyatritayāvibhāgakāritvāt sa puṇyaḥ kālaḥ pāralaukikaphalapradaḥ — making the triad non-divided: holy time, other-world-fruiting.
inference: Triad-non-division makes it holy.

speaker: Teacher (waning)
question: How does waning work?
premises: tataḥ praviśati prāṇe cidarka ekaikayā kalayā apānacandram āpūrayati — then in breath the awareness-sun fills the in-breath-moon digit by digit.
yāvat pañcadaśī tuṭiḥ pūrṇimā — until the fifteenth tuṭi: full moon.
tadanantaraṃ pakṣasaṃdhiḥ grahaṇaṃ ca iti prāgvat — then joint and seizure as before.
etat tu aihikaphalapradam iti māsodayaḥ — but this-world-fruiting: month rise.
inference: Waning as filling; same joint/seizure; this-world fruit.

speaker: Teacher (next topic)
question: What next?
premises: atha varṣodayaḥ — now year rise.
inference: Year section opened.

speaker: Teacher (northern course)
question: How is the northern course measured?
premises: tatra kṛṣṇapakṣa eva uttarāyaṇam — dark fortnight alone: northern course.
ṣaṭsu ṣaṭsu aṅguleṣu saṃkrāntiḥ makarāt mithunāntām — every six fingers a passage, Capricorn to Gemini's end.
inference: Six-finger passages, Capricorn to Gemini.

speaker: Teacher (southern course)
question: What happens coming in?
premises: tatra pratyaṅgulaṃ pañca tithayaḥ tatrāpi dinarātrivibhāgaḥ — per finger five days, with day-night division.

evaṃ praveśe dakṣiṇāyanaṃ garbhatvam udbhavecchā ... janmādivikāraṣaṭkaṃ ca iti kramāt makarādiṣu — coming in: southern course — womb-ness through birth-and-six-changes, in order among Capricorn and the rest.
inference: In-breath southern course with gestation-to-change series.

speaker: Teacher (worship fruit)
question: Does worship matter?
premises: tathaiva upāsā atra phalaṃ samucitaṃ karoti — just so worship here does fitting fruit.
inference: Worship does fitting fruit here.

speaker: Teacher (year lords)
question: Who rules the year?
premises: atra ca dakṣādyāḥ pitāmahāntā rudrāḥ śaktayaś ca dvādaśādhipataya iti varṣodayaḥ — Dakṣa to Grandfather, Rudras and powers: twelve lords.
inference: Twelve year-lords.

speaker: Teacher (great counts)
question: How do the counts scale?
premises: pratyaṅgulaṃ ṣaṣṭiḥ tithaya iti krameṇa saṃkrāntau varṣam — per finger sixty days: at passage a year.
anena krameṇa praveśanirgamayoḥ dvādaśābdodayaḥ — thus coming-going: twelve-year rise.
pratyaṅgulaṃ tithīnāṃ śatatrayaṃ sapañcāṃśe 'ṅgule varṣaṃ — per finger 300 days in finger-and-a-fifth: a year.
yatra prāk caṣakam uktam iti gaṇanayā saṃkrāntau pañca varṣāṇi — where caṣaka was said: by counting five years at passage.
anayā paripāṭyā ekasmin prāṇanirgamapraveśakāle ṣaṣṭyabdodayaḥ — in one out-in time: sixty-year rise.
atra ekaviṃśatisahasrāṇi ṣaṭ śatāni iti tithīnāṃ saṃkhyā — 21,600 the day-count.
inference: Sixty-day, twelve-year, sixty-year scales; 21,600 breaths.

speaker: Teacher (limit of inquiry)
question: How far examine?
premises: tāvatī eva ahorātre prāṇasaṃkhyā — that many alone the day-night breath-count.
iti na ṣaṣṭyabdodayāt adhikaṃ parīkṣyate ānantyāt — not beyond sixty-year rise examined, from endlessness.
inference: Inquiry stops at sixty-year rise; rest endless.

speaker: Teacher (cosmic scale)
question: How do divine years work?
premises: tatra mānuṣaṃ varṣaṃ devānāṃ tithiḥ — human year = gods' lunar day.
anena krameṇa divyāni dvādaśavarṣasahasrāṇi caturyugam — thus 12,000 divine years = four ages.
inference: Human year = divine day; 12,000 divine years = four ages.

speaker: Teacher (twilights)
question: What are the twilights?
premises: catvāri trīṇi dve ekam iti kṛtāt prabhṛti tāvadbhiḥ śataiḥ aṣṭau saṃdhyāḥ — 4,3,2,1 from kṛta on: by so many hundreds, eight twilights.
inference: Descending hundreds; eight twilights.

speaker: Teacher (Brahmā-day)
question: What happens on Brahmā's day?
premises: caturyugānām ekasaptatyā manvantaram — 71 four-ages = manu-period.
manvantaraiḥ caturdaśabhiḥ brāhmaṃ dinam — 14 = Brahmā's day.
brahmadinānte kālāgnidagdhe lokatraye ... sarve janā vegavad agnipreritā janaloke pralayākalībhūya tiṣṭhanti — at its end, worlds burnt/lulled, all stand as pralayākalas in people-world.
inference: Manu-periods; Brahmā's day; fire-dissolution stance.

speaker: Teacher (the awake)
question: Who plays on?
premises: prabuddhās tu kūṣmāṇḍahāṭakeśādyāḥ maholoke krīḍanti — awakened Kūṣmāṇḍa and the rest play in the great world.
inference: The awakened play on.

speaker: Teacher (dawn)
question: What after night?
premises: tato niśāsamāptau brāhmī sṛṣṭiḥ — then at night's end, Brahmā's emission.
inference: Night's end: Brahmā's emission.

speaker: Teacher (Brahmā-span)
question: How long is Brahmā?
premises: anena mānena varṣaśataṃ brahmāyuḥ — by this measure 100 years = Brahmā-lifespan.
inference: Hundred-year Brahmā-lifespan.

speaker: Teacher (Viṣṇu-span)
question: How long is Viṣṇu?
premises: tat viṣṇoḥ dinaṃ tāvatī ca rātriḥ — that Viṣṇu's day, that much night.
tasyāpi śatam āyuḥ — his too a hundred lifespan.
inference: A hundred Viṣṇu-years; day-night parity.

speaker: Teacher (Rudra-span)
question: What of Rudra?
premises: tat dinaṃ tadūrdhve rudralokaprabho rudrasya — that day; above that — Rudra-world-lord — Rudra's.
tāvatī rātriḥ prāgvat varṣaṃ tacchatam api ca avadhiḥ — that much night; year as before; that hundred too: the limit.
inference: Day above; night alike; hundred-year limit.
uncertainties: rudralokaprabho fork: vocative address vs nominative descriptor.

speaker: Teacher (Rudra's end)
question: What ends Rudra?
premises: tatra rudrasya tadavasitau śivatvagatiḥ — at Rudra's end, going to Śiva-ness.
rudrasya uktādhikāravadhiḥ — Rudra's stated office-limit.
brahmāṇḍadhārakāṇāṃ tat dinaṃ śatarudrāṇāṃ niśā — world-bearers' day; hundred Rudras' night.
tāvatī teṣām api ca śatam āyuḥ — that much; their too a hundred lifespan.
inference: Office-limit ends in Śiva-ness; hundred-Rudra scale.

speaker: Teacher (world-egg end)
question: What ends the world-egg?
premises: śatarudrakṣaye brahmāṇḍavināśaḥ — when a hundred Rudras end: world-egg destruction.
inference: Hundred-Rudra expiry = world-egg destruction.

speaker: Teacher (Rudra scale)
question: How far does the Rudra scale run?
premises: evaṃ jalatattvāt avyaktāntam etad eva krameṇa rudrāṇām āyuḥ — from water-principle to unmanifest: this in order the Rudras' lifespan.
inference: Water-to-unmanifest Rudra scale.

speaker: Teacher (ladder rule)
question: What is the ladder rule?
premises: pūrvasya āyur uttarasya dinam iti — the earlier's lifespan is the later's day.
inference: Fused-span rule: each lifespan = next one's day.

speaker: Teacher (officers)
question: Who stands in the unmanifest?
premises: tataś ca brahmā rudrāś ca abādyadhikāriṇaḥ avyakte tiṣṭhanti — Brahmā and Rudras, unobstructed officers, stand in the unmanifest.
inference: Unobstructed officers in the unmanifest.

speaker: Teacher (withdrawer)
question: Who withdraws?
premises: śrīkaṇṭhanāthaś ca tadā saṃhartā — Śrīkaṇṭha-lord then the withdrawer.
inference: Śrīkaṇṭha withdraws.

speaker: Teacher (interval)
question: What between dissolutions?
premises: eṣo 'vāntarapralayaḥ — this intermediate dissolution.
tatkṣaye sṛṣṭiḥ — on its ending, emission.
inference: Interval dissolution, then emission.

speaker: Teacher (other texts)
question: What of other scriptures?
premises: tatra śāstrāntaram uktā api sṛjyante — other scriptures, stated, too are emitted.
inference: Even others are emitted.
uncertainties: uktā fork: f.pl with implied emissions (verb decisive) vs scribal neuter.

speaker: Teacher (higher days)
question: How do higher days scale?
premises: yat tu śrīkaṇṭhanāthasya svam āyuḥ tat kañcukavāsināṃ rudrāṇāṃ dinaṃ — Śrīkaṇṭha's lifespan = sheath-dwellers' day.
tāvatī rajanī — that much night.
teṣāṃ yad āyuḥ tat gahaneśadinaṃ — their lifespan = Gahaneśa-day.
tāvatī eva kṣapā tasyāṃ ca samastam eva māyāyāṃ vilīyate — that much night; in her all dissolves in Māyā.
inference: Lifespan-to-day ladder up to Māyā-dissolution.

speaker: Teacher (re-emission)
question: What after Māyā?
premises: punaḥ gahaneśaḥ sṛjati — again Gahaneśa emits.
inference: Gahaneśa re-emits.

speaker: Teacher (Māyā-day)
question: How is Māyā-day told?
premises: evaṃ yaḥ avyaktakālaḥ taṃ daśabhiḥ parārdhaiḥ guṇayitvā māyādinaṃ kathayet — unmanifest-time times ten half-highests: tell Māyā-day.
tāvatī rātriḥ — that much night.
inference: Ten half-highest multiplication = Māyā-day.

speaker: Teacher (seal)
question: What is that?
premises: sa eva pralayaḥ — that alone is dissolution.
inference: Dissolution seal.

speaker: Teacher (Īśvara-day)
question: How is Īśvara-day?
premises: māyākālaḥ parārdhaśataguṇita aiśvaratattve dinam — Māyā-time times a hundred half-highests: a day in Īśvara-principle.
inference: Hundred half-highest multiplication = Īśvara-day.

speaker: Teacher (breath-quiet)
question: What where breath quiets?
premises: atra prāṇo jagat sṛjati tāvatī rātriḥ — here breath emits the world, that much night.
yatra prāṇapraśamaḥ prāṇe ca brahmabiladhāmni śānte 'pi yā saṃvit tatrāpy asti kramaḥ — where breath quiets, even in the quiet Brahman-cave, which consciousness: even there is sequence.
inference: Even in quiet, consciousness keeps sequence.

speaker: Teacher (great dissolution)
question: What is the great dissolution?
premises: aiśvare kāle parārdhaśataguṇite yā saṃkhyā tat sādāśivaṃ dinaṃ tāvatī niśā — in hundred-multiplied Īśvara-time, the number: Sadāśiva day, that much night.
sa eva mahāpralayaḥ — that alone great dissolution.
inference: Sadāśiva-number; great dissolution.

speaker: Teacher (ascent)
question: How does Sadāśiva dissolve?
premises: sadāśivaḥ svakālaparikṣaye bindvardhacandranirodhikām ākramya nāde līyate — when his time ends, ascending drop-half-moon-blocker, dissolves in resonance.
nādaḥ śaktitattve tat vyāpinyāṃ sā ca anāśrite — resonance in power-principle, that in the pervader, she in the Unsupported.
inference: Ascent ladder: drop → resonance → power → pervader → Unsupported.

speaker: Teacher (Unsupported-day)
question: How is Unsupported-day?
premises: śaktikālena parārdhakoṭiguṇitena anāśritadinam — by power-time times ten-million half-highests: Unsupported-day.
inference: Ten-million multiplication = Unsupported-day.

speaker: Teacher (Brahman)
question: What is Brahman?
premises: anāśritaḥ sāmanase pade yat tat sāmanasyaṃ sāmyaṃ tat brahma — the Unsupported in the like-minded station: which, that likeness, sameness; that is Brahman.
inference: Likeness-sameness = Brahman.
uncertainties: sāmanase sense obscure; still-place reading from station frame.

speaker: Teacher (wheel-whirl)
question: How does time turn?
premises: asmāt sāmanasyāt akalyāt kālāt nimeṣonmeṣamātratayā proktāśeṣakālaprasarapravilayacakrabhramodayaḥ — from likeness, from partless, from time, by winking measure: the stated wheel-whirl rise of all time's spread and re-dissolution.
inference: Wink-measured wheel-whirl of all time.

speaker: Teacher (number names)
question: How are numbers named?
premises: ekaṃ daśa śataṃ sahasram ayutaṃ lakṣaṃ niyutaṃ koṭiḥ arbudaṃ vṛndaṃ kharvaṃ nikharvaṃ padmaṃ śaṅkuḥ samudram antyaṃ madhyam parārdham iti — one to half-highest.
krameṇa daśaguṇitāni aṣṭādaśa iti gaṇitavidhiḥ — ten-multiplied in order, eighteen: counting-rule.
inference: Eighteen ten-multiplied names to parārdha.

speaker: Teacher (all in breath)
question: Where do all creations rest?
premises: evam asaṃkhyāḥ sṛṣṭipralayāḥ ekasmin mahāsṛṣṭirūpe prāṇe — countless emissions-dissolutions in one great-emission-formed breath.

so 'pi saṃvidi sā upādhau sa cinmātre cinmātrasyaiva ayaṃ spando yad ayaṃ kālayodo nāma — it in consciousness, she in adjunct, it in bare awareness: of bare awareness alone this pulse called time-rise.
inference: All in breath; breath in consciousness; time-rise = bare-awareness pulse.

speaker: Teacher (no contradiction)
question: Why no contradiction?
premises: tata eva svapnasaṃkalpādau vaicitryam asya na virodhāvaham — from that alone, in dream-fancy and the rest, its variety brings no contradiction.
inference: Dream-variety consistent with pulse-doctrine.

speaker: Teacher (apāna)
question: What of in-breath?
premises: evaṃ yathā prāṇe kālodayaḥ tathā apāne 'pi hṛdayāt mūlapīṭhaparyantam — as in out-breath time-rise, so in in-breath, heart to root-seat's end.
inference: Same rise in in-breath, heart to root-seat.

speaker: Teacher (six causes)
question: What are the six causes?
premises: yathā ca hṛtkaṇṭhatālulalāṭarandhradvādaśānteṣu brahmaviṣṇurudreśasadāśivānāśritākhyaṃ kāraṇaṣaṭkam tathaiva apāne 'pi — as in heart-to-twelve-ends the six Brahmā-to-Unsupported causes, so in in-breath.
hṛtkandānandasaṃkocavikāsadvādaśānteṣu bālyayauvanavārddhakyapunarbhavamuktyadhipataya ete — in heart-bulb-bliss-contraction-expansion-twelve-ends: childhood-to-release lords.
inference: Six causes above; six lords below.

speaker: Teacher (samāna)
question: What next?
premises: atha samāne kālodayaḥ — now in equal-breath time-rise.
inference: Samāna section opened.

speaker: Teacher (equal-breath)
question: How does samāna move?
premises: samāno hārdīṣu daśāsu nāḍīṣu saṃcaran samaste dehe sāmyena rasādīn vāhayati — moving in ten heart-channels, conveys juices evenly through the body.
tatra digaṣṭake saṃcaran taddikpaticeṣṭām iva pramātuḥ anukārayati — in the eight directions, imitates as it were the regents' doings.
inference: Ten channels, even juices; eight-direction regent-mime.

speaker: Teacher (vertical)
question: What of up-down?
premises: ūrdhvādhas tu saṃcaran tisṛṣu nāḍīṣu gatāgataṃ karoti — moving up and down, in three channels does going-coming.
inference: Three-channel vertical going-coming.

speaker: Teacher (equinox breath)
question: What on equinox-day?
premises: tatra viṣuvaddine bāhye prabhātakāle sapādāṃ ghaṭikāṃ madhyamārge vahati — on equinox-day, outside, at dawn, carries 1¼ ghaṭikās in the middle path.
inference: Equinox dawn middle-path measure.

speaker: Teacher (left-right)
question: How do passages alternate?
premises: tato navaśatāni prāṇavikṣepāṇām iti gaṇanayā bahiḥ sārdhaghaṭikādvayaṃ vāme dakṣiṇe vāme dakṣiṇe vāme iti pañca saṃkrāntayaḥ — 900 breath-castings; outside 2½ ghaṭikās left-right-left-right-left: five passages.
inference: 900 castings; alternating five passages.

speaker: Teacher (southern)
question: What at southern solstice?
premises: tataḥ saṃkrāntipañcake vṛtte pādonāsu caturdaśasu ghaṭikāsu atikrāntāsu — five-passage elapsed, in 13¾ passed ghaṭikās.
dakṣiṇaṃ śāradaṃ viṣuvanmadhyāhne nava prāṇaśatāni — southern autumnal: at equinox-midday nine breath-hundreds.
inference: Southern count at equinox-midday.

speaker: Teacher (night)
question: And at night?
premises: tato 'pi dakṣiṇe vāme ... pañca saṃkrāntipañcakaṃ pratyekaṃ navaśatāni ity evaṃ rātrāv api — right-left five-passage, 900 each; thus even at night.
inference: Night mirrors day.

speaker: Teacher (twelve)
question: How many passages?
premises: evaṃ viṣuvaddivase tadrātrau ca dvādaśa dvādaśa saṃkrāntayaḥ — on equinox-day and its night, twelve and twelve.
inference: Twelve by day, twelve by night.

speaker: Teacher (wax-wane)
question: What varies?
premises: tato dinavṛddhikṣayeṣu saṃkrāntivṛddhikṣayaḥ — in day wax-wane, passage wax-wane.
inference: Passages track day-length.

speaker: Teacher (two years)
question: How two years in one?
premises: evam ekasmin samānamaruti varṣadvayaṃ śvāsapraśvāsayogābhāvāt — in one equal-breath-wind two years, from absence of in-out-breath union.
inference: Union-absence doubles the year.

speaker: Teacher (same rule)
question: What of the rest?
premises: atrāpi dvādaśābdodayādi pūrvavat — even here twelve-year-rise and the rest as before.
inference: Same scales apply.

speaker: Teacher (up-breath)
question: What of udāna?
premises: udāne tu dvādaśāntāvadhiś cāraḥ spandamātrātmanaḥ kālasya — in up-breath the course is twelve-end-limited, of mere-pulse-natured time.
inference: Up-breath: twelve-end-limited pulse-time.

speaker: Teacher (same rule)
question: What rule?
premises: atrāpi pūrvavat vidhiḥ — even here as before the rule.
inference: Same rule.

speaker: Teacher (vyāna)
question: What of vyāna?
premises: vyāne tu vyāpakatvāt akrame 'pi sūkṣmocchalattāyogena kālodayaḥ — in pervading-breath, from pervasiveness, even in non-sequence, by subtle-surging-ness: time-rise.
inference: Pervasiveness lets non-sequence rise time.

speaker: Teacher (next topic)
question: What next?
premises: atha varṇodayaḥ — now letter rise.
inference: Letter section opened.

speaker: Teacher (letter rise)
question: How do letters rise?
premises: tatra ardhaprahare ardhaprahare vargodayo viṣuvati samaḥ — half-watch by half-watch class-rise is even at equinox.
varṇasya varṇasya dve śate ṣoḍaśādhike prāṇānām bahiḥ ṣaṭtriṃśat caṣakāṇi — per letter 216 breaths; outside 36 caṣakas.
iti udayaḥ ayam ayatnajo varṇodayaḥ — thus effortless-born letter-rise.
inference: 216 breaths per letter; effortless.

speaker: Teacher (mantra rise)
question: How does mantra rise?
premises: yatnajas tu mantrodayaḥ araghaṭṭaghaṭīyantravāhanavat — effort-born mantra-rise, like a water-wheel drawing.
ekānusaṃdhibalāt citraṃ mantrodayaṃ divāniśam anusaṃdadhat mantradevatayā saha tādātmyam eti — by single-attention force, joining wondrous mantra-rise day-night, gains identity with the mantra-deity.
inference: Water-wheel repetition; deity-identity.

speaker: Teacher (grāsa)
question: What is time-devouring?
premises: tatra sadodite prāṇacārasaṃkhyayaiva udayasaṃkhyā vyākhyātā — in the ever-arisen, rise-count explained by breath-count alone.
taddviguṇite tadardham ityādi krameṇa aṣṭottaraśate cakre dviśata udayaḥ — doubling, halving, in 108-wheel 200 rise.
iti krameṇa sthūlasūkṣme cārasvarūpe viśrāntasya prāṇacāre kṣīṇe kālagrāse vṛtte — in gross-subtle course-nature of the rested, breath thinned, time devoured come about.
sampūrṇām ekam evedaṃ saṃvedanaṃ citraśaktinirbharaṃ bhāsate — complete one just-this awareness, wonder-filled, shines.
inference: Count by breath alone; thinning; devouring; complete awareness shines.

speaker: Teacher (moment doctrine)
question: What is a moment?
premises: kālabheda eva saṃvedanabhedakaḥ na vedyabhedaḥ — time-difference alone divides awareness, not object-difference.
śikharasthajñānavat — like peak-abiding knowledge.
jñānasya yāvān avasthitikālaḥ sa eva kṣaṇaḥ — as much as knowing's abiding-time: that alone the moment.
prāṇodaye ca ekasmin ekam eva jñānam avaśyaṃ — in one breath-rise necessarily one knowing.
caitat anyathā vikalpajñānam ekaṃ na kiṃcit syāt — otherwise no single thought-knowing at all.
kramikaśabdārūṣitatvāt mātrāyā api kramikatvāt — since word-stained sequential, since even measure sequential.
inference: Moment = knowing's abiding-time; one breath, one knowing.

speaker: Citation (measure)
question: What is said?
premises: yad āha tasyādita udāttam ardhahrasvam iti — which says: raised, half-short.
inference: Measure-fragment cited.
uncertainties: tasyādita obscure; raised/half-short measure-sense kept.

speaker: Teacher (between pulses)
question: What between pulses?
premises: tasmāt spandāntaraṃ yāvat na uditaṃ tāvat ekam eva jñānam — until between-pulses has not arisen, so long one knowing alone.
inference: Between-pulse silence = one knowing.

speaker: Teacher (eighty-one)
question: What of eighty-one?
premises: ata eva ekāśīti padasmaraṇasamaye vividhadharmānupraveśamukhena — hence eighty-one, when remembering the word, through entering various natures.
eka eva asau parameśvaraviṣayo vikalpaḥ kālagrāse na avikalpātmā eva sampadyate — that one Lord-objected thought, when time is devoured, results as thought-free-natured alone.
inference: Eighty-onefold word-memory devoured into thought-freedom.
uncertainties: avikalpātmā ending obscure; thought-free sense secure.

speaker: Teacher (recognition)
question: What frees?
premises: evam akhilaṃ kālādhvānaṃ prāṇodaya eva paśyan — seeing the entire time-course in breath-rise alone.
sṛṣṭisaṃhārāṃś ca vicitrān niḥsaṃkhyān tatraiva ākalayan — noting countless emissions-dissolutions right there.
ātmana eva pārameśvaryaṃ pratyabhijānan mukta eva bhavati — recognizing lordship by self alone: freed.
inference: Seeing, noting, recognizing: freed.

speaker: Teacher (Bhairavī-being)
question: What is the close?
premises: saṃvidrūpasyātmanaḥ prāṇaśaktiṃ paśyan — seeing the awareness-formed self's breath-power.
rūpaṃ tatragaṃ cātikālam sākaṃ — form going there and beyond time together.
sṛṣṭisthemasaṃhāracakrair nityodyukto bhairavībhāvam eti — with emission-stay-dissolution wheels, ever-ready attains Bhairavī-being.
inference: Breath-power seen; beyond-time form; ever-ready Bhairavī-being.
uncertainties: cātikālam junction obscure; beyond-time sense from bhairavī-close.

speaker: Teacher (tattva-cosmology)
question: How does the whole path get fixed in consciousness?
premises: The whole — place-path-illumination-power-born — rested in consciousness: through its door, void, mind, prāṇa, nerve-circles, body up to liṅga-sthaṇḍila-image — the whole path firmly fixed.

Melting path→body→prāṇa→mind→void, in that consciousness all-filled-full-consciousness is attained: thirty-six-tattva-knower, seeing beyond-it Supreme-Siva-formed, world-made consciousness make-knowns the beyond-portion — some taking-as-supreme the māyā-womb-qualified, Viṣṇu-Brahmā-and-rest.
inference: The ladder-inversion (melting outer into inner) ends in full-consciousness; the 'some taking-as-supreme' clause marks who receives the beyond-portion; therefore prakriyā-jñāna-endowed is required.

speaker: Teacher (tattva-cosmology)
question: What is 'not prakriyāpara'?
premises: That is said: knowledge-endowed-with-prakriyā is not [mere] prakriyā.
inference: The formula from the prior chapter is restated: the knowledge that is prakriyā's end is not itself prakriyā.

speaker: Teacher (tattva-cosmology)
question: What is the earth-tattva?
premises: Therein earth-tattva, hundred-crore-extended, in-form-of-Brahma-cosmic-egg.
inference: Pṛthivī-tattva = śatakoṭi-extension as brahmāṇḍa-golaka-form — the cosmology's ground floor.

speaker: Teacher (tattva-cosmology)
question: What is inside it?
premises: Within: Kālāgni, hells, pātālas, earth, heaven up to Brahma-world — so.
inference: The inner inventory: fire-of-time, hells, nether-regions, earth, heaven through Brahma-world.

speaker: Teacher (tattva-cosmology)
question: What is outside?
premises: Outside the cosmic-egg, a hundred of Rudras.
inference: Śata-rudras outside — the egg's exterior population.

speaker: Teacher (tattva-cosmology)
question: How many eggs?
premises: Nor does a count of the cosmic-eggs exist.
inference: Anekānta-countlessness — no enumeration possible.

speaker: Teacher (tattva-cosmology)
question: What follows earth?
premises: Then water-tattva, tenfold from earth-tattva.
inference: Jala-tattva = 10× pṛthivī — the multiplication ladder begins.

speaker: Teacher (tattva-cosmology)
question: What follows water?
premises: Then, successively, tenfold up-to-ahaṃkāra-end.
inference: Successive tenfold growth from water to ahaṃkāra's end.

speaker: Teacher (tattva-cosmology)
question: How does the sequence expand?
premises: As water, fire, wind, sky — the five-substances-included one-eleven-wombed ahaṃkāra — and so.
inference: The tanmātra-pañcaka + aikādaśagarbha formula: each step embeds the prior five (or eleven) — recursive cosmology.

speaker: Teacher (tattva-cosmology)
question: What comes from ahaṃkāra?
premises: From ahaṃkāra, hundredfold buddhi-tattva.
inference: Buddhi-tattva = 100× ahaṃkāra.

speaker: Teacher (tattva-cosmology)
question: What comes from buddhi?
premises: Then thousandfold prakṛti-tattva — so much prakṛti-egg.
inference: Prakṛti = 1000×; the prakṛtyaṇḍa's measure stated.

speaker: Teacher (tattva-cosmology)
question: Is the prakṛti-egg countable?
premises: That, like the cosmic-egg, is countless.
inference: Like brahmāṇḍa: asaṃkhya — countlessness recurs at each egg.

speaker: Teacher (tattva-cosmology)
question: What comes from prakṛti?
premises: From prakṛti-tattva, puruṣa-tattva too, ten-thousandfold.
inference: Puruṣa = 10,000× prakṛti.

speaker: Teacher (tattva-cosmology)
question: What comes from puruṣas?
premises: From persons, niyati, lakh-fold.
inference: Niyati = 100,000× puruṣa.

speaker: Teacher (tattva-cosmology)
question: What comes from niyati?
premises: From niyati, successively ten-lakh-fold up to kalā-tattva-end.
inference: 1,000,000× successive to kalā-tattva's end.

speaker: Teacher (tattva-cosmology)
question: What constitutes niyati?
premises: As niyati, rāga, aśuddha-vidyā, kāla, kalā — and so.
inference: The five-member formula: niyati, rāga, aśuddha-vidyā, kāla, kalā — the avaraṇa set in miniature.

speaker: Teacher (tattva-cosmology)
question: What comes from kalā?
premises: From kalā-tattva, crorefold māyā — so much māyā-egg.
inference: Māyā = 10⁷×; the māyāṇḍa's measure.

speaker: Teacher (tattva-cosmology)
question: What comes from māyā?
premises: From māyā-tattva, śuddha-vidyā, ten-crore-multiplied.
inference: Śuddhavidyā = 10⁸× māyā.

speaker: Teacher (tattva-cosmology)
question: What comes from vidyā?
premises: From vidyā-tattva, īśvara-tattva, hundred-crore-fold.
inference: Īśvara = 10¹⁰× vidyā.

speaker: Teacher (tattva-cosmology)
question: What comes from īśvara?
premises: From īśvara-tattva, sādākhya, thousand-crore-fold.
inference: Sādākhya = 10¹¹× īśvara.

speaker: Teacher (tattva-cosmology)
question: What comes from sādākhya?
premises: From sādākhya, multiplied-by-group, śakti-tattva — so the śakti-egg.
inference: Śakti-tattva by vṛnda-guṇita — the śaktyaṇḍa closes the ladder's rise.

speaker: Teacher (tattva-cosmology)
question: Why is power all-pervading?
premises: That power pervading, by which the world-path inside-outside stands — hence all-pervading.
inference: Śakti's vyāpyatva: the world-path's inside-outside standing is power's pervasion — hence vyāpinī.

speaker: Teacher (tattva-cosmology)
question: How do the tattvas stand?
premises: Thus these tattvas, standing as mutual-coverings: the later pervader, the earlier pervaded — by that standing they stand.
inference: Āvaraṇa-hierarchy: each tattva covers the prior (pūrva) and is covered by the later (uttara) — vyāpaka/vyāpya sthiti.

speaker: Teacher (tattva-cosmology)
question: How far does the pervasion reach?
premises: Up to the all-power-tattva-end, the path is pervaded by Śiva-tattva.
inference: The adhvan runs to aśeṣa-śakti-tattva's end, pervaded by Śiva-tattva from without.

speaker: Teacher (tattva-cosmology)
question: What of Śiva-tattva?
premises: Śiva-tattva, further, is immeasurable, having-transcended-all-paths, pervading-all-paths.
inference: Śiva-tattva = aparimeya, sarvādhvottīrṇa, sarvādhvavyāpaka — the transcendent-pervader.

speaker: Teacher (tattva-cosmology)
question: Where do the bhuvanas dwell?
premises: These, dwelling in the gaps-between-tattvas, the bhuvanas — their lords stand in earth, here.
inference: Bhuvana-lords sit in tattva-gaps (antara-lava), established in pṛthivī here.

speaker: Teacher (tattva-cosmology)
question: What happens to those who die?
premises: In those abodes, those who die — their course there, they grant.
inference: The bhuvana-lords grant gati to the dying in their āyatanas.

speaker: Teacher (tattva-cosmology)
question: How is the cycle driven?
premises: And successively upward-downward they impel, by the dīkṣā-order.
inference: The lords prerayanti in ūrdhvordhva-krama per dīkṣā-krama — the cycle's motor.

speaker: Teacher (tattva definition)
question: What is a tattva?
premises: yad idaṃ vibhavātmakaṃ bhuvanajātam uktaṃ garbhīkṛtānantavicitrabhoktṛbhogyaṃ — this world-born glory-natured, wombing endless varied enjoyer-enjoyed.
tatra yad anugataṃ mahāprakāśarūpaṃ — what pervades as great-light-formed.
tat mahāsāmānyakalpaṃ paramaśivarūpam — that is like the great common, Supreme-Śiva-formed.
inference: Paramaśiva = what pervades the whole as great light.

speaker: Teacher (tattva defined)
question: What makes a category?
premises: yat tu katipayakatipayabhedānugataṃ rūpaṃ tat tattvam — what pervades only some differences: a category.
yathā pṛthivī nāma ... samastabrahmāṇḍānugatā — as earth, pervading all world-eggs from Kālāgni to Vīrabhadra.
inference: Partial pervasion defines tattva; earth the example.

speaker: Teacher (two causes)
question: How many cause-effect-nesses?
premises: tatra eṣāṃ tattvānāṃ kāryakāraṇabhāvo darśyate — cause-effect-ness shown.
sa ca dvividhaḥ — twofold.
inference: Twofold division announced.

speaker: Teacher (naming)
question: Which two?
premises: pāramārthikaḥ sṛṣṭeś ca — ultimate, and of emission.
inference: Ultimate and emanated named.
uncertainties: sṛṣṭeś genitive hanging; emission-side named.

speaker: Teacher (ultimate cause)
question: What is ultimate cause-effect?
premises: tatra pāramārthika etāvān kāryakāraṇabhāvaḥ — this much.

yad uta kartṛsvabhāvasya svatantrasya bhagavata evaṃvidhena śivādidharāntena vapuṣā svarūpabhinnena svarūpaviśrāntena ca prathanam — the free agent-Lord's showing-forth with Śiva-to-earth body, non-different in nature, resting in own nature.
inference: Ultimate = Lord's self-showing as the 36-level body.

speaker: Teacher (constructed cause)
question: What is constructed?
premises: kalpitas tu kāryakāraṇabhāvaḥ parameśecchayā niyatiprāṇayā nirmitaḥ — made by the Lord's will with necessity-breath.
sa ca yāvati yadā niyatapaurvāparyāvabhāsanaṃ — fixed before-after appearing.
saty api adhike svarūpānugatam etāvaty eva — even in the more, following own nature, only so far.
tena yogīcchāto 'pi aṅkuro bījād api svapnādau ghaṭāder apīti — hence sprout from seed, yogin's wish, dream, pots and the rest.
inference: Constructed = willed fixed order; sprout-from-seed/wish/dream its proof.

speaker: Teacher (agency kept)
question: Does agency lapse?
premises: tatrāpi ca parameśvarasya kartṛtvānapāya — even there no loss of the Lord's agency.
iti akalpito 'pi asau pāramārthikaḥ sthita eva — thus unconstructed too, the ultimate stands.
inference: Agency never lapses; ultimate stands even unconstructed.

speaker: Teacher (wall simile)
question: Why is the assemblage the cause?
premises: pāramārthike hi bhittisthānīye sthite rūpe sarvam idam ullikhyamānaṃ ghaṭate na anyathā — with ultimate wall-like standing form, all this drawn fits, not otherwise.
ata eva sāmagyā eva kāruṇatvaṃ yuktam — hence by the assemblage alone caused-ness fitting.
inference: Wall-standing ultimate grounds total-set causation.

speaker: Teacher (sāmagrī doctrine)
question: How does the total set work?
premises: sā hi samastabhāvasaṃdarbhamayī svatantrasaṃvedanamahimnā — made of all-being's weave, by free-awareness greatness.
tathā niyaratanijanijadeśakālabhāvarāśisvabhāvā — thus of fixed own place-time-thing-mass nature.
pratyekaṃ vastusvarūpaniṣpattisamaye tathābhūtā — each thing-nature completed, being thus.
tathābhūtāyā hi anyathābhāvo yathā yathā adhikībhavati — being-thus, being-otherwise as it increases.
tathā tathā kāryasyāpi vijātīyatvaṃ tāratamyena puṣyati — so the effect's other-kind-ness by degrees nourishes.
inference: Weave of fixed natures; deviation scales effect-difference.
uncertainties: niyata/nirata fork adjudicated (fixed; doctrine fit).

speaker: Teacher (potter proof)
question: Who makes the pot?
premises: ity evaṃ saṃvedanasvātantryasvabhāvaḥ parameśvara eva viśvabhāvaśarīro ghaṭāder nirmātā — the free-awareness Lord, world-thing-bodied, maker of pots.
kumbhakārasaṃvidas tato 'nadhikatvāt — potter-awareness nothing beyond.
kumbhakāraśarīrasya ca bhāvarāśimadhye nikṣepāt — potter's body placed amid things.
kathaṃ kumbhakāraśarīrasya kartṛtvābhimānaḥ — how the potter-body's maker-pride?
iti ced parameśvarakṛta evāsau ghaṭādivad bhaviṣyati — if asked: Lord-made like pots it will be.
inference: Lord, not potter, makes; potter-pride itself Lord-made.

speaker: Teacher (sāmagrī seal)
question: What confirms makership?
premises: tasmāt sāmagrīvādo 'pi viśvaśarīrasya saṃvedanasyaiva kartṛtāyām upodbalakaḥ — assemblage-doctrine strengthens awareness-alone's makership.
inference: Sāmagrī-vāda confirms awareness-makership.

speaker: Teacher (Meru test)
question: Where would no pot be?
premises: merau hi tatrasthe na bhavet tathāvidho ghaṭaḥ — on Meru, abiding there, no such pot would be.
inference: Meru counterfactual: conditions rule kinds.

speaker: Teacher (variety fits)
question: How do odd births fit?
premises: evaṃ kalpite 'smin kāryatve śāstreṣu tattvānāṃ kāryakāraṇabhāvaṃ prati yat bahuprakāratvaṃ tad api saṃgataṃ — in constructed caused-ness, the many-typed-ness fits.
gomayāt kīṭāt yogīcchāto mantrād auṣadhāt vṛścikodayavat — from dung worms, yogin's wish, mantra, herbs, like scorpion-arising.
inference: Dung-to-scorpion variety fits constructed causation.

speaker: Teacher (own system)
question: What now?
premises: tatra nijatantradṛśā taṃ kalpitaṃ darśayāmaḥ — by own-system view we show the constructed.
inference: Own-system exposition promised.

speaker: Teacher (five powers)
question: How does the Lord stand fivefold?
premises: tatra parameśvaraḥ pañcabhiḥ śaktibhiḥ nirbhara iti uktam — full with five powers.
sa svātantryāt śaktiṃ tāṃ tāṃ mukhyatayā prakaṭayan pañcadhā tiṣṭhati — manifesting power after power chiefly, stands fivefold.
inference: Five powers, fivefold stand by freedom.

speaker: Teacher (five principles)
question: How do the principles divide?
premises: citprādhānye śivatattvam — awareness-led: Śiva.
ānandaprādhānye śaktitattvam — bliss-led: power.
icchāprādhānye sadāśivatattvam — will-led: Sadāśiva.
icchāyā hi jñānakriyayoḥ sāmyarūpābhyupagamātmakatvāt — will is even-acceptance of knowing-doing.
jñānaśaktipradhānye īśvaratattvam — knowledge-led: Īśvara.
kriyāśaktipradhānye vidyātattvam — action-led: knowledge (-vidyā).
inference: Five principles by power-primacy; will as even-acceptance.

speaker: Teacher (pure path)
question: What is the pure path?
premises: atra ca tattveśvarāḥ śivaśaktisadāśiveśvarānantāḥ — lords Śiva through Ananta.
brahmeva nivṛttau — like Brahmā in withdrawal.
eṣāṃ sāmānyarūpāṇāṃ viśeṣā anugativiṣayāḥ pañca — five particulars with pervasion for object.
tadyathā śāmbhavāḥ śāktā mantramaheśvarā mantreśvarā mantrāḥ iti śuddhādhvā — Śāmbhavas to Mantras: pure path.
inference: Lords and five beings: the pure path.

speaker: Teacher (impure path)
question: Who makes the impure path?
premises: iyati sākṣāt śivaḥ kartā — so far directly Śiva maker.
aśuddhaṃ punar adhvānam anantāparanāmāghoreśaḥ sṛjati — impure path Aghoreśa-Ananta emits.
īśvarecchāvaśena prakṣubdhabhogalolikānām aṇūnāṃ bhogasiddhyartham — by Lord's will, for wavered atoms' enjoyment-perfection.
inference: Aghoreśa-Ananta emits the impure path for craving atoms.

speaker: Teacher (craving)
question: Is craving impurity?
premises: tatra loliko 'pūrṇam anyatārūpaḥ parispandaḥ akarmakam abhilāṣamātram eva bhaviṣyad avacchedayogyateti — waverer, incomplete, other-natured throbbing, mere longing, future fitness for bounding.
na malaḥ puṃsas tattvāntaram — not man's impurity nor another category.
inference: Craving = mere longing, not impurity, no new category.

speaker: Teacher (passion)
question: What is passion?
premises: rāgatattvaṃ tu karmāvacchinno 'bhilāṣaḥ — passion-principle is action-bounded longing.
inference: Passion = bounded longing.

speaker: Teacher (action)
question: What is action?
premises: karma tu tatra karmamātraṃ buddhidharmas tu rāgaḥ — action is mere action there; mind-nature is passion.
karmabhedacitra iti vibhāgo vakṣyate — varied by action-difference; distinction to be told.
inference: Action mere; passion mind-nature; distinction deferred.

speaker: Teacher (impurity defined)
question: What is impurity?
premises: so 'yaṃ malaḥ parameśvarasya svātmapracchādanecchātaḥ — this impurity: from the Lord's self-veiling wish.
nānyat kiṃcid vastv api — nothing else at all a thing.
ca tatparameśvarecchātmanaiva dharāder api vastutvāt — and by that Lord-wish-nature alone is earth-and-rest's thingness.
inference: Impurity = Lord's self-veiling wish; nothing else; things real only thus.

speaker: Teacher (kevalins)
question: How do kevalins differ?
premises: sa ca malo vijñānakevale vidyamāno dhvaṃsonmukha iti na svakāryaṃ karma āpyāyati — existing in knowledge-kevalin, facing destruction: does not fatten its effect-action.

pralayakevalasya tu jṛmbhamāṇa eva āsta iti malopodbalitaṃ karma saṃsāravaicitryabhoge nimittam — but yawning in dissolution-kevalin: impurity-strengthened action causes transmigration-variety-enjoyment.
inference: Knowledge-kevalin starves action; dissolution-kevalin fuels it.

speaker: Teacher (Aghoreśa emits)
question: Why does Aghoreśa emit?
premises: tadbhogavāsanānuviddhānām aṇūnāṃ bhogasiddhaye śrīmān aghoreśaḥ sṛjati — for enjoyment-pierced atoms' perfection, glorious Aghoreśa emits.
iti yuktam uktam — fittingly said.
malasya ca prakṣobha īśvarecchābalād eva — impurity's stirring by Lord-wish-force alone.
jaḍasya svataḥ kutracid api asāmarthyāt — of the inert by itself, anywhere, inability.
inference: Enjoyment-need + inert inability ground Aghoreśa's emission.

speaker: Teacher (atom and Māyā)
question: What is the atom, what Māyā?
premises: aṇur nāma kila cidacidrūpāvabhāsa eva — atom: mere conscious-unconscious shining.
tasya cidrūpam aiśvaryam eva — conscious form is lordliness.
acidrūpataiva malaḥ — unconscious-formedness alone impurity.
tasya ca sṛjataḥ parameśvarecchāmayaṃ — of it emitting, by Lord-wish-made.

tata eva ca nityaṃ srakṣyamāṇavastugatasya rūpasya jaḍatayābhāsayiṣyamāṇatvāj jaḍaṃ sakalakāryavyāpanādirūpatvāc ca vyāpakaṃ māyākhyaṃ tattvam upādānakāraṇaṃ — thence always: inert, all-effect-pervading Māyā-principle as material cause.
tadavabhāsakāriṇī ca parameśvarasya māyā nāma śaktis tato 'nyaiva — showing it forth: the Lord's Māyā-power, quite other.
inference: Atom = shining; impurity = unconscious side; Māyā-principle inert-pervading material cause; Māyā-power distinct.

speaker: Teacher (two-formedness)
question: What of kalā to earth?
premises: evaṃ kalāditattvānāṃ dharāntānām api dvairūpyaṃ nirūpyam — kalā-to-earth principles too two-formedness to be described.
inference: Two-formedness extended kalā-to-earth.

speaker: Teacher (proof cited)
question: What proof?
premises: atra ca dvairūpye pramāṇam apy āhur abhinavaguptaguravaḥ — here too proof have said Abhinavagupta's gurus.
inference: Guru saying cited as proof.

speaker: Teacher (proof verse)
question: What shines outside?
premises: yad saṃkalpe bhāti tat pṛthagbhūtaṃ bahir api asti sphuṭena vapuṣā ghaṭa iva — what shines in resolve exists outside too, with clear form, like a pot.
inference: Resolve-shining exists outside: pot proof.

speaker: Teacher (rule)
question: What rule?
premises: tathā ca māyākalādikhapuṣpāder api eṣaiva vartanī iti kevalānvayī hetuḥ — Māyā-kalā-sky-flowers too this very course: purely affirmative reason.
inference: Sky-flowers included; affirmative reason.

speaker: Teacher (siddhas)
question: Who is perfected?
premises: anena ca māyākalāprakṛtibuddhyādiviṣayaṃ sākṣātkārarūpaṃ jñānaṃ ye bhajante te 'pi siddhāḥ siddhā eva — who enjoy direct-realization knowing with Māyā-kalā-nature-mind and the rest as object: perfected indeed.
inference: Direct-realizers of Māyā-objects are perfected.

speaker: Teacher (world-birth)
question: Whence world-birth?
premises: evaṃ sthite māyātattvāt viśvaprasavaḥ — thus standing, from Māyā-principle world-birth.
inference: World-birth from Māyā-principle.

speaker: Teacher (order debate)
question: Sequential or not?
premises: sa ca yady api akramam eva tathāpi uktadṛśā kramo 'vabhāsate — though non-sequential, by the stated view sequence appears.
inference: Non-sequential yet appearing sequential.

speaker: Teacher (kalā groups)
question: How are kalā groups divided?
premises: so 'py ucyate tatra pratyātma kalādivargo bhinnaḥ — even that is told: per self the kalā-group divided.
inference: Per-self division of kalā groups.

speaker: Teacher (pure group)
question: Which group is pure?
premises: tatkāryasya kartṛtvopodbalanādeḥ pratyātmabhedena upalambhāt — from effect-makership-strengthening found by self-difference.
sa tu vargaḥ kadācit ekībhavet api īśvarecchayā sāmājikātmanām iva — but the group may become one by the Lord's wish, like social selves.

tatra sarvo 'yaṃ kalādivargaḥ śuddho yaḥ parameśvaraviṣayatayā tatsvarūpalābhānuguṇanijakāryakārī saṃsārapratidvaṃdvitvāt — all this kalā-group pure which, Lord-objected, does own work fit for gaining its nature, from world-opposition.
inference: Pure = Lord-objected work-doers; oneness possible by wish.

speaker: Teacher (how pure)
question: How become pure?
premises: sa ca parameśvaraśaktipātavaśāt tathā bhavati — by Lord-power-descent sway it becomes thus.
iti vakṣyāmas tatprakāśane — to be told in its showing.
inference: Power-descent makes pure; details deferred.

speaker: Teacher (impure)
question: What is impure?
premises: aśuddhas tu tadviparītaḥ — impure is opposite of that.
inference: Impure = opposite.

speaker: Teacher (kalā born)
question: How is kalā born?
premises: tatra māyātaḥ kalā jātā — from Māyā kalā born.
yā suptasthānīyam aṇuṃ kiṃcitkartṛtvena yunakti — which yokes the sleeping atom with slight makership.
sā ca ucchūnateva saṃsārabījasya — and as if swelling, of transmigration-seed.
māyāṇvor ubhayoḥ saṃyogāt utpannāpi māyāṃ vikaroti na avikāryam aṇum — arisen from Māyā-atom union, deforms Māyā, not the undeformable atom.
iti māyākāryatvam asyāḥ — thus her Māyā-effect-ness.
inference: Kalā yokes sleepers, swells, deforms Māyā not atoms.

speaker: Teacher (man-kalā)
question: What of man and kalā?
premises: evam anyonyaśleṣāt alakṣaṇīyāntaratvaṃ puṃskalayoḥ — from mutual clinging, indistinguishable inwardness of man and kalā.
inference: Clinging makes man-kalā indistinguishable.

speaker: Teacher (discriminations)
question: What discriminations free?
premises: māyāgarbhādhikāriṇas tu kasyacid īśvarasya prasādāt sarvakarmakṣaye māyāpuruṣaviveko bhavati — Māyā-womb officers, by some lord's grace, when all action ends: Māyā-man discrimination.
yena māyordhve vijñānākala āste — by which above Māyā sits the knowledge-kevalin.
na jātucit māyādhaḥ kalāpuṃviveko vā — never below Māyā kalā-man discrimination.
yena kalordhve tiṣṭhati — by which one stands above kalā.
inference: Grace-ending-action → Māyā-man then kalā-man discriminations, stationed above.

speaker: Teacher (nature-man)
question: What of nature-man?
premises: prakṛtipuruṣaviveko vā yena pradhānādho na saṃsaret — nature-man discrimination, by which below the chief one does not transmigrate.
inference: Below-the-chief non-transmigration.

speaker: Teacher (impurity-man)
question: What of impurity-man?
premises: malapuruṣaviveke tu śivasamānatvam — in impurity-man discrimination: Śiva-likeness.
inference: Impurity-man discrimination = Śiva-likeness.

speaker: Teacher (fullness)
question: What of fullness?
premises: puruṣapūrṇatādṛṣṭau tu śivatvam eva — when man's fullness is seen: Śiva-ness alone.
inference: Seen fullness = Śiva-ness.

speaker: Teacher (kalā alone)
question: Does kalā alone give?
premises: evaṃ kalātattvam eva kiṃcitkartṛtvdāyi na ca — kalā-principle alone gives slight makership, not... (completed u44).
inference: Kalā gives slight makership — sentence completes u44.

speaker: Teacher (not the unknowing's)
question: Whose makership?
premises: kartṛtvam ajñasya iti — makership of the unknowing: thus.
inference: Completes: slight makership, not the unknowing's full makership.

speaker: Teacher (impure knowledge)
question: What is impure knowledge?
premises: kiṃcijjñatvadāyiny aśuddhavidyā kalāto jātā — slight-knowing-giving impure knowledge born from kalā.
sā ca vidyā buddhiṃ paśyati — it sees mind.
tadgatāṃś ca sukhādīn vivekena gṛhṇāti — grasps its parts, pleasures and the rest, with discrimination.
inference: Impure knowledge from kalā: sees mind, grasps parts discriminately.

speaker: Teacher (mind's limit)
question: What limits mind?
premises: buddher guṇasaṃkīrṇākārāyā vivekena grahītum asāmarthyāt — of quality-confused mind, inability to grasp with discrimination.
inference: Confused mind cannot discriminate-grasp.

speaker: Teacher (discerned)
question: How discerned?
premises: tasmāt buddhipratibimbito bhāvo vidyayā vivicyate — hence the mind-mirrored being is discerned by knowledge.
inference: Mirrored being discerned by knowledge.

speaker: Teacher (where passion acts)
question: Where does passion act?
premises: kiṃcitkartṛtvaṃ kiṃcidbhāgasiddhaye kvacid eva kartṛtvam ity atra arthe paryavasyati — slight makership for some-part perfection: makership somewhere alone — in this sense it comes down.
kvacid eva ca ity atra bhāge rāgatattvasya vyāpāraḥ — somewhere too in this part is passion-principle's business.
inference: Slight makership somewhere; passion's business in the part.

speaker: Teacher (dispassion)
question: Is it from dispassion?
premises: na ca avairāgyakṛtaṃ tat — not from non-dispassion made.
avairāgyasyāpy arakradarśanāt — seeing non-attachment even of the non-dispassionate.
inference: Not from dispassion; non-attached even the dispassionate.

speaker: Teacher (attachment seen)
question: Where is attachment seen?
premises: vairāgye dharmādāv api raktir dṛśyate — in dispassion, even in duty and the rest, attachment is seen.
inference: Attachment seen even in dispassion-duty.

speaker: Teacher (sated)
question: What of the sated?
premises: tṛptasya ca annādau avairāgyābhāve 'pi antaḥstharāgānapāyāt — of the sated in food and the rest, though non-dispassion absent, from unremoved inner passion.
inference: Sated yet inner passion unremoved.

speaker: Teacher (contingency)
question: Why contingency?
premises: tena vinā punar avairāgyānutpattiprasaṅgāt — without that, again non-dispassion-non-arising contingency.
inference: Without it, non-dispassion wouldn't arise.

speaker: Teacher (necessity's business)
question: What is necessity's business?
premises: kālaś ca kāryaṃ kalayaṃs tadavacchinnaṃ kartṛtvam api kalayati — time reckoning effect reckons even bounded makership.
tulye kvacittve asmin eva kartṛtvam ity atrārthe niyater vyāpāraḥ — in the like some-where-ness, this alone makership: in this sense necessity's business.
inference: Time reckons bounded makership; necessity's business in this sense.

speaker: Teacher (beast defined)
question: What is the beast?
premises: kāryakāraṇabhāve 'pi asyā eva vyāpāraḥ — in cause-effect-ness too hers alone is the business.
tena kalāta eva etac catuṣkaṃ jātam — hence from kalā alone this fourfold born.

idam eva kiṃcid adhunā jānan abhiṣvaktaḥ karomi ity evaṃrūpā saṃvid dehapuryaṣṭakādigatā paśur ity ucyate — this very, slightly now knowing, clinging, I-do: thus-formed awareness gone to body-city-eight and the rest is called beast.
inference: Her business; kalā-born fourfold; clinging I-do awareness = beast.

speaker: Teacher (six sheaths)
question: What are the six?
premises: tad idaṃ māyādiṣaṭkaṃ kañcukaṣaṭkam ucyate — this Māyā-and-rest six is called six sheaths.
inference: Māyā-six = six sheaths named.

speaker: Teacher (why sheaths)
question: Why sheaths?
premises: saṃvido māyayā apahastitatvena kalādīnām uparipātināṃ kañcukavat avasthānāt — awareness by Māyā set aside; kalā and the rest falling above stand like sheaths.
inference: Set-aside awareness; above-falling kalā stands sheath-like.

speaker: Teacher (kalā's issue)
question: What issues from kalā?
premises: evaṃ kiṃcitkartṛtvaṃ yat māyākāryaṃ — slight makership which is Māyā-effect.
tatra kiṃcit tv aviśiṣṭaṃ yat kartṛtvaṃ viśeṣyaṃ — there the slight, but, undistinguished which makership to be qualified.
tatra vyāpriyamāṇā kalā vidyādiprasavahetuḥ iti nirūpitam — there engaged kalā is the cause of knowledge-and-rest birth: described.
inference: Engaged kalā births knowledge-and-rest.

speaker: Teacher (enjoyed-common)
question: What is the enjoyed-common?
premises: idānīṃ viśeṣaṇabhāgo yaḥ kiṃcid ity ukto jñeyaḥ kāryaś ca — now the qualifier part called slight is to be known, and the effect.
taṃ yāvat sā kalā svātmanaḥ pṛthak kurute — as long as she, kalā, makes apart from own self.

tāvad eṣa eva sukhaduḥkhamohātmakabhogyaviśeṣānusyūtasya sāmānyamātrasya tadguṇasāmyāparanāmnaḥ prakṛtitattvasya sargaḥ — so long this very, of enjoyment-particular interwoven with pleasure-pain-delusion-nature, of mere common, of that-guṇa-sameness-alias, of nature-principle is the emission.
iti bhoktṛbhogyayugalasya samam eva kalātattvāyattā sṛṣṭiḥ — thus enjoyer-enjoyed pair together dependent on kalā-principle is emission.
inference: Qualifier part; kalā's apart-making emits the enjoyed-common; pair-emission kalā-dependent.

speaker: Teacher (sequence debate)
question: Sequential or not?
premises: atra caiṣāṃ vāstavena pathā kramavandhyaiva sṛṣṭir ity uktaṃ — here, and by the real path, emission is sequence-barren: said.
kramāvabhāso 'pi cāstīty api uktam eva — sequence-appearing too is, and-is-thus, too said indeed.
inference: Real path barren, appearance sequential: both said.

speaker: Teacher (varied order)
question: Is order varied?
premises: kramaś ca vidyārāgādīnām vicitro 'pi dṛṣṭaḥ — sequence of knowledge-passion and the rest though varied is seen.
kaścid rajyan vetti — someone loving knows.
ko 'pi vidan rajyate ityādi — who knowing is loved, and the rest.
inference: Loving-knowing varies in order: both directions seen.

speaker: Teacher (scriptural variety)
question: Does variety contradict?
premises: tena bhinnakramanirūpaṇam api rauravādiṣu śāstreṣv aviruddhaṃ mantavyaṃ — different-order description even in Raurava and the rest deemed uncontradicted.
tad eva tu bhogyasāmānyaṃ prakṣobhagataṃ guṇatattvam — but that very, become-stirred enjoyed-common: guṇa-principle.
inference: Varied order uncontradicted; stirred enjoyed-common = guṇa.

speaker: Teacher (guṇa natures)
question: What are the guṇa natures?
premises: yatra sukhaṃ bhogyarūpaprakāśaḥ sattvam — where pleasure, enjoyed-form-light: lucidity.
duḥkhaṃ prakāśāprakāśāndolanātmakam ata eva kriyārūpaṃ rajaḥ — pain light-unlight-swing-natured, hence action-formed passion.
mohaḥ prakāśābhāvarūpas tamaḥ — delusion unlight-formed darkness.
inference: Pleasure-light, pain-swing-action, delusion-darkness.

speaker: Teacher (triad)
question: What is the triad?
premises: tritayam api etad bhogyarūpam — triad too, this enjoyed-formed.
inference: Triad all enjoyed-formed.

speaker: Teacher (stirring needed)
question: Must the chief stir?
premises: evaṃ kṣubdhāt pradhānāt kartavyāntarodayaḥ na akṣubdhād iti — from stirred chief, to-be-done-arising; not from unstirred.
inference: Only stirred chief yields effects.

speaker: Teacher (proof needed)
question: Why assume stirring?
premises: kṣobhaḥ avaśyam eva antarāle 'bhyupagantavya iti siddhaṃ sāṃkhyaparidṛṣṭaṃ pṛthagbhūtaṃ guṇatattvam — stirring necessarily indeed in between to be assumed: thus proved Sāṃkhya-seen separated guṇa-principle.
inference: Stirring must be assumed between; Sāṃkhya-seen separated guṇa.

speaker: Teacher (presiding needed)
question: Why presiding?
premises: sa ca kṣobhaḥ prakṛtes tattveśādhiṣṭhānād eva — and that stirring from category-lord-presiding alone.
anyathā niyataṃ puruṣaṃ prati iti na sidhyet — otherwise toward fixed man, thus would not succeed.
inference: Without presiding, no fixed-man success.

speaker: Teacher (mind born)
question: How is mind born?
premises: tato guṇatattvāt buddhitattvaṃ yatra puṃprakāśo viṣayaś ca pratibimbam arpayataḥ — then from guṇa-principle mind-principle, where man-light and object offer reflection.
inference: Guṇa to mind; man-light and object reflect.

speaker: Teacher (I-maker born)
question: How is I-maker born?
premises: buddhitattvāt ahaṃkāro yena buddhipratibimbite vedyasamparke kaluṣe puṃprakāshi 'nātmani ātmābhimānaḥ śuktau rajatābhimānavat — from mind-principle I-maker, by which in mind-mirrored object-contact turbid, in man-light, in non-self is self-pride, like silver-pride in shell.
inference: Mind-mirror turbid contact breeds self-pride; shell-silver simile.

speaker: Teacher (Sāṃkhya refused)
question: Why not Sāṃkhya?
premises: ata eva kāra ity anena kṛtakatvam asya uktaṃ — hence making-ness by this of it is said.
sāṃkhyasya tu tat na yujyate — Sāṃkhya's that does not fit.
sa hi na ātmano 'haṃvimarśamayatām icchati — for he does not wish self's I-feeling-nature.
vayaṃ tu kartṛtvam api tasya icchāmaḥ — but we wish makership too of it.
inference: We keep I-feeling and makership; Sāṃkhya fits neither.

speaker: Teacher (pure I)
question: What is pure I?
premises: tac ca śuddhaṃ vimarśa eva apratiyogi svātmacamatkārarūpo 'ham iti — and that pure deliberation alone, non-rivalled, own-self-wonder-formed I: thus.
inference: Pure I: non-rivalled wonder-formed deliberation.

speaker: Teacher (instrument heap)
question: What is the instrument heap?
premises: eṣo 'sya ahaṃkārasya karaṇaskandhaḥ — this is of it, of I-maker: instrument-heap.
inference: I-maker's instrument-heap named.

speaker: Teacher (nature heap)
question: What is the nature heap?
premises: prakṛtiskandhas tu tasyaiva trividhaḥ sattvādibhedāt — nature-heap of it alone threefold, by lucidity-and-rest difference.
inference: Threefold nature-heap by guṇa difference.

speaker: Teacher (lucid creation)
question: What does the lucid create?
premises: tatra sāttviko yasmāt manaś ca buddhīndriyapañcakaṃ ca — there the lucid, from which mind and five mind-senses.
tatra manasi janye sarvatanmātrajanasaṃsāmarthyayuktaḥ sa janakaḥ — there in generable mind, endowed with all-subtle-birth power: it the begetter.
inference: Lucid mind begets; all-subtle-birth power in generable mind.

speaker: Teacher (sense proof)
question: How are senses proved?
premises: śrotre tu śabdajananasāmarthyaviśiṣṭa iti — in ear, distinguished by sound-birth power: thus.
yāvad ghrāṇe gandhajananayogyatāyukta iti — up to nose, fit with smell-birth fitness: thus.
bhautikam api na yuktam — elemental too not fitting.
