premises: tato yathāśakti hutvā sruksruvau ūrdhvādhomukhatayā śaktiśivarūpau parasparonmukhau vidhāya — offered as able; ladle-spoon up-down-facing as power-Śiva-formed, mutually facing arranged.

samapādotthito dvādaśāntagaganoditaśivapūrṇacandraniḥsṛtapatatparāmṛtadhārābhāvanāṃ kurvan — standing even-footed, contemplating the stream of supreme nectar fallen, risen in the sky of the twelve-end, risen full-Śiva-moon.
vauṣaḍantaṃ mantram uccārayan ca — and uttering the vauṣaḍ-ending mantra.
ājyakṣayāntaṃ tiṣṭhet — until ghee's end stand.
iti pūrṇāhutiḥ mantracakrasaṃtarpaṇī — full oblation, mantra-wheel-sating.
inference: Even-footed, nectar-stream contemplated, vauṣaḍ uttered till ghee ends.

speaker: Teacher (caru)
question: How share caru?
premises: tataś caruṃ prokṣitam ānīya sthaṇḍilakalaśakumbhavahniṣu bhāgaṃ bhāgaṃ nivedya ekabhāgam avaśeṣya śiṣyāya bhāgaṃ dadyāt — sprinkled caru brought; on altar-vessel-jar-fires share by share offered; one share left; to the disciple give a share.
inference: Shared caru; one share left; disciple's share given.

speaker: Teacher (tooth-stick)
question: What next?
premises: tato dantakāṣṭham — then the tooth-stick.
inference: Tooth-stick next.

speaker: Teacher (omen)
question: What of the throw?
premises: tatpāto 'gniyamanirṛtidikṣu adhaś ca na śubha iti — its falling in fire-Yama-Nirṛti directions and below is not auspicious: thus.
inference: Fall there inauspicious.

speaker: Teacher (oblation)
question: What oblation?
premises: tatra homo 'stramantreṇa kāryaḥ — there oblation by weapon-mantra is to be done.
inference: Weapon-mantra oblation.

speaker: Teacher (blindfold)
question: How bring in?
premises: tato vikṣepaparihāreṇa bhāvimantradarśanayogyatāyai baddhanetraṃ śiṣyaṃ praveśya — for distraction-avoidance, for fitness to see the future mantra, having brought in the blindfolded disciple.
jānusthitaṃ taṃ kṛtvā puṣpāñjaliṃ kṣepayet — having made him kneeling, have him cast a flower-handful.
inference: Blindfolded, kneeling, flower-cast for mantra-fitness.

speaker: Teacher (sight)
question: What on unveiling?
premises: tataḥ sahasā apāsitanetrabandho 'sau śaktipātānugṛhītakaraṇatvāt — suddenly unfastened-eye-bound, through descent-graced instrument-ness.
saṃnihitamantraṃ tatsthānaṃ sākṣātkāreṇa paśyan tanmayo bhavati — seeing the present mantra in that place face-to-face, becomes made of that.
anugṛhītakaraṇānāṃ mantrasaṃnidhiḥ pratyakṣaḥ — of graced instruments mantra-nearness is visible.
yatas trasyatām iva bhūtānām — since as it were of trembling beings.
inference: Unveiled seeing makes one of that; mantra-nearness visible to graced.

speaker: Teacher (bonds)
question: How burn bonds?
premises: tataḥ svadakṣiṇahaste dīpyatayā devatācakraṃ pūjayitvā — in one's own right hand with blazing, having worshipped the deity-wheel.
taṃ hastaṃ mūrdhahṛnnābhiṣu śiṣyasya pāśān dahantaṃ nikṣipet — placing it burning the disciple's bonds on head-heart-navel.
inference: Blazing right hand burns head-heart-navel bonds.

speaker: Teacher (left hand)
question: What with the left?
premises: tato vāme somyatayā pūjayitvā śuddhatattvāpyāyinaṃ — then in the left with gentleness, having worshipped, fattening with pure principle.
tataḥ praṇāmaṃ kuryāt — then bow.
inference: Gentle left fattens with pure principle; then bow.

speaker: Teacher (offering out)
question: What outside?
premises: tato bhūtadevatādigbaliṃ madyamāṃsajalādipūrṇaṃ bahir dadyāt — being-deity-direction-offering, full of wine-meat-water, outside give.
ācāmeta — having sipped.
inference: Outside offering; sipping.

speaker: Teacher (staying)
question: How stay?
premises: tataḥ svayaṃ carubhojanaṃ kṛtvā śiṣyātmanā saha aikyam āpannaḥ prabuddhavṛttiḥ tiṣṭhet — having eaten the oblation-meal oneself, with disciple-self attaining oneness, awakened-natured stay.
inference: Meal eaten; oneness with disciple; awakened stay.

speaker: Teacher (dreams)
question: What of dreams?
premises: svapan api prabhāte śiṣyaḥ cet aśubhaṃ svapnaṃ vadet — dreaming too, at dawn if the disciple tells an inauspicious dream.
tat asmai na vyākuryāt — that to him one should not explain.
inference: Inauspicious dreams unexplained.

speaker: Teacher (fear)
question: What of fear?
premises: śaṅkātaṅkau hi tathāsya syātām — doubt and fear would be his.
kevalam astreṇa tanniṣkṛtiṃ kuryāt — merely with the weapon make its expiation.
inference: Unexplained dreams breed fear; weapon-expiation only.

speaker: Teacher (entering)
question: How enter the disciple?
premises: tatas tathaiva parameśvaraṃ pūjayitvā tadagre śiṣyasya prāṇakrameṇa praviśya — just so worshipped the Lord, entered before him by the disciple's breath-course.
hṛtkaṇṭhatālulalāṭarandhradvādaśānteṣu ṣaṭsu kāraṇaṣaṭkasparśaṃ kurvan — in heart-throat-palate-brow-cleft-twelve-ends, six six-cause-touchings doing.
pratyekam aṣṭau saṃskārān cintayan — each eight refinements contemplating.
kaṃcit kālaṃ śiṣyaprāṇaṃ tatraiva viśramayya — some time resting the disciple-breath right there.
punar avarohet — again descend.
inference: Breath-course entry; six places touched; eight refinements each; rest; descend.

speaker: Teacher (samayin)
question: What results?
premises: ity evāpāditāṣṭācatvāriṃśatsaṃskāroparikṛtarudrāṃśāpattiḥ samayībhavati — thus effected-forty-eight-refinements-upon-made-Rudra-part-attainment becomes a samayin.
inference: 48 refinements + Rudra-part = samayin.

speaker: Teacher (mantra gift)
question: What bestowed?
premises: tataḥ asmai pūjyaṃ mantraṃ puṣpādyaiḥ saha arpayet — then to him the worshippable mantra with flowers and the rest bestow.
inference: Worshippable mantra bestowed with flowers.

speaker: Teacher (rules)
question: What next?
premises: tataḥ samayān asmai nirūpayet — then the rules to him lay down.
inference: Rules laid down.

speaker: Teacher (samaya code)
question: What are the rules?
premises: gurau sarvātmanā bhaktiḥ — in the guru with whole self, devotion.
tathā śāstre deve tatpratidvaṃdvini parāṅmukhatā — so in scripture; in God; aversion toward their opponents.
guruvat guruputrādeḥ — like the guru, of the guru's son and the rest.
vidyāsambandhakṛtasya tatpūrvadīkṣitādeḥ saṃdarśanam — of the knowledge-tied made, of the before-initiated and the rest, seeing.
yaunasambandhasya tadārādhanārtham na tu svata — of the womb-tie, for its honouring, not by oneself.
iti mantavyam — thus to be deemed.
inference: Devotion to guru/scripture/God; aversion to opponents; reverence to kin and fellow-initiates.

speaker: Teacher (women)
question: What of women?
premises: striyo vandhyāyās tajjugupsāhetuṃ na kuryāt — of women, of the barren that-loathing-cause one should not do.
inference: No loathing-cause toward barren women.
uncertainties: tajjugupsāhetuṃ formation obscure; reading follows print.

speaker: Teacher (names)
question: What of names?
premises: devatānāma gurunāma tathā mantraṃ pūjākālāt ṛte na uccārayet — deity-name, guru-name, and mantra, apart from worship-time, one should not utter.
inference: Names unspoken outside worship-time.

speaker: Teacher (guru's things)
question: What of the guru's things?
premises: gurūpabhuktaṃ śayyādi na bhuñjīta — what the guru has enjoyed — bed and the rest — one should not enjoy.
inference: Guru-enjoyed things not to be enjoyed.

speaker: Teacher (play)
question: What of play?
premises: yat kiṃcit laukikaṃ krīḍādi tat gurusaṃnidhau na kuryāt — what games and the rest are worldly, that in the guru's nearness one should not do.
inference: No worldly play near the guru.

speaker: Teacher (excellence)
question: What of excellence?
premises: tadvyatirekeṇa na anyatra utkarṣabuddhiṃ kuryāt — apart from that, elsewhere one should not make excellence-thought.
inference: No excellence-thought elsewhere.

speaker: Teacher (worship)
question: Whom worship?
premises: sarvatra śrāddhādau gurum eva pūjayet — everywhere, in śrāddha and the rest, the guru alone worship.
inference: Guru alone everywhere.

speaker: Teacher (speech)
question: What not say?
premises: sarveṣu ca naimittikeṣu śākinītyādiśabdān na vadet — and in all occasionals, śākinī-and-the-rest words one should not say.
inference: No śākinī-words on occasionals.

speaker: Teacher (festivals)
question: What of festivals?
premises: parvadināni pūjayet — festival days worship.
inference: Festival days worshipped.

speaker: Teacher (company)
question: Whose company?
premises: vaiṣṇavādyair adhodṛṣṭibhiḥ saha saṃgatiṃ na kuryāt — with those of lower sight, Vaiṣṇavas and the rest, company one should not make.
inference: No company with the lower-seeing.

speaker: Teacher (birth)
question: What of birth?
premises: etacchāsanasthān pūrvajātibuddhyā na paśyet — abiding in this teaching, one should not see with former-birth thought.
inference: No former-birth thought in this teaching.

speaker: Teacher (hospitality)
question: What hospitality?
premises: guruvarge gṛhāgate yathāśakti yāgaṃ kuryāt — when the guru's circle has come home, as able do worship.
inference: Worship as able for the guru's circle.

speaker: Teacher (apostates)
question: What of apostates?
premises: adhomārgasthitaṃ kaṃcit vaiṣṇavādyaṃ tacchāstrakulāt gurūkṛtyāpi tyajet — a lower-path abider, having even made him guru, from his teaching-clan abandon.
inference: Abandon even a guru-turned-apostate with his clan.

speaker: Teacher (seeing)
question: How see them?
premises: tadāpi na utkarṣabuddhyā paśyet — even then one should not see with excellence-thought.
inference: No excellence-thought even then.

speaker: Teacher (sects)
question: What of sects?
premises: liṅgibhiḥ saha samācāramelanaṃ na kuryāt — with mark-bearers no conduct-meeting make.
tān kevalaṃ yathāśakti pūjayet — them only as able worship.
inference: No mixing with sects; mere as-able worship.

speaker: Teacher (doubt)
question: What of doubt?
premises: śaṅkās tyajet — doubts abandon.
inference: Doubts abandoned.

speaker: Teacher (divisions)
question: What of divisions?
premises: cakre sthitaś caramāgryādivibhāgaṃ janmakṛtaṃ na saṃkalpayet — in the wheel, standing, of last-and-first division, birth-made, one should not fancy.
inference: No birth-made last-first fancy in the wheel.

speaker: Teacher (holy places)
question: What of holy places?
premises: śarīrāt ṛte na anyat āyatanatīrthādikaṃ bahumānena paśyet — apart from the body, no other abode-ford and the rest with high regard see.
inference: No abode higher than the body.

speaker: Teacher (dakṣiṇā)
question: What giving?
premises: mantrahṛdayam anavarataṃ smaret — constantly remember the mantra-heart.

ity evaṃ śiṣyaḥ śrutvā praṇamya abhyupagamya guruṃ dhanadāraśarīraparyantayā dakṣiṇayā paritoṣya — thus the disciple, having heard, bowed, accepted, the guru with wealth-wife-body-up-to gift pleasing.
pūrvadīkṣitāṃś ca dīnānāthādikān tarpayet — and the before-initiated and poor-lordless sating.
inference: Constant mantra-heart; wealth-to-body dakṣiṇā; sating of priors and poor.

speaker: Teacher (image)
question: What image rite?
premises: bhāvividhinā ca mūrticakraṃ tarpayet — and with the future rule, the image-wheel sate.
inference: Image-wheel sated by future rule.

speaker: Teacher (seal)
question: What is he?
premises: itthaṃ samayībhavati — thus one becomes a samayin.
inference: Thus samayin: seal of the ahnika.

speaker: Teacher (entitlement)
question: What entitlement?
premises: mantrābhyāse nityapūjāyāṃ śravaṇe 'dhyayane adhikārī — in mantra-practice, daily worship, hearing, study: entitled.
naimittike tu sarvatra gurum eva abhyarthayet — but in the occasional, everywhere the guru alone request.
inference: Entitled to practice/study; occasionals need the guru.

speaker: Teacher (seal)
question: What rule?
premises: iti sāmayiko vidhiḥ — thus the samayin rule.
inference: Samayin rule: final seal.

speaker: Teacher (putraka-dīkṣā)
question: What is announced?
premises: Now the child-initiation rite.
inference: The topic: putrakadīkṣāvidhi — child-initiation rite declared.

speaker: Teacher (putraka-dīkṣā)
question: How is it sourced?
premises: It is expanded, determined from the Tantrāloka.
inference: The rite's expansion derives from Tantrāloka — authority by derivation.

speaker: Teacher (putraka-dīkṣā)
question: How is it presented here?
premises: But it is stated condensed.
inference: Condensed restatement (saṃkṣipta) for this manual's use.

speaker: Teacher (putraka-dīkṣā)
question: What is the third-day mandala-worship order?
premises: Samaya-ending rite on the third day; group-sacrifice in trident-lotus mandala; outer-retinue + door-deity-wheel outside; from Aiśa-corner to Agneya in row-order: Gaṇapati, gurus, parameṣṭhin, former-teachers, yoginī-wheel, Vāgīśvarī, Kṣetrapāla.
inference: The pūjā-krama: three-day samaya-close, then sequential deity-installation from Aiśa to āgneya.

speaker: Teacher (putraka-dīkṣā)
question: Where do the three Parās stand?
premises: Whole path placed trident-root to white-lotus; middle-axis Śrīparābhaṭṭārikā with Bhairavanatha, left Śrīmadaparā, right Śrīparāparā; right-trident-middle Śrīmadaparā, left-trident-middle Śrīparāparā — two each in their own places.
inference: The triśūla-axis placement of the three Parā-deities (bhagavatī + Bhairavanātha + apāra-parā pairs), each on its axis.

speaker: Teacher (putraka-dīkṣā)
question: What does all-place-enshrinement do?
premises: Thus by all-place-enshrinement of the Goddess, all becomes complete from her enshrinement — thus.
inference: Tathāvidha sarvasthāna-adhiṣṭhātṛtva: everything becomes pūrṇa from the Goddess's enshrinement.

speaker: Teacher (putraka-dīkṣā)
question: What of the middle-axis wheel?
premises: Then in the middle-trident's middle-axis, whole deity-wheel to lokapāla-missile worshipped by non-difference-alone; from its enshrinement, worshipped everywhere.
inference: The devatā-cakra on the middle axis is worshipped abhinnatayā; its enshrinement extends pūjā everywhere.

speaker: Teacher (putraka-dīkṣā)
question: What is the five-ground conjunction?
premises: In pot, kalasa, mandala, fire, own-self — by non-difference-contemplation join the five-grounds; then special-worship by the Lord two-nature-juice's flowers and rest.
inference: Pañcādhikaraṇa-saṃdhi: five vessels joined by abhedabhāvanā, then viśeṣa-pūjā with puṣpādi enriched by parameśvara-advaya-rasa.

speaker: Teacher (putraka-dīkṣā)
question: Why is wealth-deception excluded?
premises: Why bother? Complete with satisfaction-food-offering, without wealth-deception — let him make the sacrifice-place.
inference: The yāgasthāna must be tarpaṇa-naivedya-paripūrṇa and vitta-śāṭhya-virahita — no fraud in funding.

speaker: Teacher (putraka-dīkṣā)
question: When is the great-mandala-sacrifice forbidden?
premises: In non-being wealth, the great-mandala-sacrifice is not to be done — indeed.
inference: Mahā-maṇḍala-yāga requires actual wealth (asati vitte); without it, na kartavya eva.

speaker: Teacher (putraka-dīkṣā)
question: What about animals?
premises: And living animals let him offer.
inference: Jīvataḥ paśūn nivedayet — living animals are offered (the paśu-rite licensed).

speaker: Teacher (putraka-dīkṣā)
question: Why not doubt the animal-rite?
premises: They too become graced thus — by compassion in the animal-rite one should not doubt.
inference: Kāruṇikatayā: even paśus are anugrītā — the rite benefits them; no doubt (na vicikitset).

speaker: Teacher (putraka-dīkṣā)
question: What follows the paśu-offering?
premises: Fire: Supreme-Lord satisfied by sesame-ghee; another animal for vapa-hom; deity-wheel satisfied by its fat; mandala worshipped again; approaching the Lord, contemplating self all-six-path-complete, the disciple placed in front.
inference: The vapa-homārtha sequence: saṃtaraṇa → paśu-vapa → devatā-cakra-tarpaṇa → maṇḍala → parameśvara-vijñāpana → self-contemplation → disciple placed.

speaker: Teacher (putraka-dīkṣā)
question: What is contemplated for parokṣa-dīkṣā?
premises: In indirect initiation, of-living-dead-form, contemplate him in front — or establish a darba-cow-dung likeness in front.
inference: Jīvan-mūrta or pratikṛti: the (dead) disciple contemplated or represented before the rite.

speaker: Teacher (putraka-dīkṣā)
question: How is the disciple prepared?
premises: Such a disciple — sprinkled with offering-drops, worshipped by flowers — the whole path placed in his body.
inference: Argha-pātra-prokṣaṇa + puṣpa-pūjā, then samastam adhvānaṃ taddehe nyaset — path installed in the disciple's body.

speaker: Teacher (putraka-dīkṣā)
question: What does the teacher consider for a bhogecchu?
premises: Then thus let him consider: for the enjoyment-seeker, the auspicious — let him not cleanse.
inference: For the bhogeccha, the śubha is NOT to be purified (na śodhayet) — desire left intact.

speaker: Teacher (putraka-dīkṣā)
question: What about the mumukṣu?
premises: For the liberation-seeker, the auspicious-and-unauspicious — both even.
inference: For mumukṣu both śubha-aśubha are handled (ubhayam api) — full purification.

speaker: Teacher (putraka-dīkṣā)
question: What is the nirbījā rule?
premises: In the seedless, covenant-nooses also cleansed; she is for near-death, even most-foolish — the Lord's command; attainment for him by mere teacher-deity-fire devotion-faith.
inference: Nirbījā dīkṣā cleanses samaya-pāśas even for mūḍha (Lord's ājñā); siddhi by guru-devatā-agni-bhakti-niṣṭha alone.

speaker: Teacher (putraka-dīkṣā)
question: What distinguishes the mantras?
premises: Herein everywhere habit-capture is the distinguishing [factor], by habit-conformity — from that-and-that work-doing.
inference: Vāsanā-grahaṇam is the bhedaka: mantra-efficacy follows vāsanā-conformity (tattatkārya-kāritva).

speaker: Teacher (putraka-dīkṣā)
question: How is the whole path cleansed?
premises: Having traced habit-distinction, by main-mantra-consideration-special, the path in-own-body, by Siva-two-nature-contemplation.
inference: Anusaṃdhāya-vāsanābheda → mukhya-mantra-parāmarśa-viśeṣa + śivādvaya-bhāvanā = svadeha-gata-adhvan-śodhanā.

speaker: Teacher (putraka-dīkṣā)
question: What is the disciple's transformation?
premises: From foot-thumb to twelve-end, disciple-body-consciousness made non-different from self-body-consciousness — right-there, in infinite-bliss-lake, freedom-sovereignty essence, Lord of the deity-wheel, world-manḍala — by union in such form with disciple-self, one becomes, rest attained; thus non-different from the Lord.
inference: The climax: pāda-aṅguṣṭha-to-dvādaśānta identity-attainment — śiṣya-caitanya abhinnī-kṛta with self-caitanya, viśrānti in the anantānanda-sarovara — parameśvara-abhinna bhavati.

speaker: Teacher (putraka-dīkṣā)
question: How is an enjoyment-seeker joined?
premises: If enjoyment-seeker: where in-tattva his desire becomes, right-there by whole-and-scattered-manner join.
inference: Bhogeccha-tattva-yojana: join at exactly the tattva where desire stands, samasta-vyasta-tayā.

speaker: Teacher (putraka-dīkṣā)
question: What is the final body?
premises: Thereafter for residual-function, from the Lord's nature, suddenly emerged, made-of-pure-tattva body contemplate — thus this all-noose-releasing initiation.
inference: The śeṣa-vṛtti body: jhaṭiti-prasṛta, śuddhatattva-maya — this dīkṣā is the samasta-pāśa-vyojikā.

speaker: Teacher (putraka-dīkṣā)
question: How does the disciple close?
premises: Then the disciple the guru by fees, as-before, let worship.
inference: Guru-pūjā with dakṣiṇā, pūrvavat — the closing courtesy.

speaker: Teacher (putraka-dīkṣā)
question: What is the disciple's fire-rite?
premises: In fire the disciple's rite: Sri-Para-mantra — so-and-so's so-and-so tattva I-purify — ending-with-svaha, three oblations per tattva, complete ending-with-vausad at end.
inference: The śiṣya-homa: pratitattva tri-āhuti with svāhānta, pūrṇā vauṣaḍantā — per-tattva purification formula.

speaker: Teacher (putraka-dīkṣā)
question: What completes the tattva-purification?
premises: Thus Siva-end-tattva-purification; then by-yojanika-told-order full-offering.
inference: Śivānta-tattva-śuddhi closed, then pūrṇāhuti by the yojanika-described order.

speaker: Teacher (putraka-dīkṣā)
question: Which offerings for which seeker?
premises: For the enjoyment-seeker, in the enjoyment-place, for-yojanika one [offering]; another for pure-tattva-creation, one-more.
inference: Two pūrṇāhutis: bhogeccha's for yojanā in bhoga-sthāna; the other for śuddhatattva-sṛṣṭi.

speaker: Teacher (putraka-dīkṣā)
question: How does the rite end?
premises: Then worship of the guru by fees — thus this child-initiation.
inference: Guru-dakṣiṇā-pūjana closes: ity eṣā putrakadīkṣā — the rite names itself at the end.

speaker: Teacher (putraka-dīkṣā)
question: What gets purified?
premises: In-which ongoing one [tattva] — having-excluded past and future — act is purified.
inference: The seal: vartamāna-eka-varjita-bhūta-bhaviṣyat-karma-śuddhi — ongoing tattva purified of past/future acts.

speaker: Teacher (dīkṣā-vidhi)
question: When is the exit-initiation performed?
premises: Near death, a power-descent arises — of himself or through a kinsman's mouth.
Then for him immediately the samutkramaṇa-initiation is performed.
inference: Śaktipāta near death triggers the exit-initiation at once, whether it comes of oneself or through another's mouth.

speaker: Teacher (dīkṣā-vidhi)
question: What is done to the disciple before the full-offering?
premises: The whole path is placed in the disciple and he is purified in order.
Blessed Kālarātrī the vein-cutter is placed, joint by joint; the vein-nooses are split, and the disciple's consciousness is made dwell at the brahmarandhra.
inference: Nyāsa of the adhvan, ordered purification, and Kālarātrī's joint-by-joint vein-cutting move the disciple's caitanya to the brahmarandhra.

speaker: Teacher (dīkṣā-vidhi)
question: Why is the full-offering given, and with what result?
premises: By the aforesaid order the full-offering is given for yojanā's sake.
At the full-offering the departed soul goes out and becomes one with Paramaśiva.
inference: The pūrṇāhuti completes yojanā: the jīva, exiting, becomes abhinna with Paramaśiva.

speaker: Teacher (dīkṣā-vidhi)
question: Which full-offering comes for the enjoyer?
premises: For the desirer of enjoyment there is a second full-offering.
inference: A second pūrṇāhuti is reserved for the bubhukṣu — desire of bhoga gets its own oblation.

speaker: Teacher (dīkṣā-vidhi)
question: What if yojanā falls in the enjoyment-place — what rescues it?
premises: In the bhoga-sthāna for yojanā, at that time in his jīvalaya, no śeṣa-vartana remains.
Or Brahma-vidyā is recited in the ear: of parāmarśa-nature, she instantly awakens vimarśa in the already-awakened paśu-caitanya.
inference: No residual turning remains there; the alternative is aural Brahma-vidyā, whose parāmarśa-nature instantly makes vimarśa manifest in the paśu's awakened consciousness.

speaker: Teacher (dīkṣā-vidhi)
question: On what authority does the ear-recitation stand?
premises: Also in this recitation there is authority from samayya and the rest.
inference: The etat-pāṭha's adhikāra derives from samayya-ādi — the recitation is licensed, not invented.

speaker: Teacher (dīkṣā-vidhi)
question: What is the rite of the seedless initiation shown to a fool or a late-comer?
premises: To a fool and to one whose power-descent has come, a with-conviction seedless dīkṣā is shown; at Śiva-hand-giving-time this rite: a triangular āgneya mandala, flame-terrible, repha-spark, outward-vāta-wheel-rolling, contemplated in the right hand, a little seed cast therein, burnt by phaṭkāra-successions of up-down repha.
Doing thus, the hand is cast onto the disciple's head; for both, this seedless initiation destroys the capacity for doing one's own work — since even inanimate things are stated initiatable.
The disciple is contemplated installed inside the vāyupura, shaken and become-light — by which, compared, he is seen light.
inference: The nirbījā dīkṣā works palm-mandala → seed-burning by phaṭkāras → hand-on-head, destroying svakārya-karaṇa-sāmarthya; even sthāvara qualify, and the light-comparison confirms the disciple's laghūbhāva.

speaker: Teacher (parokṣa-dīkṣā)
question: What two kinds of indirect initiation?
premises: Now indirect initiation is twofold: the dead one, and the jīva-part.
inference: Parokṣa-dīkṣā splits into mṛta and jīvaṃśa — the chapter's two subjects.

speaker: Teacher (parokṣa-dīkṣā)
question: Who is commanded to be initiated thus?
premises: One who has served the guru — dead, banished, sorcery-killed, infant-killed, arisen at the death-moment, or power-descent through another mouth — likewise one to be initiated: such the command.
inference: The ājñā lists the eligible cases: guru-service plus the death-circumstances, closed by the catch-all 'to be initiated'.

speaker: Teacher (parokṣa-dīkṣā)
question: Is adhivāsa used for the dead?
premises: And in the dead-initiation, adhivāsa-and-rest is not used.
inference: Mṛtadīkṣā excludes adhivāsa-ādi — the living-rite preliminaries dropped.

speaker: Teacher (parokṣa-dīkṣā)
question: What are the presence-causes in the mandala?
premises: In the mandala: abundant rite, supreme instrument, flower-and-rest seat, pedestal-and-rest, trident-lotus form, specific meditation-mantra, itself radiant — of the meditation-devoted yogi, the one-devotion-immersion-rich, and the knower: these are the saṃnidhāna-hetavaḥ, stated in order.
inference: Seven presence-causes (kriyā, upakaraṇa, sthāna, maṇḍala, ākṛti, dhyeya-mantra, radiant self) plus the two yogic subjects — the sequence is authoritative.

speaker: Teacher (parokṣa-dīkṣā)
question: What happens when they come together?
premises: In their conjunction, what talk would there be? — thus it was said by the Supreme Lord.
inference: Samuditatve makes the question rhetorical: once present, nothing further to ask — divine verdict.

speaker: Teacher (parokṣa-dīkṣā)
question: What does the seer do after worship?
premises: Having worshipped the god and established his form, by the guru-derived teaching-order let him see it; rising from muladhara, crossing by seminal power the endless nerve-path-staff to the nose-sky — let him seek to pervade.
inference: The jāla-sequence: worship → establish → see by guru-order → muladhara-rise → nāḍī-crossing to nāsāgagana → vyāpti-desire.

speaker: Teacher (parokṣa-dīkṣā)
question: How long does the great jala-named practice run?
premises: As long as, by smoke heaped fine-flame mesh, the path-wheel is covered and the desired jīva is brought — thus the great jala-named practice.
inference: The practice's duration = smoke-coverage of dhvacakra + ānayana of the jīva — named mahā-jalānāma-prayoga.

speaker: Teacher (parokṣa-dīkṣā)
question: What does the covering achieve?
premises: By this, the to-be-covered goes into another's power — facing first; afterwards the whole is brought, if — or then even from the path's middle, as he wishes.
inference: Acchādanīya enters paravaśa (saṃmukhīnatvam ādau); the whole follows paścāt or adhvamadhyāt yatheṣṭam.

speaker: Teacher (parokṣa-dīkṣā)
question: Which yoga is this, told by whom?
premises: Two-drawn or two-raised, or in a dead person's scope: the yoga gone through blessed Śaṃbhunātha's tradition — jala-named, told by me.
inference: The ākṛṣṭāv/uddhatau/mṛtajana scopes are covered by the jālanāmā yoga as transmitted by Śrīśaṃbhunātha-āgama and authored here.

speaker: Teacher (parokṣa-dīkṣā)
question: Why does the outside case not behave the same?
premises: Outside too — how does it not happen? From drawing-and-rest without practice, if asked: by passion-hatred-yoga-vaśa in its operation, from the aiśvarya-āveśa-yoga.
inference: The outside fails without abhyāsa — its operation runs on rāga-dveṣa-yoga-vaśa, not on the aiśvarya-immersion that inner drawing has.

speaker: Teacher (parokṣa-dīkṣā)
question: What follows from niyati-niyantrita?
premises: Then, from being necessarily controlled, dependence on practice-and-rest would indeed be.
inference: Because the krama is niyata-niyamtrita, abhyāsa-āpekṣā follows necessarily.

speaker: Teacher (parokṣa-dīkṣā)
question: What differs here?
premises: Here, however, from immersion in grace-natured Lordhood, such is the state.
inference: Iha-tu: the grace-natured parameśvara-tāveśa produces tathābhāva directly — no practice-dependence.

speaker: Teacher (parokṣa-dīkṣā)
question: Who does the gracing, and by what door?
premises: For the Supreme Lord himself, by the door of the guru's body-abode, graces those to be graced.
inference: Anugraha flows parameśvara → guru-śarīra-adhiṣṭhāna-dvāra → anugrāhyāḥ.

speaker: Teacher (parokṣa-dīkṣā)
question: What is said of him?
premises: And he, of unthinkable glory — it is mostly said.
inference: Acintya-mahimā: the claim is ukta-prāyam — mostly told, hedge kept.

speaker: Teacher (parokṣa-dīkṣā)
question: What becomes of the drawn jīva, and does he tremble?
premises: Thus drawn by jala-practice, the jīva enters dārbha, jasmine-fruit or body, becomes; nor trembles — equipment absent; but by that contemplation's force trembles even so: purification-consecration, within the full-offering's yojana-end.
inference: Entered-body samāviṣṭa has no spanda (sāmagrī-absence) yet has tadanudhyāna-bala spanda — the double movement ends in prokṣaṇa-saṃskāra within pūrṇāhuti-yojanā.

speaker: Teacher (parokṣa-dīkṣā)
question: What happens to the dārbha-form in the fire?
premises: Here, further, by the full-offering, dissolution of the dārbha-and-rest form in the supreme fire is to be done.
inference: Pūrṇāhuti effects laya of the dārbhādyākāra in paratejas.

speaker: Teacher (parokṣa-dīkṣā)
question: When is the raised one released?
premises: Thus raised out, he is released by the full-offering itself — if he stands in hell-ghost-animal classes.
inference: Apavāra by pūrṇāhutyā eva, conditioned on the svarnāraka-preta-tiryak standing.

speaker: Teacher (parokṣa-dīkṣā)
question: What does a man obtain then?
premises: A man, just then, obtains knowledge, yoga, initiation, or discernment.
inference: Manuṣya-tadaiva: jñāna/yoga/dīkṣā/viveka available in the same moment.

speaker: Teacher (parokṣa-dīkṣā)
question: Why can the dead be raised?
premises: From being an eligible body — thus the raising-of-the-dead.
inference: Adhikāri-śarīratva grounds mṛtoddharaṇa — eligibility, not sentiment.

speaker: Teacher (parokṣa-dīkṣā)
question: What is the krama for the living too?
premises: Even for the living, in indirect initiation when power-descent arises: this very sequence — excepting dārbha-form-imagination jīva-drawing.
inference: The same krama extends to jīvataḥ parokṣa-utpanna-śaktipāta, minus the dārbha-ākṛti-kalpana-ākṛṣṭi.

speaker: Teacher (parokṣa-dīkṣā)
question: Who gets consecrated without the rite?
premises: The consecration of the one established by mere meditation itself.
inference: Dhyāna-mātra-upasthāpita alone suffices for saṃskāra — meditation-established, no fire.

speaker: Teacher (parokṣa-dīkṣā)
question: What does dīkṣā give?
premises: Initiation gives both the enjoyment and the enjoyer.
inference: Bhoga-bhokṣa-ubhaya-dāyinī — dīkṣā grants both sides of enjoyment at once.

speaker: Teacher (parokṣa-dīkṣā)
question: Why is the higher-doctrine consecration stronger for many?
premises: From the strength of one's own habit, and the unthinkability of severing the enjoyment-habit: by many, in initiation, the higher-doctrine consecration is strong; another would be for that consecration.
inference: Sva-vāsanā-balīyastva + bhoga-vāsanā-viccheda-asambhāvyamānatva make ūrdhva-śāsana-saṃskāra balavān for the many; anya is for that saṃskāra.

speaker: Teacher (parokṣa-dīkṣā)
question: What of the initiated from outside?
premises: Likewise for the initiated from outside — the manifestation of knowledge-and-rest, it is said.
inference: Paroṣa-dīkṣita gets jñāna-ādy-āvirbhāva tathaiva — the same outward-benefit clause extends.

speaker: Teacher (reclamation)
question: Who may be reclaimed, and how unwound?
premises: Dwellers in scriptures from Vaiṣṇava to southern tantras, or their vow-takers; even highest-scripture men serving unentitled lower gurus.

Turned hither by the Lord's power-descent: fast observed, worshipped with common mantras, doings told, led before the Lord; vow taken, cast in water; bathed, sprinkled, purified with gruel and tooth-stick, led blindfolded in, Lord worshipped by common mantra.
inference: Converts from any lower order are receivable on one condition: the Lord's turning-them-hither; then unwound in order — fasted, worshipped, confessed, led in, vow cast in water, bathed, purified, blindfolded, worshipped anew.

speaker: Teacher (fire-rite)
question: How is the vow purified?
premises: In Śiva-made fire by common mantra, vow purified; name casketed in own mantra.
'I purify the expiation,' ending in svāhā: a hundred offered.
inference: Vow-mantra dialogue in transformed fire: a hundred self-purifications ending in svāhā.

speaker: Teacher (full oblation)
question: What seals it?
premises: Then too the full offering, ending in vauṣaṭ.
inference: Full oblation with vauṣaṭ closes the fire-work.

speaker: Teacher (release)
question: What happens to the old bond?
premises: Vrateśvara invoked, worshipped, told by Śiva's order to be harmless.
Satisfied, dismissed; fire dismissed: thus liṅga-lifting.
inference: The old vow-lord is retired with honors: invoked, worshipped, ordered harmless, fed, dismissed with the fire — thus liṅga-lifting.

speaker: Teacher (return)
question: What then?
premises: Consecration-dwelling and the rest, as before.
inference: Adhivāsa and the rest as before: the convert rejoins the standard sequence.

speaker: Teacher (close)
question: And finally?
premises: Initiation at will.
inference: Initiation at will: the convert stands where the born stood.

speaker: Teacher (injunction)
question: Who is to be consecrated, and why?
premises: Consecrate the well-practised knower as practitioner or guru.
The knower alone, even markless, is entitled to practitionerhood and grace-bestowing; no other, even consecrated.
inference: Entitlement follows knowledge, not marks and not prior consecration: the markless knower alone is fit for practitionerhood or guruhood.

speaker: Teacher (discipline)
question: What binds, what frees, what disciplines the consecrated?
premises: The guru who has handed over authority incurs no fault by not initiating; before that, non-initiating IS bondage.
The consecrated does the six-month vidyāvrata for mantra-deity identity; then, that-made, he is entitled to initiate.
Test the unfit out, never shun the fit; test even the initiated; overlook known deceit; worship by consecration-splendor.
inference: Delegation ends the duty to initiate; before it, omission binds. The consecrated earns initiation-rights through vidyāvrata, then examines strictly and overlooks knowingly.

speaker: Teacher (post-mortem admission)
question: Who is initiated after death?
premises: For those standing in lower doctrines, even up to gurus — immediately after death.
Solely by the power-descent arisen for raising the dead: the final-sacrament initiation.
And for higher-doctrine men who lost observance and skipped expiation — thus the Lord commands.
inference: Even the unqualified dead qualify: power-descent alone admits, immediately after death, to the final sacrament.

speaker: Teacher (corpse-rite)
question: How is the rite done on the body?
premises: Whatever raising-rite was told — all of it to the body: full-oblation corpse-burning.
For the deluded, a trust-bearing funeral to plant conviction.
Net-drawn mantras, curbing-piercing-rubbing, breath-moving through heart-throat-forehead — till the corpse-body trembles.
inference: The corpse is worked like a ritual ground: burned, convinced, net-drawn, curbed, breathed into trembling.

speaker: Teacher (joining)
question: What then?
premises: Having made the joining with supreme Śiva, burn with full oblation.
For purified and others too — or a three-day śrāddha-initiation, fourth day, monthly, yearly.
inference: Joining done, burning done, on schedule: third-day śrāddha-initiation, monthly, yearly.

speaker: Teacher (offering)
question: What is offered, to whom?
premises: Oblation-ending rite, food in one hand, virile-formed knowable-power attained to beast-identity — offered to the Lord as enjoyer.
Knowable-being ceased, he is the Lord; succeeded or not, multitude of rites for the desirer.
inference: The offering is imagined into identity and given to the Lord as enjoyer; success or not, the enjoyer gets rites upon rites.

speaker: Teacher (daily)
question: And the living?
premises: Even the liberation-seeker's: this made-of-That attainment.
Of the living, daily, like sustained practice.
inference: Even the liberation-seeker practices daily, like sustained observance, toward made-of-That-ness.

speaker: Teacher (knower)
question: What of the knower's death?
premises: But for the knower of reality, no funeral-to-śrāddha rite is of use.
His death is festival day for his knowledge-lineage — consciousness-portion filling, lineage all mere consciousness, like knowledge-attainment day while living.
inference: The knower needs no funeral-to-śrāddha machinery: his death feasts his lineage with consciousness itself.

speaker: Teacher (seal)
question: What holds, and what comes next?
premises: Everywhere here, in the śrāddha rite, image-abandonment is chief — so holds the revered Siddhāmata.
And its rule will be told in the exposition of the occasional.
inference: Image-abandonment ruled chief on Siddhāmata authority; its rule deferred to the occasional-rite exposition.

speaker: Teacher (śeṣavartana charter)
question: What follows initiation?
premises: yā dīkṣā saṃskārasiddhyai jñānayogyān prati — initiation for refinement-perfection, for the knowledge-fit.
yā ca tadaśaktān prati mokṣadīkṣā sabījā — and with-seed release-initiation for the incapable.
tasyāṃ kṛtāyām ājīvaṃ śeṣavartanaṃ guruḥ upadiśet — once performed, the guru teaches the lifelong remainder.
inference: Charter: two initiations (knowledge-fit vs incapable) → lifelong course taught by guru.

speaker: Teacher (threefold remainder)
question: How is the remainder divided?
premises: tatra nityaṃ naimittikaṃ kāmyam iti trividhaṃ śeṣavartanam — daily, occasional, desired-for.
antyaṃ ca sādhakasyaiva — the last for the practitioner alone.
tat na iha niścetavyam — not decided here.
inference: Threefold remainder; desired-for rite deferred (practitioner-only, out of scope).

speaker: Teacher (daily vs occasional)
question: What is daily, what occasional?
premises: tatra niyatabhavaṃ nityaṃ — the regularly occurring is daily.
tanmayībhāva eva naimittikaṃ — identity-with-that alone is occasional.
tadupayogi saṃdhyopāsanaṃ pratyaham anuṣṭhānaṃ parvadinaṃ pavitrakam ityādi — serving it: twilight worship, daily practice, festival day, sacred thread.
inference: Daily = recurrent; occasional = identity; servants listed.

speaker: Some (ke-cit view)
question: Is even that daily?
premises: tad api nityaṃ svakālanaiyatyāt — that too is daily, by fixedness of its own time.
iti kecit — say some.
inference: Minority view: fixed-time occasional counts as daily.

speaker: Some (occasional irregularity)
question: When is the occasional irregular?
premises: naimittikaṃ tu tacchāsanasthānām api aniyatam — occasional even for his abiders is irregular.
tadyathā gurutadvargāgamanaṃ tatparvadinaṃ jñānalābhadinam ityādikam — e.g. guru's circle coming, their festival, knowledge-day.
iti kecit.
inference: Occasion list; irregularity even for insiders.

speaker: Teacher (unfailing set)
question: What never lapses?
premises: tatra niyatapūjā saṃdhyopāsā gurupūjā parvapūjā pavitrakam iti avaśyaṃbhāvi — fixed, twilight, guru, festival worship, sacred thread: unfailing.
inference: The unfailing five.

speaker: Teacher (occasion catalogue)
question: What triggers special worship?
premises: naimittikam jñānalābhaḥ śāstralābho ... samayaniṣkṛtilābhaḥ — knowledge-gain through rule-expiation-gain.
ity etat naimittikaṃ viśeṣārcanakāraṇam — this occasional causes special worship.
inference: Twelve occasions catalogued; special worship their fruit.

speaker: Teacher (mantra transmission)
question: How is the chief mantra given?
premises: kṛtadīkṣākasya śiṣyasya pradhānaṃ mantraṃ savīryakaṃ saṃvittisphuraṇasāram alikhitaṃ vaktrāgamenaiva arpayet — unwritten, power-holding mantra transmitted by mouth-lineage alone.
tanmayībhāvasiddhyarthaṃ ... saṃdhyāsu tanmayībhāvābhyāsaṃ kuryāt — practice identity at twilights.
taddvāreṇa sarvakālaṃ ... pratyahaṃ ca parameśvaraṃ ca sthaṇḍile vā liṅge vā abhyarcayet — through that, always; daily worship the Lord on altar or liṅga.
inference: Unwritten mouth-transmission; twilight identity-practice; daily altar/liṅga worship.

speaker: Teacher (mirror rite)
question: How is identity contemplated?
premises: hṛdye sthaṇḍile vimalamakuravad dhyāte — on the heart-altar meditated as stainless mirror.
svam eva rūpaṃ yājyadevatācakrābhinnaṃ mūrtibimbitam iva dṛṣṭvā — seeing own form non-different from the deity-wheel, body-reflected.
hṛdyapuṣpagandhāsavatarpaṇanaivedyadhūpadīpopahārastutigītavādyanṛttādinā pūjayet japet stuvīta — worship with the full offering train; murmur; praise.
tanmayībhāvam aśaṅkitaṃ labdhum — to gain doubt-free identity.
inference: Mirror-contemplation of own form as deity-wheel; full offerings; doubt-free identity.

speaker: Teacher (mirror reason)
question: Why does the mirror work?
premises: ādarśe hi svamukham aviratam avalokayataḥ tatsvarūpaniścitiḥ acireṇaiva bhavet — ceaseless mirror-gazing swiftly certifies own form.
na cātra kaścit kramaḥ pradhānam ṛte tanmayībhāvāt — no order here is chief apart from identity.
inference: Swiftness without order; identity alone chief.

speaker: Our gurus (heart doctrine)
question: What is to be taken up?
premises: paramantrat...raśajālasya — entered into supreme-mantra identity, stain gone, bond-net melted.
yad adhivasati hṛdayaṃ tad eva paramam upādeyam — whatever heart dwells in that is highest to take up.
iti asmadguravaḥ — say our gurus.
inference: Guru saying: the indwelling heart is the highest take-up.

speaker: Verse (flash)
question: What flashes?
premises: adhiśayya pāramārthikaḥ bhāvaprasaraṃ prakāśam ullasati — lying upon, the ultimate-minded flashes forth the flood of being as light.
yā — which.
inference: Flash-verse; relative open.
uncertainties: yā antecedent open; flash-sense secure.

speaker: Verse (secret worship)
question: Who is worshipped?
premises: paramāmṛtadṛktvaṃ tayārcayante rahasyavidaḥ — by her, supreme-nectar-visioned, secret-knowers are worshipped.
inference: Inversion: knowers worshipped by her vision.

speaker: Stotra verse (ground rite)
question: How is the ground made?
premises: kṛtvādhāradharāṃ camatkṛtirasaprokṣākṣaṇakṣālitām — the ground-bearer sprinkled in wonder-taste's moment.
āttair mānasataḥ svabhāvakusumaiḥ svāmodasaṃdohibhiḥ — with taken mental own-being flowers exuding own fragrance.
inference: Wonder-sprinkled ground; mental flowers.
uncertainties: kṛtvādhāradharāṃ junction obscure; rite-sense from stotra frame.

speaker: Stotra verse (day-night worship)
question: What is the worship?
premises: ānandāmṛtanirbharasvahṛdayānarghārghapātrakramāt — from the priceless cup of my bliss-nectar-full heart.
tvāṃ devyā saha dehadevasadane devārcaye 'harniśam — you with the Goddess, in the body-temple, I worship day and night.
inference: Priceless-cup offering; day-night temple worship.

speaker: Teacher (seal)
question: What follows the verses?
premises: iti ślokadvayoktam artham antar bhāvayan devatacakraṃ bhāvayet — contemplating within the two-verse sense, contemplate the deity-wheel.
inference: Two-verse sense internalized as wheel-contemplation.

speaker: Teacher (closing acts)
question: What closes worship?
premises: tato mudrāpradarśanaṃ japaḥ tannivedanam — then seal-showing, murmuring, offering of that.
inference: Seal, murmur, offer.

speaker: Teacher (dismissal)
question: How dismiss?
premises: bodhyaikātmyena visarjanam — dismissal through unity with the to-be-awakened.
inference: Dismissal by unity, not sending away.

speaker: Scripture-knowers (remains)
question: What of the food-offering?
premises: mukhyaṃ naivedyaṃ svayam aśnīyāt sarvaṃ vā jale kṣipet — eat the chief offering, or cast all in water.
jalajā hi prāṇinaḥ pūrvadīkṣitāḥ carubhojanadvāreṇa — for water-born beings are previously initiated, through oblation-food.
iti āgamavidaḥ.
inference: Eat or water-cast; water-beings already initiated.

speaker: Teacher (limit)
question: What is forbidden?
premises: mārjāramūṣakaśvādibhakṣaṇe tu śaṅkā janitā nirayāya — eating cats, mice, dogs: doubt born, for hell.
jñānī api lokānugrahecchayā na tādṛk kuryāt — even the knower, to favor the world, should not.
lokaṃ vā parityajya āsīta — or leave the world and stay.
iti sthaṇḍilayāgaḥ — thus altar-rite.
inference: Impure eating barred even for knowers; withdrawal alternative; altar-rite sealed.

speaker: Teacher (liṅga rule)
question: How worship the liṅga?
premises: atha liṅge tatra na rahasyamantraiḥ liṅgaṃ pratiṣṭhāpayet — with secret mantras install no liṅga.
viśeṣāt vyaktam — especially the manifest.
pūrvapratiṣṭhiteṣu āvāhanavisarjanakrameṇa pūjāṃ kuryāt ādhāratayā — on installed ones, invocation-dismissal worship, as support.
inference: No secret-mantra installation; manifest preferred; installed ones worshipped in order.

speaker: Teacher (liṅga substitutes)
question: What can serve as liṅga?
premises: tatra guruḥ svadehaḥ ... śaktidehe rahasyaśāstrapustakaṃ vīrapātram akṣasūtraṃ prāharaṇaṃ bāṇīyaṃ mauktikaṃ sauvarṇaṃ ... makuraṃ vā liṅgam arcayet — guru's body through mirror: any may be worshipped as liṅga.
inference: Fourteen substitutes catalogued; any worshippable as liṅga.
uncertainties: bāṇīyaṃ formation obscure; missile-sense from weapon series. makuraṃ sense uncertain; reflective object in series.

speaker: Scripture-gurus (support doctrine)
question: Why does support matter?
premises: tatra ca ādhārabalād eva adhikādhikamantrasiddhiḥ bhavati — by support-power alone ever-greater mantra-success.
pūrvaṃ pūrvaṃ pradhānam ādhāraguṇānuvidhāyitvāt — earlier ever chief, following the support's qualities.
tatra tatra sādhye tattatpradhānam — in each goal, each chief.
iti śāstraguravaḥ.
inference: Support-power scales success; earlier supports chief.

speaker: Teacher (highest refinement)
question: What is highest?
premises: sarvatra parameśvarābhedābhimāna eva paramaḥ saṃskāraḥ — everywhere, pride of non-difference from the Lord alone is highest refinement.
inference: Abheda-pride as supreme saṃskāra.

speaker: Teacher (next topic)
question: What next?
premises: atha parvavidhiḥ — now the festival rule.
inference: Parvan section opened.

speaker: Teacher (six parvan)
question: How is festival sixfold?
premises: tatra sāmānyaṃ sāmānyasāmānyaṃ sāmānyaviśeṣo viśeṣasāmānyaṃ viśeṣo viśeṣaviśeṣaś ca iti ṣoḍhā parva — six.
pūraṇāt vidheḥ — from completion of rite.
inference: Six festival grades; parvan = rite-completion celebrated.

speaker: Teacher (definition)
question: Why parvan?
premises: pūraṇāt vidheḥ — from completion of the rite.
inference: Festival defined by rite-completion.

speaker: Teacher (calendar)
question: Which days?
premises: māsi māsi prathamaṃ pañcamaṃ dinaṃ sāmānyaṃ — monthly 1st, 5th: general.
caturthāṣṭamanavamacaturdaśapañcadaśāni dvayor api pakṣayoḥ sāmānyasāmānyam — 4/8/9/14/15 both fortnights: general-general.
anayor ubhayor api rāśyoḥ ... sāmānyaviśeṣaḥ — with fitting planet-star conjunctions: general-special.

gandhadhūpapuṣpādibhiḥ krameṇa pūjayet — worship in order.
pātraṃ sadāśivarūpaṃ dhyātvā ... pūrayitvā — vessel as Sadāśiva, filled with Śakti-nectar wine.

punaḥ pratisaṃcaraṇakrameṇa evaṃ pūrṇaṃ bhramaṇaṃ cakraṃ puṣṇāti — re-circulation completes the circling.

kṛtvā punar dviguṇaṃ cakrayāgaṃ kuryāt — instead do double wheel-rite.
tato 'vadaṃśān ... vikīryeta ... devatāśabdena sarvān yojayet — scatter foods; in hidden house, join all by deity-name.
iti vīrasaṃkarayāgaḥ — thus hero-mixture rite.

iti pradhānatamo 'yaṃ mūrtiyāgaḥ — thus this most excellent image-rite.

vinā saṃdhyānuṣṭhānādibhiḥ — without twilight practices.
vṛddhānāṃ bhogināṃ strīṇāṃ vidhir ayam śaktipāte sati upadeṣṭavyo guruṇā — for old, enjoyers, women, when power descends, the guru teaches it.
inference: Concession rite for old/enjoyers/women with śaktipāta; putraka-fruit within a year.

uktaṃ caitat śrītantrāloke — said in the Tantrāloka.
vinā pavitrakeṇa sarvaṃ niṣphalam — without the thread, all fruitless.
Ratnamālā, Triśiromata, Siddhāmata cited.
inference: Rule-precedent + Lord's command + Tantrāloka seal: thread indispensable.

speaker: Nitya-tantra knowers (season)

kārttikakṛṣṇapañcadaśī kulacakraṃ nityacakraṃ pūrayati — Kārttika dark fifteenth fulfills both wheels.
iti śrīnityātantravidaḥ.

speaker: Bhairavakulormi knowers (date)

inference: Rival date: winter-solstice fifteenth.

speaker: Teacher (thread making)

sauvarṇamuktāratnaviracitāt prabhṛti paṭasūtrakārpāsakuśagarbhāntam api kuryāt — from gold-jewel-made down to cloth-thread-cotton-kuśa, make.
inference: Means-graded materials, gold to kuśa-grass.

speaker: Teacher (thread sizes)
question: How many, what size?
premises: tac ca tattvasaṃkhyagranthikaṃ padakalābhuvanavarṇamantrasaṃkhyagranthi ca — tattva-number knots and adhva-number knots.
jānvantam ekaṃ nābhyantam aparaṃ kaṇṭhāntam anyat śirasi anyat — knee, navel, throat, head: four.
devāya ... gurave ca ... dadyāt — to God and guru.
śeṣebhya ekam — one to the rest.
samastādhvaparipūrṇatadrūpabhāvanena — contemplating all-paths-full forms.
inference: Four threads (body-lengths) + one for rest; knot-counts = adhva numbers.

speaker: Teacher (festival and lapse)
question: What festival, what if lapsed?
premises: tato mahotsavaḥ kāryaḥ cāturmāsyaṃ saptadinaṃ tridinaṃ ca — great festival; four-month rite, seven or three days.
mukhyānvāpatkalpāḥ — chief and fallback courses.
sati vibhave māsi māsi pavitrakam atha vā caturṣu māseṣu atha vā sakṛt — monthly, or four-monthly, or once.
tadakaraṇe prāyaścittaṃ japet — if not done, murmur expiation.
jñānī api sambhavadvitto 'pi akaraṇe pratyavaiti — even the knowing with means incurs by not doing.
lobhopahitajñānākaraṇe jñānanindāpatteḥ — from greed-covered non-doing, disgrace of knowledge.
inference: Festival courses; lapse = japa; means-withholding = knowledge-disgrace.
uncertainties: mukhyānvāpatkalpāḥ formation obscure; chief-fallback sense from context. sambhavadvitto formation obscure; means-sense from context.

īśvarecchāvaicitryodbhāvitaśaktipātasambhāvanābhāvitahṛdayo vyākcakṣīta — heart stirred by hope of power-descent, expound.

inference: Expound to fit disciples, even lower ones from compassion, on śaktipāta-hope; secrets excluded.

speaker: Teacher (exposition setup)

prathamaṃ gandhādiliptāyāṃ bhuvi ullikhya saṃkalpya vā — first on perfumed ground, drawn or resolved.

ādhārapadme vyākhyeyakalpadevatām — on base-lotus the wish-deity of exposition.

paṭalāntaṃ vyākcakṣīta nādhikam — to chapter's end, no more.
tatrāpi vastvante vastvante tarpaṇaṃ pūjanam — at each section's end sating and worship.

inference: Established need none; conduct-sharers get the course shown.

iti prāyaścittavidhiḥ vaktavyaḥ — so the expiation rule is to be stated.

yāvat śaṅkāvicyutiḥ bhavati — until doubt falls.
tadante viśeṣapūjā tatrāpi cakrayāgaḥ sa hi sarvatra śeṣabhūtaḥ — then special worship; even there wheel-rite, everywhere remaining.
inference: Woman-slaying inexpiable; Mālinī-repetition to doubt's fall; wheel-rite everywhere remaining.

speaker: Teacher (section seal)

pūrvaṃ hi sa vidhyaṅgatayā toṣito na tu prādhānyena — before pleased as rite-limb, not chiefly.
tāṃ prādhānyena akurvan adhikārabandhena baddho bhavati — not doing it chiefly, bound by office-bond.
inference: Next-day chief worship; limb-only before; omission binds office.

speaker: Teacher (guru-rite)

tasmai pūjāṃ kṛtvā tarpaṇaṃ bhojanaṃ dakṣiṇām ātmānam iti nivedya — to him worship, sating, meal, gift, self offered.
naivedyocchiṣṭaṃ prārthya vanditvā svayaṃ prāśya cakrapūjāṃ kuryāt — begging leavings, bowing, tasting, do wheel-worship.
inference: Seat, path, self-offering; leavings tasted; wheel-worship close.

speaker: Teacher (seal)
question: What was this?
premises: ita gurupūjāvidhiḥ — is guru-worship rule.
inference: Ahnika sealed.

speaker: Teacher (āgama-prāmāṇya)
question: What has just been concluded?
premises: Thus the whole, permanent, occasion-bound rite is established.
inference: The nitya-naimittika-karma exposition closes: the whole rite-class is nirūpita.

speaker: Teacher (āgama-prāmāṇya)
question: What is announced now?
premises: Now the authority of this very tradition is stated.
inference: The discourse turns from rite to prāmāṇya: āgama's authority takes the floor.

speaker: Teacher (āgama-prāmāṇya)
question: What makes something scripture?
premises: In the consciousness-made universe, vimarśa's sound-nature established, whatever contemplation of the world-thing and its act-fruit manifoldness that is — that is scripture.
Whole scripture is one-fruit-attaining by one-duty-declaration; yet people's rūḍhi stands part-by-part by the Lord's niyati-śakti.
inference: Śāstra is defined as vimarśana of the established world: structurally one-fruit, pedagogically part-graded by the Lord's necessity-power.

speaker: Teacher (āgama-prāmāṇya)
question: Where are the one-fruit attainments seated?
premises: Some in Veda-āgama scripture (Māyā-difference self), others Sāṃkhya-Vaiṣṇava, others Śaiva-Siddhānta, others Maṅgala-āgama, some rare in Trika's reflected Lord-nature, some by earlier-abandonment or transcendence.
All from one āgama alone: ekaphalasiddhi.
inference: Each school's rūḍhi sits in its own scripture, yet the single fruit issues from one āgama — school plurality does not multiply the fruit.

speaker: Teacher (āgama-prāmāṇya)
question: Does difference-doctrine cancel scripture's authority?
premises: In bheda-vāda too — all scriptures being one Lord's work — authority stands.
Partial agreement undenied, operation unstopped: mutual bādha from viśaya-bheda is akiṃcitkara.
inference: Even rival doctrines leave āgama's authority standing: contradiction by subject-difference alone is powerless.

speaker: Teacher (āgama-prāmāṇya)
question: How is āgama's prasiddhi rooted?
premises: Like brahma-killing-prohibition and ashrama-distinction: excellence follows fruit; in Upaniṣad-Bhāgavata distinct-authorship still conceivable, from meaning in what is said and beyond.
'I see gold, silver' — recognition through goldsmiths IS the āgama; child's engagement by recognition alone, inference-elimination absent in youth.
Rooted in recognition, some give impotence-dissolution-solitude fruits, some Siva-equality, some oneness-ending: whoever comes, force-of-heart recognition assumes it.
inference: Āgama's authority is prasiddhi-based (gold-silver by goldsmiths, child by seeing): recognition, not inference, roots it; and its fruits range severally to the heart's close.

speaker: Teacher (āgama-prāmāṇya)
question: What licenses the surplus verbal-connections?
premises: For the empty being's surplus vāc-yukti, any recognition taken as proof grants āgama-prāmāṇya; that āgama is relied on where utkṛṣṭa-phala is: enough by another.
inference: Surplus speech is licensed by any taken-as-proof recognition; the āgama is adopted where the excellent fruit stands — alam anyena.

speaker: Teacher (āgama-prāmāṇya)
question: How does the light behave?
premises: By consciousness-light-supreme-truth-nature, as it shines it touches also, so — discriminating.
inference: The paramārtha-light both manifests and contacts: the vivecana follows the double move.

speaker: Teacher (āgama-prāmāṇya)
question: Whose refuge is the scripture?
premises: Being, take refuge in the scripture — essence of all-made-consciousness-reflection-vimarśa, O Unsurpassable-self.
inference: The being is bidden to āśraya the śāstra whose sāra is the all-made vimarśa-nature — addressed to the anuttarātman.

speaker: Teacher (āgama-prāmāṇya)
question: What does the Prakrit verse declare?
premises: In the firm-establishment-made transaction, that very I am fearless.
inference: The Prakrit seal: in the vyavahāra of made-firm prasiddhi, the speaker is niṣaṅka.

speaker: Teacher (āgama-prāmāṇya)
question: What follows in the second Prakrit verse?
premises: Then you will be, according-as establishment-attained, Parama-Siva.
inference: Prasiddhi-attainment issues in Paramaśiva-tva: the verse promises the state conditionally.

speaker: Teacher (āgama-prāmāṇya)
question: What is asserted of the world?
premises: In own-firm-establishment-made transaction, the world is without doubt.
inference: The world's transaction, rooted in nija-ḍṛḍha-prasiddhi, stands niḥśaṅka — doubtless.

speaker: Teacher (āgama-prāmāṇya)
question: What does the āhnika close with?
premises: Then becomes, established-through-recognitions-crossed, Parama-Siva.
inference: Closing seal: paramaśivatva achieved once the recognitions are crossed — the prasiddhi-series ends in the Lord.

speaker: Teacher (kulayāga-prakāśana opening)
question: For whom is the Kaula teaching given, and on what authority?
premises: atha samastā iyam upāsā ... nirūpyate — the whole worship is set out now, not piecemeal.
śrīmatkaulikaprakriyayā ... prati — by the glorious Kaula method, for the fit ones mounted on firm resolve (samunmiṣat-tādṛśa-dṛḍha-vāsanārūḍhān).
yogasaṃcārādau uktam — the Yogasaṃcāra is cited as āgamic warrant.
ānandaṃ brahma taddehe tridhauṣṭyāntyavyavasthitam — bliss is Brahman, seated in the body at three places (lips and lowest end).
inference: Opening frame: audience (resolve-mounted fit ones), method (Kaula), warrant (Yogasaṃcāra), thesis (bliss-Brahman in the body) — the ahnika's charter.

speaker: Scripture (Yogasaṃcāra quote)
question: What happens to those who abandon bliss?
premises: abrahmacāriṇaḥ — non-abiders in Brahman (a + brahmacārin, ethical not celibate sense).
tasya tyāgād ānandavarjitāḥ — by abandoning it, cut off from bliss.
inference: First hell-bound class: the bliss-abandoners.

speaker: Scripture (quote continued)
question: Who else falls?
premises: ānandakṛtrimāhāravarjam — without bliss, with artificial food (kṛtrima = forced, unspontaneous).
cakrasya yājakāḥ — sacrificers who feed the wheel thus.
inference: Second hell-bound class: mechanical feeders of the wheel.

speaker: Teacher (seal of the quote)
question: What follows from the two cases?
premises: dvaye 'pi narake ghore — both fall into dreadful hell.
